sentences.zh: }}秦滅禮學，事多違古。

translations.literal: When Qin extinguished the study of ritual, affairs in many respects departed from antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin suppressed the study of ritual, government practice often broke with ancient precedent.

sentences.zh: 漢初崇簡，不存改作，車服之儀，多因秦舊。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Han, simplicity was honored; no thought was given to reform. The rites of carriages and dress mostly followed Qin usage.
translations.idiomatic: Early Han prized austerity and undertook no sweeping reforms, so carriage and dress protocol largely preserved Qin custom.

sentences.zh: 至明帝始乃修復先典，司馬彪輿服志詳之矣。

translations.literal: Only when Emperor Ming came to the throne did he begin to restore the former canons; Sima Biao's Treatise on Carriages and Dress records them in detail.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Emperor Ming did the court begin restoring the old canon, which Sima Biao's Treatise on Carriages and Dress describes at length.

sentences.zh: 魏代唯作指南車，其餘雖小有改易，不足相變。

translations.literal: In the Wei period only the south-pointing carriage was newly made; although other matters had minor changes, they were not enough to alter the whole.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei the court chiefly rebuilt the south-pointing carriage; other rules shifted only slightly and did not amount to a real break with tradition.

sentences.zh: 晉立服制令，辨定眾儀，徐廣車服注，略明事目，並行於今者也。

translations.literal: Jin established regulations on dress, distinguishing and fixing the many rites; Xu Guang's commentary on carriages and dress briefly clarifies the items, and these all remain in force today.
translations.idiomatic: Jin codified dress regulations, sorted out the full range of ceremony, and Xu Guang's notes on carriages and dress sketched the main categories—rules that still govern practice today.

sentences.zh: 故復敍列，以通數代典事。

translations.literal: Therefore [this chapter] sets them forth again in order, to make known the canonical matters of several ages.
translations.idiomatic: The present account therefore rehearses them in sequence so that the ceremonial usage of successive dynasties may be understood together.

sentences.zh: 上古聖人見轉蓬，始為輪，輪行可載，因為輿。

translations.literal: The sages of high antiquity, seeing a whirling thistle-down, first made a wheel; when the wheel could roll and bear a load, they thereby made a carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient sages, watching thistle-down spin in the wind, fashioned wheels; once wheels could roll and bear weight, the carriage followed.

sentences.zh: 任重致遠，流運無極。

translations.literal: Bearing heavy burdens and reaching far places, its circulation and transport know no limit.
translations.idiomatic: It could carry heavy loads over long distances, extending human reach without end.

sentences.zh: 後代聖人觀北斗魁方杓曲攜龍角，為帝車，曲其輈以便駕。

translations.literal: Later sages observed the Northern Dipper's handle square, the ladle curved, carrying the Horn of the Dragon, and made it the Imperial Carriage; they curved the shafts to make driving convenient.
translations.idiomatic: Later sages took the square handle, curved ladle, and Dragon's Horn of the Northern Dipper as the model for the Imperial Carriage and bent the shafts for easier driving.

sentences.zh: 系本云：「奚仲始作車。

translations.literal: The Genealogical Annals says: "Xi Zhong first made the carriage."
translations.idiomatic: The Genealogical Annals states, "Xi Zhong was the first to make the carriage."

sentences.zh: 」案庖羲畫八卦而為大輿，服牛乘馬，以利天下。

translations.literal: But consider: Fuxi drew the Eight Trigrams and made the great carriage, yoking oxen and riding horses to benefit all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Fuxi had already drawn the Eight Trigrams and devised the great carriage, harnessing oxen and riding horses for the good of the realm.

sentences.zh: 奚仲乃夏之車正，安得始造乎。

translations.literal: Xi Zhong was only the Director of Carriages of Xia—how could he have been the first maker?
translations.idiomatic: Xi Zhong was merely Xia's Director of Carriages; he could hardly have been the original inventor.

sentences.zh: 系本之言非也。

translations.literal: The statement in the Genealogical Annals is incorrect.
translations.idiomatic: That passage in the Genealogical Annals is wrong.

sentences.zh: 「車服以庸」，著在唐典。

translations.literal: "Carriages and dress according to merit" is recorded in the canon of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang canon already records that carriages and dress should match merit and rank.

sentences.zh: 夏建旌旗，以表貴賤。

translations.literal: Xia established banners and flags to mark noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: Xia introduced banners and flags to distinguish rank.

sentences.zh: 周有六職，百工居其一焉。

translations.literal: Zhou had the Six Offices, and the hundred crafts occupied one of them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou organized six great offices, one of which oversaw the hundred crafts.

sentences.zh: 一器而羣工致其巧，車最居多。

translations.literal: For a single implement many craftsmen contributed their skill, and carriages accounted for the greatest share.
translations.idiomatic: Many artisans lavished skill on a single type of work, and carriages required more of it than anything else.

sentences.zh: 明堂位曰：「鸞車，有虞氏之路也。

translations.literal: The Record of the Bright Hall says: "The luan carriage was the route-carriage of the Youyu clan."
translations.idiomatic: The Record of the Bright Hall says, "The luan carriage was the state carriage of the house of Yu."

sentences.zh: 大路，殷路也。

translations.literal: The great carriage was the Yin carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The great carriage was that of Yin.

sentences.zh: 乘路，周路也。

translations.literal: The riding carriage was the Zhou carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The riding carriage was that of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 」殷有山車之瑞，謂桑根車，殷人制為大路。

translations.literal: Yin had the auspicious omen of the mountain carriage, called the mulberry-root carriage; the Yin people fashioned it into the great carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Yin received the auspicious "mountain carriage," the mulberry-root carriage, which they made into the great state carriage.

sentences.zh: 禮緯曰：「山車垂句。

translations.literal: The Ritual Apocrypha says: "The mountain carriage hangs with curved timbers."
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Apocrypha says, "The mountain carriage has timbers that hang in curves."

sentences.zh: 」句，曲也。

translations.literal: "Ju" means curved.
translations.idiomatic: "Ju" means bent.

sentences.zh: 言不揉治而自曲也。

translations.literal: The text means that without steaming and shaping they curved of themselves.
translations.idiomatic: It means the wood curved naturally without being steamed and bent by craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 周之五路，則有玉、金、象、革、木。

translations.literal: Among Zhou's five routes there were jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou's five ceremonial routes were named for jade, gold, ivory, leather, and wood.

sentences.zh: 五者之飾，備於考工記。

translations.literal: The ornamentation of the five is fully set out in the Records of Craftsmen.
translations.idiomatic: Their ornamentation is fully described in the Records of Craftsmen.

sentences.zh: 輿方法地，蓋圓象天，輻以象日月，二十八弓以象列宿。

translations.literal: The carriage body is square to model earth; the canopy is round to model heaven; the spokes model sun and moon; twenty-eight bows model the constellations.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage body was square like the earth, the canopy round like heaven, the spokes like sun and moon, and the twenty-eight rim-segments like the lunar lodges.

sentences.zh: 玉、金、象者，飾車諸末，因為名也。

translations.literal: Jade, gold, and ivory ornament the carriage's extremities, and from this they take their names.
translations.idiomatic: The jade, gold, and ivory routes were named for the precious materials that ornamented the carriage's fittings.

sentences.zh: 革者漆革，木者漆木也。

translations.literal: Leather means lacquered leather; wood means lacquered wood.
translations.idiomatic: The leather route used lacquered leather, the wood route lacquered wood.

sentences.zh: 玉路，建大常以祀；

translations.literal: The jade route bore the great constant banner for sacrifice;
translations.idiomatic: The jade route carried the great constant banner for sacrifice;

sentences.zh: 金路，建大旂以賓；

translations.literal: the gold route bore the great banner to receive guests;
translations.idiomatic: the gold route the great banner to receive guests;

sentences.zh: 象路，建大赤以朝；

translations.literal: the ivory route bore the great crimson for court audience;
translations.idiomatic: the ivory route the great crimson for court audience;

sentences.zh: 革路，建大白以戎；

translations.literal: the leather route bore the great white for war;
translations.idiomatic: the leather route the great white for military affairs;

sentences.zh: 木路，建大麾以田。

translations.literal: the wood route bore the great standard for the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: the wood route the great standard for the hunt.

sentences.zh: 黑色，夏所尚也。

translations.literal: Black was what Xia honored.
translations.idiomatic: Black was the color Xia favored.

sentences.zh: 秦閱三代之車，獨取殷制。

translations.literal: Qin reviewed the carriages of the Three Dynasties and took only the Yin system.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin surveyed the carriages of the Three Dynasties, it adopted Yin practice alone.

sentences.zh: 古曰桑根車，秦曰金根車也。

translations.literal: Antiquity called it the mulberry-root carriage; Qin called it the golden-root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Antiquity knew it as the mulberry-root carriage; Qin renamed it the golden-root carriage.

sentences.zh: 漢氏因秦之舊，亦為乘輿，所謂乘殷之路者也。

translations.literal: The Han house followed Qin's usage and likewise made it the imperial carriage—the so-called riding of Yin's route.
translations.idiomatic: Han followed Qin and made it the imperial carriage, the so-called "riding of Yin's route."

sentences.zh: 禮論輿駕議曰：「周則玉輅最尊，漢之金根，亦周之玉路也。

translations.literal: The Discussion of Rites on Imperial Carriages says: "In Zhou the jade chariot was most exalted; Han's golden root is also Zhou's jade route."
translations.idiomatic: The Discussion of Rites on Imperial Carriages says, "Zhou's jade chariot ranked highest; Han's golden-root carriage corresponds to Zhou's jade route."

sentences.zh: 」漢制，乘輿金根車，輪皆朱斑，重轂兩轄，飛軨。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations the imperial golden-root carriage had wheels all vermilion-spotted, double hubs and twin linchpins, and flying naves.
translations.idiomatic: Han prescribed that the imperial golden-root carriage have vermilion-spotted wheels, double hubs with paired linchpins, and flying nave-strips.

sentences.zh: 轂外復有轂，施轄，其外復設轄，施銅貫其中。

translations.literal: Outside the hub there was again a hub, fitted with linchpins; outside that linchpins were set again, with copper run through them.
translations.idiomatic: An outer hub ringed the inner hub, each fitted with linchpins and bound together with copper pins.

sentences.zh: 東京賦曰：「重輪貳轄，疏轂飛軨。

translations.literal: The Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital says: "Double wheels, paired linchpins, open hubs and flying naves."
translations.idiomatic: The Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital reads, "Double wheels, paired linchpins, open hubs and flying nave-strips."

sentences.zh: 」飛軨以赤油為之，廣八寸，長三尺注地，繫兩軸頭，謂之飛軨也。

translations.literal: Flying naves were made of red lacquer, eight inches wide and three feet long reaching to the ground, fastened to both axle ends—this is what was called the flying nave.
translations.idiomatic: The flying nave-strips were of red lacquer, eight inches wide and three feet long to the ground, tied to both axle ends—hence the name.

sentences.zh: 以金薄繆龍，為輿倚較。

translations.literal: Gold foil was laid in coiling dragon patterns to make the carriage's leaning rails.
translations.idiomatic: Gold foil in coiling dragon patterns formed the carriage's leaning rails.

sentences.zh: 較在箱上。

translations.literal: The rails were above the box.
translations.idiomatic: The rails stood above the carriage box.

sentences.zh: 𣝛文畫蕃。

translations.literal: The sideboards were painted with patterned designs.
translations.idiomatic: The sideboards bore painted ornamental designs.

sentences.zh: 蕃，箱也。

translations.literal: "Fan" means the box.
translations.idiomatic: "Fan" means the carriage box.

sentences.zh: 文虎伏軾，龍首銜軛，鸞雀立衡，𣝛文畫轅，翠羽蓋黃裏，所謂黃屋也。

translations.literal: Patterned tigers crouched on the front rail; a dragon head held the yoke; luan birds and sparrows stood on the crossbar; the shafts were painted on the sideboards; the canopy of kingfisher feathers had a yellow lining—this is what was called the yellow house.
translations.idiomatic: Tigers in relief crouched on the front rail, a dragon head gripped the yoke, luan birds and sparrows stood on the crossbar, the shafts were painted on the sideboards, and the kingfisher-feather canopy had a yellow lining—the famed "yellow house."

sentences.zh: 金華施橑末，建大常十二旒，畫日月升龍，駕六黑馬，施十二鸞，金為叉髦，插以翟尾。

translations.literal: Golden splendor was applied to the canopy frame ends; the great constant banner with twelve tassels was raised, painted with sun, moon, and ascending dragon; six black horses drew it; twelve luan ornaments were set; gold made the forked plumes, with pheasant tails inserted.
translations.idiomatic: Gold ornament crowned the canopy arms; a great constant banner of twelve tassels painted with sun, moon, and ascending dragon was raised; six black horses drew the carriage; twelve luan finials, gold forked plumes, and pheasant tail feathers completed the equipage.

sentences.zh: 又加氂牛尾，大如斗，置左騑馬軛上，所謂左纛輿也。

translations.literal: A yak-tail banner as large as a bushel was also added, placed on the yoke of the left outrigger horse—this is what was called the left-banner carriage.
translations.idiomatic: A yak-tail standard the size of a bushel was fixed to the left outrigger horse's yoke—the so-called left-banner carriage.

sentences.zh: 路如周玉路之制。

translations.literal: The route followed the system of Zhou's jade route.
translations.idiomatic: The equipage followed the pattern of Zhou's jade route.

sentences.zh: 應劭漢官鹵簿圖，乘輿大駕，則御鳳皇車，以金根為副。

translations.literal: In Ying Shao's Diagram of the Han Offices' Guard of Honor, for the imperial great escort the phoenix carriage was driven, with the golden root as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's diagram of the Han guard of honor shows that on a full imperial progress the phoenix carriage led and the golden-root carriage served as secondary.

sentences.zh: 又五色安車、五色立車各五乘。

translations.literal: There were also five each of the five-colored seated carriages and five-colored standing carriages.
translations.idiomatic: There were also five each of the five-colored seated carriages and standing carriages.

sentences.zh: 建龍旂，駕四馬，施八鸞，餘如金根之制，猶周金路也。

translations.literal: They bore dragon banners, were drawn by four horses, bore eight luan ornaments, and otherwise followed the golden-root system—like Zhou's gold route.
translations.idiomatic: They bore dragon banners, were drawn by four horses, carried eight luan finials, and otherwise matched the golden-root pattern—equivalent to Zhou's gold route.

sentences.zh: 其車各如方色，所謂五時副車，俗謂為「五帝車」也。

translations.literal: Each carriage matched the color of its season—the so-called seasonal secondary carriages, commonly called the "Five Emperors' carriages."
translations.idiomatic: Each carriage matched its seasonal color—the five seasonal secondary carriages popularly known as the "Five Emperors' carriages."

sentences.zh: 江左則闕矣。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi they were lacking.
translations.idiomatic: South of the Yangzi the practice died out.

sentences.zh: 白馬者，朱其鬣，安車者，坐乘。

translations.literal: White horses had their manes dyed vermilion; seated carriages were for sitting while riding.
translations.idiomatic: White horses had vermilion manes; seated carriages were ridden sitting down.

sentences.zh: 又有建華蓋九重。

translations.literal: There were also nine tiers of flowery canopy.
translations.idiomatic: Some carriages bore canopies of nine tiers.

sentences.zh: 甘泉鹵簿者，道車五乘，游車九乘，在乘輿車前。

translations.literal: For the Sweet Springs guard of honor there were five path carriages and nine touring carriages, placed before the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The Sweet Springs guard of honor placed five path carriages and nine touring carriages ahead of the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 又有象車，最在前，試橋道。

translations.literal: There was also an elephant carriage, foremost of all, to test bridges and roads.
translations.idiomatic: An elephant carriage went first of all to test bridges and roadbeds.

sentences.zh: 晉江左駕猶有之。

translations.literal: Under Jin east of the Yangzi the imperial escort still had it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin courts south of the Yangzi still kept this practice.

sentences.zh: 凡婦人車皆坐乘，故周禮王后有安車而王無也。

translations.literal: All women's carriages were for seated riding; therefore in the Rites of Zhou the queen had a seated carriage but the king did not.
translations.idiomatic: Women's carriages were always ridden seated, which is why the Rites of Zhou give the queen a seated carriage but not the king.

sentences.zh: 漢制乘輿乃有之。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations the imperial carriage alone had it.
translations.idiomatic: Han alone extended the seated carriage to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 天子所御駕六，其餘副車皆駕四。

translations.literal: What the Son of Heaven himself drove was six horses; all other secondary carriages were drawn by four.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven himself drove six horses; all secondary carriages used four.

sentences.zh: 案書稱朽索御六馬。

translations.literal: The Documents speak of a rotten rope driving six horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents mention driving six horses with a rotten rope.

sentences.zh: 逸禮王度記曰：「天子駕六，諸侯駕五，卿駕四，大夫三，士二，庶人一。

translations.literal: The Lost Rites, Record of Royal Measures, says: "The Son of Heaven drives six; feudal lords five; ministers four; grand masters three; officers two; commoners one."
translations.idiomatic: The Lost Rites, Record of Royal Measures, states, "The Son of Heaven drives six horses, feudal lords five, ministers four, grand masters three, officers two, and commoners one."

sentences.zh: 」楚平王駕白馬。

translations.literal: King Ping of Chu drove white horses.
translations.idiomatic: King Ping of Chu drove white horses.

sentences.zh: 梁惠王以安車駕三送淳于髠，大夫之儀。

translations.literal: King Hui of Liang sent Chunyu Kun off in a seated carriage drawn by three—a grand master's rite.
translations.idiomatic: King Hui of Liang sent off Chunyu Kun in a seated carriage with three horses, the proper honor for a grand master.

sentences.zh: 周禮，四馬為乘。

translations.literal: In the Rites of Zhou, four horses make a team.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou define four horses as one team.

sentences.zh: 毛詩，「天子至大夫同駕四，士駕二」。

translations.literal: The Mao version of the Odes says, "From the Son of Heaven down to grand masters all drive four alike; officers drive two."
translations.idiomatic: The Mao Odes say, "From the Son of Heaven to grand masters all drive four; officers drive two."

sentences.zh: 袁盎諫漢文馳六飛。

translations.literal: Yuan Ang remonstrated with Emperor Wen of Han for galloping six flying steeds.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Ang admonished Emperor Wen for racing six flying steeds.

sentences.zh: 魏時天子亦駕六。

translations.literal: In Wei times the Son of Heaven also drove six.
translations.idiomatic: Wei emperors likewise drove six horses.

sentences.zh: 晉先蠶儀，皇后安車駕六，以兩轅安車駕五為副。

translations.literal: In Jin's early sericulture rites the empress's seated carriage was drawn by six; a two-shaft seated carriage drawn by five served as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Jin's early sericulture protocol had the empress's seated carriage drawn by six horses, with a two-shaft seated carriage of five as secondary.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，相承無六，駕四而已。

translations.literal: Since east of the Yangzi the tradition handed down has had no six—only four are driven.
translations.idiomatic: Since the move south of the Yangzi, court usage has dispensed with six-horse teams and driven four only.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武大明三年，使尚書左丞荀萬秋造五路。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daming under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the Left Assistant Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Wanqiu was ordered to make the five routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daming, Emperor Xiaowu of Song ordered Left Assistant Director Xun Wanqiu to build the five ceremonial routes.

sentences.zh: 禮圖，玉路，建赤旂，無蓋，改造依擬金根，而赤漆𣝛畫，玉飾諸末，建青旂，十有二旒，駕玄馬四，施羽葆蓋，以祀。

translations.literal: According to the Ritual Diagrams, the jade route bore a crimson banner, had no canopy, and was remade on the model of the golden root but with crimson lacquer and painted sideboards, jade ornament on the extremities, an azure banner with twelve tassels, four black horses, and a feathered canopy—used for sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The Ritual Diagrams describe the jade route with a crimson banner and no canopy, rebuilt on the golden-root pattern with crimson lacquer and painted sideboards, jade fittings, an azure twelve-tassel banner, four black horses, and a feathered canopy for sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 即以金根為金路，建大青旂，十有二旒，駕玄馬四，羽葆蓋，以賓。

translations.literal: The golden root itself became the gold route, bearing a great azure banner with twelve tassels, four black horses, and a feathered canopy—used to receive guests.
translations.idiomatic: The golden-root carriage became the gold route, with a great azure twelve-tassel banner, four black horses, and a feathered canopy for receiving guests.

sentences.zh: 象、革、木路，周官、輿服志、禮圖並不載其形段，並依擬玉路，漆𣝛畫，羽葆蓋，象飾諸末，建立赤旂，十有二旒，以視朝。

translations.literal: The ivory, leather, and wood routes are not described in form in the Offices of Zhou, the Treatise on Carriages and Dress, or the Ritual Diagrams; all were modeled on the jade route with lacquered painted sideboards, feathered canopy, ivory ornament on the extremities, and a raised crimson banner with twelve tassels—for court audience.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory route (for court audience), along with the leather and wood routes, is not described in detail in the Offices of Zhou, the Treatise on Carriages and Dress, or the Ritual Diagrams; all were modeled on the jade route with lacquered painted sideboards, feathered canopy, ivory fittings, and a crimson twelve-tassel banner.

sentences.zh: 革路，建赤旂，十有二旒，以即戎。

translations.literal: The leather route bore a crimson banner with twelve tassels—for going to war.
translations.idiomatic: The leather route bore a crimson twelve-tassel banner for military campaigns.

sentences.zh: 木路，建赤麾，以田。

translations.literal: The wood route bore a crimson standard—for the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: The wood route bore a crimson standard for the hunt.

sentences.zh: 象、革駕玄，木駕赤，四馬。

translations.literal: Ivory and leather routes were drawn by black horses; wood by red—four horses each.
translations.idiomatic: The ivory and leather routes used black horses, the wood route red horses—four in each team.

sentences.zh: 舊有大事，法駕出，五路各有所主，不俱出也。

translations.literal: Formerly on great occasions when the statutory escort went out, each of the five routes had its own function and they did not all go out together.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly on major occasions when the statutory escort departed, each of the five routes had its assigned role and they did not all appear together.

sentences.zh: 大明中，始制五路俱出。

translations.literal: In the Daming period it was first ordered that all five routes go out together.
translations.idiomatic: During Daming the court first required all five routes to go out together.

sentences.zh: 親耕籍田，乘三蓋車，一名芝車，又名耕根車，置耒耜於軾上。

translations.literal: For personally plowing the sacred field one rode the triple-canopy carriage, also called the mushroom carriage or plowing-root carriage, with plow and spade placed on the front rail.
translations.idiomatic: For the personal plowing of the sacred field the emperor rode the triple-canopy carriage, also called the mushroom carriage or plowing-root carriage, with plow and spade set on the front rail.

sentences.zh: 戎車立乘，夏曰鉤車，殷曰寅車，周曰元戎。

translations.literal: The war chariot was ridden standing; Xia called it the hook carriage, Yin the yin carriage, Zhou the primal war [chariot].
translations.idiomatic: The war chariot was ridden standing: Xia called it the hook carriage, Yin the yin carriage, Zhou the primal war chariot.

sentences.zh: 建牙麾，邪注之，載金鼓羽幢，置甲弩於軾上。

translations.literal: It bore a battle standard planted slanting, carried gold drums and feather banners, and had armor and crossbows set on the front rail.
translations.idiomatic: It carried a battle standard set at an angle, gold drums and feather banners, with armor and crossbows on the front rail.

sentences.zh: 獵車，輞幰，輪畫繆龍繞之。

translations.literal: The hunting carriage had enclosed sides and wheels painted with coiling dragons wound around them.
translations.idiomatic: The hunting carriage had enclosed sides and wheels painted with coiling dragons.

sentences.zh: 一名蹋猪車。

translations.literal: It was also called the trampling-pig carriage.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called the trampling-pig carriage.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝改曰蹋虎車。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Wei changed the name to trampling-tiger carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Wei renamed it the trampling-tiger carriage.

sentences.zh: 指南車，其始周公所作，以送荒外遠使。

translations.literal: The south-pointing carriage was first made by the Duke of Zhou to escort distant envoys from the wild borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: The south-pointing carriage was first built by the Duke of Zhou to guide envoys returning from distant lands.

sentences.zh: 地域平漫，迷於東西，造立此車，使常知南北。

translations.literal: In level and boundless country one loses east and west; this carriage was made so that one might always know south and north.
translations.idiomatic: On flat open ground travelers lose their bearings; this carriage was devised so they could always tell south from north.

sentences.zh: 鬼谷子云：「鄭人取玉，必載司南，為其不惑也。

translations.literal: Guiguzi says: "When men of Zheng went to gather jade they always carried the south-controller, so as not to lose their way."
translations.idiomatic: Guiguzi says, "When men of Zheng went to gather jade they always carried the south-pointer so they would not lose their way."

sentences.zh: 」至于秦、漢，其制無聞。

translations.literal: As for Qin and Han, nothing is heard of its form.
translations.idiomatic: By Qin and Han, however, its design was no longer known.

sentences.zh: 後漢張衡始復創造。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng of Later Han first recreated it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng of Later Han was the first to rebuild it.

sentences.zh: 漢末喪亂，其器不存。

translations.literal: At the end of Han through turmoil and disorder the instrument did not survive.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Han the device was lost in the chaos of civil war.

sentences.zh: 魏高堂隆、秦朗，皆博聞之士，爭論於朝，云無指南車，記者虛說。

translations.literal: Gao Tanglong and Qin Lang of Wei, both men of broad learning, argued at court that there was no south-pointing carriage and that the recorders spoke falsely.
translations.idiomatic: Wei scholars Gao Tanglong and Qin Lang, both widely read, argued at court that no such carriage had ever existed and that historians had invented it.

sentences.zh: 明帝青龍中，令博士馬鈞更造之而車成。

translations.literal: In the Qinglong era of Emperor Ming he ordered the academician Ma Jun to remake it, and the carriage was completed.
translations.idiomatic: In Emperor Ming's Qinglong era he ordered Academician Ma Jun to rebuild it, and the carriage was completed.

sentences.zh: 晉亂復亡。

translations.literal: Through Jin disorder it was lost again.
translations.idiomatic: It was lost again in the chaos of Jin.

sentences.zh: 石虎使解飛，姚興使令狐生又造焉。

translations.literal: Shi Hu had Xie Fei and Yao Xing had Linghu Sheng make it again.
translations.idiomatic: Shi Hu had Xie Fei rebuild it, and Yao Xing had Linghu Sheng do so again.

sentences.zh: 安帝義熙十三年，宋武帝平長安，始得此車。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Yixi under Emperor An, when Emperor Wu of Song pacified Chang'an, he first obtained this carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year of Yixi, after Emperor Wu of Song captured Chang'an, the court recovered this carriage for the first time.

sentences.zh: 其制如鼓車，設木人於車上，舉手指南。

translations.literal: Its form was like the drum carriage: a wooden figure was set on the carriage and raised a hand pointing south.
translations.idiomatic: It was built like the drum carriage, with a wooden figure mounted on top that raised its arm to point south.

sentences.zh: 車雖回轉，所指不移。

translations.literal: Though the carriage turned, what it pointed to did not shift.
translations.idiomatic: No matter how the carriage turned, the figure still pointed the same way.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿，最先啟行。

translations.literal: In the great escort guard of honor it was the first to set out.
translations.idiomatic: On a full imperial progress it led the statutory guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 此車戎狄所制，機數不精，雖曰指南，多不審正。

translations.literal: This carriage was made by the Rong and Di; its mechanism was not refined, and though called south-pointing, it often was not accurate.
translations.idiomatic: That carriage had been built by northern peoples; its gearing was crude, and despite the name "south-pointing," it was often inaccurate.

sentences.zh: 回曲步驟，猶須人功正之。

translations.literal: On winding paths and in changing pace, human labor was still needed to correct it.
translations.idiomatic: On twisting roads it still had to be adjusted by hand.

sentences.zh: 范陽人祖沖之，有巧思，常謂宜更構造。

translations.literal: Zu Chongzhi of Fanyang, a man of ingenious thought, often said it ought to be rebuilt.
translations.idiomatic: Zu Chongzhi of Fanyang was a clever craftsman who often argued it should be rebuilt.

sentences.zh: 宋順帝昇明末，齊王為相，命造之焉。

translations.literal: In the last years of Emperor Shun of Song's Shengming era, when the Prince of Qi was chief minister, he ordered it made.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Shengming years of Emperor Shun of Song, while the Prince of Qi served as chief minister, he ordered a new one built.

sentences.zh: 車成，使撫軍丹陽尹王僧虔、御史中丞劉休試之。

translations.literal: When the carriage was completed, he had Wang Sengqian, Defender-general and Governor of Danyang, and Liu Xiu, Supervising Censor, test it.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished, Wang Sengqian (Defender-general and governor of Danyang) and Liu Xiu (supervising censor) were sent to test it.

sentences.zh: 其制甚精，百屈千回，未常移變。

translations.literal: Its construction was very refined; through a hundred turns and a thousand twists it never shifted.
translations.idiomatic: The mechanism was exquisitely precise—the pointer never wavered through countless turns.

sentences.zh: 晉代又有指南舟。

translations.literal: In Jin times there was also a south-pointing boat.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also had a south-pointing boat.

sentences.zh: 索虜拓跋燾使工人郭善明造指南車，彌年不就。

translations.literal: The Northern Wei Tuoba ruler Tuoba Tao had the craftsman Guo Shanming make a south-pointing carriage, but after a full year it was still not completed.
translations.idiomatic: The Northern Wei ruler Tuoba Tao assigned the craftsman Guo Shanming to build a south-pointing carriage, but a full year passed without success.

sentences.zh: 扶風人馬岳又造，垂成，善明酖殺之。

translations.literal: Ma Yue of Fufeng made another; when it was nearly finished, Shanming poisoned him to death.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Yue of Fufeng built another, but just before it was finished Guo Shanming poisoned him.

sentences.zh: 記里車，未詳所由來，亦高祖定三秦所獲。

translations.literal: The li-recording carriage—its origin is not clear in detail; it too was captured when the High Ancestor pacified the Three Qins.
translations.idiomatic: The li-recording carriage is of obscure origin; like the south-pointer, it was taken when the High Ancestor conquered the Three Qins.

sentences.zh: 制如指南，其上有鼓，車行一里，木人輒擊一槌。

translations.literal: Its form was like the south-pointing carriage; above it was a drum, and for each li the carriage traveled a wooden figure would strike one blow.
translations.idiomatic: Built like the south-pointing carriage, it carried a drum on top; for every li traveled a wooden figure struck one beat.

sentences.zh: 大駕鹵簿，以次指南。

translations.literal: In the great escort guard of honor it followed immediately after the south-pointing carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On a full imperial progress it followed right behind the south-pointing carriage.

sentences.zh: 輦車，周禮王后五路之卑者也。

translations.literal: The palanquin carriage was the lowliest of the queen's five routes in the Rites of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin carriage was the humblest of the queen's five ritual carriages in the Rites of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 后宮中從容所乘，非王車也。

translations.literal: It was what the queen rode at leisure within the inner palace—it was not a king's carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Queens used it for leisurely travel inside the palace; it was not a royal state carriage.

sentences.zh: 漢制乘輿御之，或使人輓，或駕果下馬。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations the imperial carriage used it; sometimes men pulled it, sometimes it was drawn by pony-sized horses.
translations.idiomatic: Han emperors also used it, sometimes pulled by attendants, sometimes drawn by small horses.

sentences.zh: 漢成帝欲與班婕妤同輦是也。

translations.literal: This is what is meant when Emperor Cheng of Han wished to ride the same palanquin as Lady Ban.
translations.idiomatic: That was the carriage Emperor Cheng of Han wanted to share with Lady Ban.

sentences.zh: 後漢陰就外戚驕貴，亦輦。

translations.literal: In Later Han Yin Jiu of the empress's kin, arrogant and exalted, also used a palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: In Later Han the empress's relative Yin Jiu, swollen with rank, rode a palanquin too.

sentences.zh: 井丹譏之曰：「昔桀乘人車，豈此邪！

translations.literal: Jing Dan ridiculed him, saying: "In antiquity Jie rode a human-drawn carriage—is this not that?"
translations.idiomatic: Jing Dan mocked him: "Jie of old rode in a carriage drawn by men—is this not the same thing?"

sentences.zh: 」然則輦夏后氏末代所造也。

translations.literal: Thus the palanquin was made in the last age of the Xia dynasty.
translations.idiomatic: The palanquin, then, dates from the last rulers of Xia.

sentences.zh: 井丹譏陰就乘人，而不云僭上，豈貴臣亦得乘之乎？

translations.literal: Jing Dan ridiculed Yin Jiu for riding a human-drawn carriage but did not speak of usurping the sovereign—could eminent ministers also ride it?
translations.idiomatic: Jing Dan mocked Yin for riding a man-drawn cart yet never accused him of lèse-majesté—did that mean great ministers were permitted to use it?

sentences.zh: 未知何代去其輪。

translations.literal: It is not known in which age its wheels were removed.
translations.idiomatic: No one knows when its wheels were removed.

sentences.zh: 傅玄子曰：「夏曰余車，殷曰胡奴，周曰輜車。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan's son said: "In Xia it was called the surplus carriage, in Yin the barbarian-slave carriage, in Zhou the transport carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan wrote: "Xia called it the yu carriage, Yin the hulu carriage, Zhou the transport carriage."

sentences.zh: 」輜車，即輦也。

translations.literal: The transport carriage is the palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The transport carriage was the palanquin.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉御小出，常乘馬，亦多乘輿車。

translations.literal: In Wei and Jin for small outings emperors usually rode horses, but they also often rode the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and Jin emperors usually rode horses on short outings but often used the lighter imperial carriage as well.

sentences.zh: 輿車，今之小輿。

translations.literal: The yu carriage is today's small palanquin.
translations.idiomatic: The yu carriage corresponds to today's small palanquin.

sentences.zh: 犢車，軿車之流也。

translations.literal: The calf carriage was a branch type of the enclosed carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The calf carriage was a variety of enclosed carriage.

sentences.zh: 漢諸侯貧者乃乘之，其後轉見貴。

translations.literal: In Han only poor feudal lords rode it; later it came to be regarded as prestigious.
translations.idiomatic: In Han only impoverished lords used it; later it grew fashionable.

sentences.zh: 孫權云「車中八牛」，即犢車也。

translations.literal: When Sun Quan spoke of "eight oxen in the carriage," he meant the calf carriage.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Quan's "eight oxen in the carriage" referred to the calf carriage.

sentences.zh: 江左御出，又載儲偫之物。

translations.literal: In the southeast court on imperial outings it also carried stores and reserve supplies.
translations.idiomatic: Eastern Jin emperors also loaded it with provisions on outings.

sentences.zh: 漢代賤軺車而貴輜軿，魏、晉賤輜軿而貴軺車。

translations.literal: In Han the light carriage was despised and the enclosed transport carriage honored; in Wei and Jin the enclosed transport carriage was despised and the light carriage honored.
translations.idiomatic: Han prized enclosed transport carriages over light chariots; Wei and Jin reversed that preference.

sentences.zh: 又有追鋒車，去小平蓋，加通幔，如軺車，而駕馬。

translations.literal: There was also the pursuing-vanguard carriage: the small flat canopy was removed, a full curtain added, like a light carriage but drawn by horses.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the pursuing-vanguard carriage—like a light chariot with the small canopy removed and a full curtain added, but horse-drawn.

sentences.zh: 又以雲母飾犢車，謂之雲母車，臣下不得乘，時以賜王公。

translations.literal: Calf carriages were also ornamented with mica and called mica carriages; ministers and subordinates could not ride them—they were given to kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Calf carriages inlaid with mica were called mica carriages; officials could not use them and they were reserved as gifts for princes and dukes.

sentences.zh: 晉氏又有四望車，今制亦存。

translations.literal: Jin also had the four-view carriage, and today's regulations still preserve it.
translations.idiomatic: Jin also had the four-view carriage, which survives in present regulations.

sentences.zh: 又漢制，唯賈人不得乘馬車，其餘皆乘之矣。

translations.literal: Again, under Han regulations only merchants could not ride horse carriages; all others could.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law only merchants were barred from horse carriages; everyone else could ride them.

sentences.zh: 除吏赤蓋杠，餘則青蓋杠云。

translations.literal: Dismissed officials had crimson canopy poles; the rest had azure canopy poles.
translations.idiomatic: Retired officials used crimson canopy poles; others used azure ones.

sentences.zh: 周禮王后亦有五路，重翟、厭翟、安車、翟車、輦車，凡五也。

translations.literal: The Rites of Zhou also give the queen five routes: the double-pheasant, the suppressed-pheasant, the comfortable carriage, the pheasant carriage, and the palanquin carriage—five in all.
translations.idiomatic: The Rites of Zhou likewise prescribe five carriages for the queen: double-pheasant, suppressed-pheasant, comfortable, pheasant, and palanquin—five in all.

sentences.zh: 漢制，太皇太后、皇太后、皇后法駕乘重翟羽葢金根車，駕青交絡，青帷裳，雲𣝛畫轅，黃金塗五末，葢爪施金華，駕三馬，左右騑。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, on statutory escort the Grand Empress Dowager, Empress Dowager, and Empress rode the double-pheasant feather-canopied golden-root carriage, drawn by horses with azure crossed reins, azure curtain skirts, cloud-patterned painted sideboards on the shafts, gold on the five extremities, gold blossoms on the canopy claws, three horses with outriders left and right.
translations.idiomatic: Han rules required the grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress on statutory escort to ride the double-pheasant golden-root carriage with feather canopy, azure crossed reins and curtains, cloud-motif painted sideboards on the shafts, gilded fittings, gold blossoms on the canopy claws, three horses with outriders.

sentences.zh: 其非法駕則紫罽軿車。

translations.literal: When not on statutory escort they rode purple felt enclosed carriages.
translations.idiomatic: On informal occasions they used purple felt enclosed carriages.

sentences.zh: 按字林，軿車有衣蔽，無後轅。

translations.literal: According to the Forest of Characters, the enclosed carriage had drapery screening but no rear shaft.
translations.idiomatic: The Forest of Characters defines the enclosed carriage as screened by drapery and lacking a rear shaft.

sentences.zh: 其有後轅者謂之輜。

translations.literal: Those with a rear shaft were called transport carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages with a rear shaft were called transport carriages.

sentences.zh: 應劭漢官，明帝永平七年，光烈陰皇后葬，魂車，鸞路青羽葢，駕駟馬，龍旂九旒，前有方相。

translations.literal: In Ying Shao's Offices of Han, in the seventh year of Yongping under Emperor Ming, at the burial of the Bright Empress Empress Yin, the soul carriage—the ritual path carriage with azure feather canopy, four horses, a dragon banner of nine tassels, and an exorcist figure before it.
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Offices of Han records that in Emperor Ming's seventh Yongping year, at Empress Yin's burial, the soul carriage—the spirit path carriage with azure feather canopy, four horses, a nine-tassel dragon banner, and an exorcist mask leading the way.

sentences.zh: 鳳皇車，大將軍妻參乘，太僕妻、御女騎夾轂，此前漢舊制也。

translations.literal: The phoenix carriage—the general-in-chief's wife served as companion rider, the Grand Marshal of Ceremonies' wife and palace women rode flanking the hub: this was the old institution of Former Han.
translations.idiomatic: The phoenix carriage followed, with the general's wife as companion rider and the grand marshal's wife and palace women riding beside the hub—an old Former Han custom.

sentences.zh: 晉先蠶儀注，皇后乘油畫雲母安車，駕六騩馬。

translations.literal: Jin protocol for the First Silkworm ceremony: the empress rode an oil-painted mica comfortable carriage drawn by six piebald horses.
translations.idiomatic: Jin rites for the First Silkworm had the empress ride an oil-painted mica comfortable carriage with six piebald horses.

sentences.zh: 騩，淺黑色也。

translations.literal: "Gui" means light black.
translations.idiomatic: "Gui" denotes a pale black coat.

sentences.zh: 油畫兩轅安車，駕五騩馬為副。

translations.literal: An oil-painted two-shaft comfortable carriage with five piebald horses served as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: A secondary oil-painted two-shaft comfortable carriage used five piebald horses.

sentences.zh: 公主油畫安車，駕三。

translations.literal: Princesses rode oil-painted comfortable carriages drawn by three.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses used oil-painted comfortable carriages with three horses.

sentences.zh: 三夫人青交絡安車，駕三。

translations.literal: The Three Ladies rode azure crossed-rein comfortable carriages drawn by three.
translations.idiomatic: The three chief consorts rode azure-trimmed comfortable carriages with three horses.

sentences.zh: 皆以紫絳罽軿車，駕三為副。

translations.literal: All had purple crimson felt enclosed carriages with three horses as secondary.
translations.idiomatic: Each also had a purple felt enclosed carriage with three horses as escort.

sentences.zh: 九嬪世婦軿車，駕二。

translations.literal: The nine consorts and palace ladies-in-waiting rode enclosed carriages drawn by two.
translations.idiomatic: Nine consorts and palace ladies used enclosed carriages drawn by two horses.

sentences.zh: 宮人輜車，駕一。

translations.literal: Palace women rode transport carriages drawn by one.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary palace women rode single-horse transport carriages.

sentences.zh: 王妃、公侯特進夫人、封君皁交絡安車，駕三。

translations.literal: Princesses by marriage, wives of dukes and marquises and specially advanced officials, and ennobled ladies rode black crossed-rein comfortable carriages drawn by three.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial princesses by marriage, wives of nobles and specially advanced officials, and ennobled ladies rode black-trimmed comfortable carriages with three horses.

sentences.zh: 漢制，貴人、公主、王妃、封君油軿皆駕二，右騑而已。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, favored ladies, princesses, princesses by marriage, and ennobled ladies all used oil-painted enclosed carriages drawn by two horses with only a right outrider.
translations.idiomatic: Han rules gave favored consorts, princesses, princesses-by-marriage, and ennobled ladies oil-painted enclosed carriages with two horses and only a right outrider.

sentences.zh: 漢制，太子、皇子皆安車，朱斑輪，倚虎較，伏鹿軾，黑𣝛文畫蕃，青蓋，金華施橑末，黑𣝛文畫轅，黃金塗五末。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, the heir apparent and imperial princes all used comfortable carriages with vermilion spotted wheels, tiger-patterned side panels leaning inward, deer crouching on the front rail, black painted sideboards with patterned body panels, azure canopy, gold blossoms on the canopy tips, black painted sideboards on the shafts, gold on the five extremities.
translations.idiomatic: Han rules gave the crown prince and imperial sons comfortable carriages with vermilion-spotted wheels, tiger panels on the sideboards, deer figures on the front rail, black painted ornamental sideboards and body panels, azure canopy, gilded canopy tips, painted shafts, and gold fittings.

sentences.zh: 皇子為王，錫以此乘，故曰王青蓋車。

translations.literal: When a prince was enfeoffed as king, this equipage was granted him—hence it was called the king's azure-canopy carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince was enfeoffed as king he received this equipage, hence the "king's azure-canopy carriage."

sentences.zh: 皆左右騑駕，五旂，旂九旒，畫降龍。

translations.literal: All were drawn with outriders left and right, five banners, banners of nine tassels, painted with descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: They used outriders on both sides, five banners, and nine-tassel banners painted with descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 皇孫乘綠蓋車，亦駕三。

translations.literal: Imperial grandsons rode green-canopy carriages, also drawn by three.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial grandsons rode green-canopy carriages with three horses.

sentences.zh: 魏、晉之制，太子及諸王皆駕四。

translations.literal: Under Wei and Jin regulations, the heir apparent and all princes were drawn by four.
translations.idiomatic: Under Wei and Jin rules the crown prince and all princes used four-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 晉元帝太興三年，太子釋奠。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taixing under Emperor Yuan of Jin, the crown prince performed the libation rite.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Emperor Yuan's third Taixing year the crown prince conducted the libation ceremony at the schools.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「未有高車，可乘安車。

translations.literal: An edict said: "If there is no raised carriage, one may ride the comfortable carriage."
translations.idiomatic: An edict read, "When no raised carriage is available, use the comfortable carriage."

sentences.zh: 」高車，即立乘車也。

translations.literal: The raised carriage is the standing carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The "raised carriage" was the standing carriage.

sentences.zh: 公及列侯安車，朱斑輪、倚鹿較、伏熊軾、黑蕃者謂之軒，皁繒蓋，駕二，右騑。

translations.literal: Dukes and ranked marquises used comfortable carriages with vermilion spotted wheels, deer leaning on the side panels, bears crouching on the front rail, and black body panels—this was called the xuan carriage; black silk canopy, two horses, right outrider.
translations.idiomatic: Dukes and marquises rode comfortable "xuan" carriages with vermilion-spotted wheels, deer panels, bear figures on the front rail, and black body panels, black silk canopy, two horses, and a right outrider.

sentences.zh: 王公旂八旒，侯七旒，卿五旒，皆降龍。

translations.literal: Kings and dukes had banners of eight tassels, marquises seven, grandees five—all with descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and dukes bore eight-tassel banners, marquises seven, ministers five—all with descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 公卿中二千石二千石郊陵法駕出，皆大車立乘，駕四。

translations.literal: When grandees, ranked officials at two thousand dan and full two-thousand-dan officials went out on statutory escort to the suburban altars or imperial tombs, all used large standing carriages drawn by four.
translations.idiomatic: On statutory escort to suburban rites or imperial tombs, high ministers and two-thousand-dan officials rode large standing carriages with four horses.

sentences.zh: 後導從大車，駕二，右騑。

translations.literal: Retainers following behind used large carriages drawn by two with a right outrider.
translations.idiomatic: Following attendants used two-horse large carriages with a right outrider.

sentences.zh: 他出乘安車。

translations.literal: On other outings they rode comfortable carriages.
translations.idiomatic: On other occasions they used comfortable carriages.

sentences.zh: 其去位致仕，皆賜安車四馬。

translations.literal: Those who left office and retired were all granted comfortable carriages with four horses.
translations.idiomatic: Retiring officials were all granted a four-horse comfortable carriage.

sentences.zh: 中二千石皆皁蓋、朱蕃，銅五末，駕二，右騑。

translations.literal: Officials at the two-thousand-dan middle rank all had black canopies and vermilion body panels, bronze on the five extremities, two horses and a right outrider.
translations.idiomatic: Middle-ranked two-thousand-dan officials used black canopies, vermilion panels, bronze fittings, two horses, and a right outrider.

sentences.zh: 晉令，王公之世子攝命治國者，安車，駕三，旂七旒，其侯世子，五旒。

translations.literal: Jin regulations: when a king's or duke's heir held regency and governed the state, comfortable carriage, three horses, banner of seven tassels; for a marquis's heir, five tassels.
translations.idiomatic: Jin law gave regent heirs of kings and dukes comfortable carriages with three horses and seven-tassel banners; marquises' heirs had five tassels.

sentences.zh: 傅暢故事，三公安車，駕三。

translations.literal: In Fu Chang's precedents, the three high ministers used comfortable carriages drawn by three.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang's precedents assigned the three chief ministers comfortable carriages with three horses.

sentences.zh: 特進駕二。

translations.literal: Specially advanced officials were drawn by two.
translations.idiomatic: Specially advanced officials used two-horse teams.

sentences.zh: 卿一。

translations.literal: Ministers by one.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers used one horse.

sentences.zh: 漢制，公、列侯、中二千石、二千石夫人會廟及蠶，各乘其夫之安車，右騑，加皁交絡，帷裳皆皁。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, when wives of dukes, ranked marquises, officials at middle two thousand dan, and full two thousand dan attended temple rites and the silkworm ceremony, each rode her husband's comfortable carriage with a right outrider, adding black crossed reins; curtain skirts were all black.
translations.idiomatic: Han rules required nobles' wives attending temple or silkworm rites to ride their husbands' comfortable carriages with a right outrider, black crossed reins, and black curtains.

sentences.zh: 非公會，則乘漆布輜軿，銅五末。

translations.literal: When not at public assemblies they rode lacquered cloth transport enclosed carriages with bronze on the five extremities.
translations.idiomatic: On private occasions they used lacquered cloth transport enclosed carriages with bronze fittings.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝太康四年，詔依漢故事，給九卿朝車駕及安車各一乘。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taikang under Emperor Wu of Jin, an edict followed Han precedent and granted the nine ministers each one court carriage team and one comfortable carriage.
translations.idiomatic: In Jin Emperor Wu's fourth Taikang year an edict revived Han practice, granting each of the nine ministers a court carriage and a comfortable carriage.

sentences.zh: 傅暢故事，尚書令詔車，黑耳後戶。

translations.literal: In Fu Chang's precedents, the Director of the Masters of Writing used the edict carriage with black ears on the rear doors.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Chang records that the director of the Masters of Writing used the edict carriage with black door ears at the rear.

sentences.zh: 僕射但後戶無耳。

translations.literal: The Supervisor had only rear doors without ears.
translations.idiomatic: The supervisor had rear doors without those ears.

sentences.zh: 中書監令如僕射。

translations.literal: The supervisors and directors of the Palace Secretariat were like the Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Secretariat directors and supervisors followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 漢制，乘輿御大駕，公卿奉引，太僕御，大將軍參乘，備千乘萬騎。

translations.literal: Under Han regulations, for the imperial great escort the emperor rode it; dukes and ministers led the way, the Grand Marshal of Ceremonies drove, the General-in-Chief served as companion rider, with a thousand carriages and ten thousand riders in readiness.
translations.idiomatic: Han protocol for the full great escort had the emperor ride in state while dukes and ministers led, the grand marshal drove, the general-in-chief sat as companion, and a thousand chariots and ten thousand horsemen stood ready.

sentences.zh: 屬車八十一乘。

translations.literal: Retinue carriages numbered eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: The retinue comprised eighty-one follow carriages.

sentences.zh: 古者諸侯貳車九乘，秦滅九國，兼其車服，故八十一乘也。

translations.literal: In antiquity feudal lords had nine secondary carriages each; Qin extinguished nine states and annexed their carriage dress—hence eighty-one carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient lords each kept nine spare carriages; Qin conquered nine kingdoms and absorbed their ceremonial equipage—hence eighty-one follow cars.

sentences.zh: 漢遵弗改。

translations.literal: Han followed this without change.
translations.idiomatic: Han preserved the number unchanged.

sentences.zh: 漢都長安時，祠天於甘泉用之。

translations.literal: When Han made its capital at Chang'an, this was used when sacrificing to Heaven at Sweet Springs.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital was at Chang'an it was used for Heaven worship at Sweet Springs.

sentences.zh: 都洛陽，上原陵，又用之，大喪又用之。

translations.literal: When the capital was at Luoyang, for visits to the Yuan tombs it was used again, and for great mourning as well.
translations.idiomatic: After the move to Luoyang it served tomb visits at the Yuan imperial mausolea and state funerals.

sentences.zh: 法駕則河南尹、洛陽令奉引，奉車郎御，侍中參乘。

translations.literal: For statutory escort the Governor of Henan and Governor of Luoyang led the way, the Gentlemen of the Imperial Carriage drove, and the Palace Attendant served as companion rider.
translations.idiomatic: Statutory escort was led by the governors of Henan and Luoyang, driven by gentlemen of the imperial carriage office, with a palace attendant as companion.

sentences.zh: 屬車三十六乘。

translations.literal: Retinue carriages numbered thirty-six.
translations.idiomatic: The retinue numbered thirty-six follow carriages.

sentences.zh: 凡屬車皆皁蓋赤裏。

translations.literal: All retinue carriages had black canopies with crimson lining.
translations.idiomatic: All follow carriages had black canopies lined in crimson.

sentences.zh: 後漢祠天郊用法駕，祠宗廟用小駕。

translations.literal: Later Han sacrificed to Heaven at the suburban altar with statutory escort and to the ancestral temple with small escort.
translations.idiomatic: Later Han used statutory escort for suburban Heaven sacrifice and small escort for the ancestral temple.

sentences.zh: 小駕，減損副車也。

translations.literal: Small escort means reduced secondary carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Small escort meant a reduced complement of follow cars.

sentences.zh: 前驅有九斿雲罕，皮軒鸞旗，車皆大夫載之。

translations.literal: The vanguard had the nine-tassel cloud-bird banner, the hide-canopied carriage, and the luan banner carriage—all borne by grandees.
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard included the nine-tassel cloud banner, hide-canopied carriage, and luan banner carriage, each driven by a grandee.

sentences.zh: 鸞旗者，編羽旄列繫幢傍也。

translations.literal: The luan banner: feathers and yak-tails woven in rows and attached beside the banner staff.
translations.idiomatic: The luan banner wove feathers and yak-tails in rows along the staff.

sentences.zh: 金鉦黃鉞，黃門鼓車，乘輿之後有屬車，尚書、御史載之。

translations.literal: Golden gongs and yellow battle-axes, yellow-gate drum carriages—behind the imperial carriage were retinue carriages on which the Masters of Writing and the Censor rode.
translations.idiomatic: Golden gongs and yellow axes led the yellow-gate drum carriage; behind the emperor rode follow cars carrying the masters of writing and censor.

sentences.zh: 最後一車懸豹尾。

translations.literal: The last carriage hung a leopard tail.
translations.idiomatic: The rear-most carriage bore a leopard tail.

sentences.zh: 豹尾以前，比於省中。

translations.literal: Before the leopard tail was like being inside the palace offices.
translations.idiomatic: Everything ahead of the leopard tail corresponded to the inner palace precinct.

sentences.zh: 每出警蹕清道，建五旗。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went out on patrol, the road was cleared and five banners were raised.
translations.idiomatic: On every imperial outing the route was cleared and five banners raised.

sentences.zh: 太僕奉駕條上鹵簿，尚書郎侍御史令史皆執注以督整車騎，所謂護駕也。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal of Ceremonies presented the driving roster to the guard of honor; gentlemen of the Masters of Writing, attending censors, and clerks all held registers to supervise the array of carriages and horses—this was called escort protection.
translations.idiomatic: The grand marshal submitted the driving roster for the guard of honor; masters of writing, attending censors, and clerks carried registers to supervise the carriage-and-horse array—the "escort guard."

sentences.zh: 春秋上陵，尤省於小駕。

translations.literal: Spring and autumn tomb visits were even more reduced than small escort.
translations.idiomatic: Spring and autumn tomb visits used an escort even smaller than small escort.

sentences.zh: 直事尚書一人從，其餘令史以下皆從行，所謂先置也。

translations.literal: One Master of Writing on duty followed; all other clerks and below went along on foot—this was called advance deployment.
translations.idiomatic: One duty master of writing attended; lower clerks went on foot ahead—the "advance guard."

sentences.zh: 薛綜東京賦注以雲罕九斿為旌旗別名，亦不辨其形。

translations.literal: Xue Zong's commentary on the Eastern Capital Rhapsody takes the cloud-bird banner with nine tassels as an alternate name for banners and flags, yet does not distinguish its form.
translations.idiomatic: In his commentary on the Eastern Capital Rhapsody, Xue Zong treats the nine-tasseled yunhan as merely another name for regimental banners, without clarifying what it looked like.

sentences.zh: 案魏命晉王建天子旌旗，置旄頭雲罕。

translations.literal: Examining it: Wei ordered the Prince of Jin to be established with the Son of Heaven's banners and flags, setting up maotou and yunhan.
translations.idiomatic: Records show that when Wei invested the Prince of Jin, it granted him imperial banners and flags, including maotou and yunhan.

sentences.zh: 是知雲罕非旌旗也。

translations.literal: From this one knows that yunhan is not a banner or flag.
translations.idiomatic: This proves that yunhan was not a banner or flag at all.

sentences.zh: 徐廣車服注以為九斿，斿車九乘。

translations.literal: Xu Guang's commentary on carriages and dress takes it as the nine tassels—nine you-carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang, in his notes on carriages and dress, interpreted it as the nine tassels: nine you escort carriages.

sentences.zh: 雲罕疑是罼罕。

translations.literal: Yunhan is suspected to be bihan.
translations.idiomatic: Yunhan is probably the same as bihan.

sentences.zh: 詩敍曰：「齊侯田獵罼弋，百姓苦之。

translations.literal: The Preface to the Odes says: 'The Marquis of Qi hunted in the fields with biyi nets; the people suffered from it.'
translations.idiomatic: The Preface to the Odes records: 'The Marquis of Qi hunted with biyi nets and bird-snares; the people were worn down by it.'

sentences.zh: 」罼罕本施遊獵，遂為行飾乎？

translations.literal: ' Bihan was originally deployed for roaming hunts—did it then become a procession ornament?
translations.idiomatic: Were bihan nets, originally used on the hunt, later turned into parade regalia?

sentences.zh: 潘岳籍田賦先敍五路九旗，次言瓊鈒雲罕。

translations.literal: Pan Yue's Rhapsody on the Ploughing Ceremony first relates the five routes and nine banners, then speaks of jade-studded halberds and the cloud-bird banner.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue's Rhapsody on the Ploughing Ceremony first describes the five routes and nine banners, then mentions jade-inlaid halberds and the yunhan.

sentences.zh: 若罕為旗，則岳不應頻句於九旗之下。

translations.literal: If han were a banner, Yue ought not to have repeated lines beneath the nine banners.
translations.idiomatic: If han were a flag, Pan Yue would not have returned to it again and again right under his account of the nine banners.

sentences.zh: 又以其物匹鈒戟，宜是今罼網明矣。

translations.literal: Moreover, since its object is paired with inlaid halberds, it should clearly be the biyi net of today.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because it is grouped with jeweled halberds, it must be the hunting net known today as biyi—this much is clear.

sentences.zh: 此說為得之。

translations.literal: This explanation hits the mark.
translations.idiomatic: That reading is the correct one.

sentences.zh: 皮軒，以虎皮為軒也。

translations.literal: The hide-canopied carriage: a canopy made of tiger hide.
translations.idiomatic: The pixuan, or hide-canopied carriage, used tiger skin for its canopy.

sentences.zh: 徐又引淮南子「軍正執豹皮以制正其眾。

translations.literal: Xu again cites the Huainanzi: 'The army rectifier holds leopard hide to correct and align the host.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu also quotes the Huainanzi: 'The army rectifier carries leopard hide to keep the ranks in order.'

sentences.zh: 」禮記「前有士師，則載虎皮」。

translations.literal: ' The Record of Rites: 'When the Minister of Crime goes before, then leopard hide is borne.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites adds: 'If the Minister of Crime precedes the train, leopard hide is displayed on the carriage.'

sentences.zh: 乘輿豹尾，亦其義類乎？

translations.literal: The imperial carriage's leopard tail—is it of the same kind of meaning?
translations.idiomatic: Does the leopard tail hung on the imperial carriage belong to the same symbolic family?

sentences.zh: 五旗者，五色各一旗，以木牛承其下。

translations.literal: The five banners: one banner in each of the five colors, with a wooden ox supporting them below.
translations.idiomatic: The five banners were five flags, one for each color, each mounted on a wooden ox beneath the staff.

sentences.zh: 徐又云：「木牛，蓋取其負重而安穩也。

translations.literal: Xu again says: 'The wooden ox—probably taking its bearing of weight and stability.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu explains further: 'The wooden ox was meant to suggest load-bearing steadiness.'

sentences.zh: 」五旗纏竿，即禮記德車結旌不盡飾也，戎事乃散之。

translations.literal: ' The five banners' wrapped staffs are just the Record of Rites' virtue carriage with bound banners not fully adorned; in military affairs they are loosed.
translations.idiomatic: The wrapped staffs of the five banners correspond to the virtue carriage in the Record of Rites, whose pennants were tied but not fully decorated—only in war were they unfurled.

sentences.zh: 又武車綏旌，垂舒之也。

translations.literal: Again, the war carriage's sui banner is hung out and let trail.
translations.idiomatic: On war chariots, the sui pennant was hung loose so that it streamed behind.

sentences.zh: 史臣案：今結旌綏旌同，而德車武車之所不建。

translations.literal: The historiographer remarks: today the bound banner and the sui banner are the same, yet neither the virtue carriage nor the war carriage erects them.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler notes that the tied pennant and the trailing sui pennant are now identical, though neither the virtue carriage nor the war carriage is supposed to carry them.

sentences.zh: 又木牛之義，亦未灼然可曉。

translations.literal: Again, the meaning of the wooden ox is not yet lucid and intelligible.
translations.idiomatic: The rationale for the wooden ox, too, remains far from clear.

sentences.zh: 又案周禮辨載法物，莫不詳究，然無相風、罼網、旄頭之屬，此非古制明矣。

translations.literal: Again examining the Offices of Zhou, which distinguishes every object borne on carriages and investigates each in detail—yet there are no such items as the wind-indicator, biyi net, or maotou. That these are not ancient institutions is obvious.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou catalogues every ritual object carried on chariots in meticulous detail, yet mentions nothing like the wind-vane, biyi net, or maotou—clear proof that these are later accretions.

sentences.zh: 何承天謂戰國並爭，師旅數出，懸烏之設，務察風祲，宜是秦矣。

translations.literal: He Chengtian says that in the Warring States, states contended together and armies marched out repeatedly; the device of the suspended crow was meant to observe wind omens—probably it was Qin.
translations.idiomatic: He Chengtian argued that when the warring states clashed and campaigns followed one upon another, the hanging crow was introduced to read the winds—an innovation he attributed to Qin.

sentences.zh: 晉武嘗問侍臣：「旄頭何義？

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Jin once asked his attendants: 'What is the meaning of maotou?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Jin once asked his court, 'What does maotou signify?'

sentences.zh: 」彭推對曰：「秦國有奇怪，觸山截水，無不崩潰，唯畏旄頭，故虎士服之，則秦制也。

translations.literal: ' Peng Tui replied: 'In Qin there was a prodigy that, striking mountains and cutting off waters, made everything collapse—only maotou was feared; therefore tiger warriors wore it. Thus it is Qin custom.'
translations.idiomatic: Peng Tui answered: 'Qin had a monster that shattered mountains and dams alike, yet feared maotou alone; tiger warriors therefore wore it. The practice is Qin's.'

sentences.zh: 」張華曰：「有是言而事不經。

translations.literal: ' Zhang Hua said: 'Such words exist, but the matter is not canonical.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Hua objected: 'The story exists, but it will not bear scrutiny.'

sentences.zh: 臣謂壯士之怒，髮踊衝冠，義取於此。

translations.literal: I take it that when a stalwart rages, hair leaps and the cap is struck—its meaning is drawn from this.'
translations.idiomatic: 'I believe it evokes the warrior whose hair bristles and whose cap is knocked awry in fury.'

sentences.zh: 」摯虞決疑無所是非也。

translations.literal: ' Zhi Yu, in resolving doubts, pronounced neither side right nor wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhi Yu, adjudicating the dispute, would affirm neither explanation.

sentences.zh: 徐爰曰：「彭、張之說，各言意義，無所承據。

translations.literal: Xu Ai said: 'The explanations of Peng and Zhang each state a meaning, with nothing to support them.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai remarked: 'Peng and Zhang each offer a gloss, but neither rests on any authority.'

sentences.zh: 案天文畢昴之中謂之天街，故車駕以罼罕前引，畢方昴圓，因其象。

translations.literal: Examining astronomical texts: between Bi and Mao is called the Celestial Street; therefore the carriage train takes the bihan forward to lead, Bi being square and Mao round—following their images.
translations.idiomatic: Astronomical texts place the Celestial Street between the Bi and Mao constellations; the imperial train therefore led with bihan, square like Bi and round like Mao, imitating the stars.

sentences.zh: 星經，昴一名旄頭，故使執之者冠皮毛之冠也。」

translations.literal: In the Star Canon, Mao has another name, maotou; therefore those who bear it wear a fur-and-feather cap.'
translations.idiomatic: The Star Canon also names Mao 'maotou,' which is why those who carried it wore caps of fur and feathers.

sentences.zh: 輕車，古之戰車也。

translations.literal: The light carriage: the war chariot of antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: The light carriage was the ancient battle chariot.

sentences.zh: 輪輿洞朱，不巾不蓋，建矛戟幢麾，置弩於軾上，駕二。

translations.literal: Wheel and body hollow-painted vermilion, without curtain or canopy; spears, halberds, banners, and pennants were erected; crossbows set on the rail; drawn by two.
translations.idiomatic: Its wheels and body were lacquered vermilion, open to the sky; spears, halberds, standards, and flags rose from it, crossbows mounted on the side rail, and two horses in harness.

sentences.zh: 射聲校尉司馬吏士載，以次屬車。

translations.literal: Masters of the shouting archers, marshals, clerks, and soldiers rode them, following in order among the retinue carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Officers and men of the shouting-archer command rode them in sequence among the follow cars.

sentences.zh: 漢儀曰：「出稱警，入稱蹕。

translations.literal: Han protocol says: 'On going out one is called jing; on entering, bi.'
translations.idiomatic: Han court ritual prescribed: 'Going forth is announced as jing; entering, as bi.'

sentences.zh: 」說者云，車駕出則應稱警，入則應稱蹕也，而今俱唱之。

translations.literal: ' Expositors say that when the carriage train goes out one should respond with jing, and on entering with bi—yet today both are shouted together.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that the escort should cry jing on departure and bi on return; in practice both cries were used at once.

sentences.zh: 史臣以為警者，警戒也。

translations.literal: The historiographer takes jing to mean alertness and warning.
translations.idiomatic: The compiler explains jing as vigilance and warning.

sentences.zh: 蹕者，止行也。

translations.literal: Bi means to halt movement.
translations.idiomatic: Bi means to stop traffic.

sentences.zh: 今從乘輿而出者，並警戒以備非常也。

translations.literal: Today those who follow the imperial carriage going out are all on alert to guard against the unexpected.
translations.idiomatic: Today everyone who accompanies the emperor leaving the palace is kept on alert against mishap.

sentences.zh: 從外而入乘輿相干者，蹕而止之也。

translations.literal: Those coming in from outside who would intersect the imperial carriage are halted by bi.
translations.idiomatic: Anyone approaching from outside who would cross the emperor's path is stopped with a cry of bi.

sentences.zh: 董巴、司馬彪云：「諸侯王遮迾出入，稱警設蹕。」

translations.literal: Dong Ba and Sima Biao say: 'When feudal kings block and screen going in and out, they announce jing and set bi.'
translations.idiomatic: Dong Ba and Sima Biao note that when princes screened their comings and goings, they too proclaimed jing and enforced bi.

sentences.zh: 武剛車，有巾有蓋，在前為先驅。

translations.literal: The armored carriage: it has curtain and canopy, going before as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: The wugang carriage had both side curtains and a canopy, riding ahead as the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 又在輕車之後為殿也。

translations.literal: Again, behind the light carriage it serves as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: It also brought up the rear behind the light chariots.

sentences.zh: 駕一。

translations.literal: Drawn by one.
translations.idiomatic: A single team drew it.

sentences.zh: 史記，衞青征匈奴，以武剛車為營是也。

translations.literal: In the Records of the Historian, when Wei Qing campaigned against the Xiongnu, he used wugang carriages to form encampments—that is the thing.
translations.idiomatic: The Shiji relates that Wei Qing, campaigning against the Xiongnu, ringed his camps with wugang carriages—this is that usage.

sentences.zh: 漢制，大行載轀輬車，四輪。

translations.literal: Han regulation: on a grand mourning journey the wenliang carriage was borne—four wheels.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, the great funeral procession carried the wenliang carriage on four wheels.

sentences.zh: 其飾如金根，加施組連璧，交絡，四角金龍首銜璧，垂五采，析羽流蘇，前後雲氣畫帷裳，𣝛文畫曲蕃，長與車等。

translations.literal: Its ornament matched the golden-root carriage, with added knotted cords linking disks, interlaced tracery, golden dragon heads at the four corners holding disks in the mouth, hanging five colors, split feathers and flowing tassels; front and rear cloud-air painted curtain skirts, carved-pattern painted curved side-boxes, as long as the carriage itself.
translations.idiomatic: It was decorated like the golden-root imperial hearse, with knotted cords linking jade disks, interwoven fittings, dragon heads at each corner biting disks, five-colored pendants, split plumes and silk tassels, cloud motifs painted on the curtains fore and aft, and carved lacquer on the curved carriage box, all as long as the vehicle.

sentences.zh: 太僕御，駕六白駱馬，以黑藥灼其身為虎文，謂之布施馬。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal drove; six white camels were harnessed, their bodies branded with black medicine into tiger patterns—called 'distributed alms horses.'
translations.idiomatic: The grand marshal drove six white Bactrian camels, their hides branded with black dye in tiger stripes—the 'alms horses.'

sentences.zh: 既下，馬斥賣，車藏城北祕宮。

translations.literal: Once the burial was complete, the horses were sold off at reduced price; the carriage was stored in the secret palace north of the city.
translations.idiomatic: After the interment the camels were sold cheaply and the carriage stored in the northern secret palace.

sentences.zh: 今則馬不虎文，不斥賣；

translations.literal: Today the horses are not tiger-marked and are not sold off;
translations.idiomatic: Nowadays the camels are neither striped like tigers nor sold afterward;

sentences.zh: 車則毀也。

translations.literal: the carriage is simply destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: the carriage itself is simply broken up.

sentences.zh: 自漢霍光、晉安平、齊王、賈充、王導、謝安、宋江夏王葬以殊禮者，皆大輅黃屋，載轀輬車。

translations.literal: From Han's Huo Guang, Jin's Duke of Anping, the Prince of Qi, Jia Chong, Wang Dao, Xie An, and the Song Prince of Jiangxia, all buried with extraordinary rites—each used the great carriage and yellow canopy, bearing the wenliang carriage.
translations.idiomatic: From Huo Guang in Han through the Duke of Anping, Prince of Qi, Jia Chong, Wang Dao, and Xie An in Jin, down to the Song Prince of Jiangxia, every statesman granted extraordinary funeral honors rode the great carriage under the yellow canopy with the wenliang hearse.

sentences.zh: 晉令曰：「乘傳出使，遭喪以上，即自表聞，聽得白服乘騾車，到副使攝事。

translations.literal: The Jin code says: 'When one goes out on relay service and encounters mourning of a parent or above, he shall at once memorialize; he is permitted to wear white and ride a mule carriage, and on arrival the deputy envoy shall administer affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: Jin statute allowed: if an envoy on relay service learned of a parent's death, he was to report it at once, travel in white on a mule cart, and let his deputy conduct the mission on arrival.

sentences.zh: 」徐廣車服注：「傳聞騾車者，犢車裝而馬車轅也。

translations.literal: ' Xu Guang's commentary on carriages and dress: 'What relay protocol calls a mule carriage is a calf-carriage body with a horse-carriage yoke.'
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang explains that the 'mule carriage' of relay travel was really a light calf-cart frame fitted with horse shafts.

sentences.zh: 」又車無蓋者曰科車。

translations.literal: ' Again, a carriage without canopy is called a ke carriage.
translations.idiomatic: A carriage without a canopy was termed a ke carriage.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝時，護軍將軍羊琇乘羊車，司隸校尉劉毅奏彈之。

translations.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Jin, the Defender-General Yang Xiu rode a sheep carriage; the Director of the Secretariat Liu Yi memorialized to impeach him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wu of Jin, Defender-General Yang Xiu rode in a sheep cart, and Director Liu Yi impeached him for it.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「羊車雖無制，猶非素者所服。

translations.literal: An edict said: 'Though the sheep carriage has no regulation, it is still not what the plain and austere should wear.'
translations.idiomatic: The throne replied: 'Even if the sheep cart is nowhere forbidden, it is not fitting for men who profess simplicity.'

sentences.zh: 」江左來無禁也。

translations.literal: ' Since the eastward move of the court there has been no prohibition.
translations.idiomatic: After the court moved south, the practice went unchecked.

sentences.zh: 舊有充庭之制，臨軒大會，陳乘輿車輦旌鼓於殿庭。

translations.literal: Formerly there was the 'filling the courtyard' institution: at great assemblies before the throne, the imperial carriages, palanquins, banners, and drums were arrayed in the palace courtyard.
translations.idiomatic: An old rite called chongting required that at grand audiences the emperor's chariots, palanquins, banners, and drums be displayed throughout the palace courtyard.

sentences.zh: 張衡東京賦云：「龍路充庭，鸞旗拂霓。

translations.literal: Zhang Heng's Eastern Capital Rhapsody says: 'Dragon paths fill the court; luan banners brush the rainbow.'
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Heng wrote: 'Dragon paths crowd the courtyard; luan banners sweep the rainbow sky.'

sentences.zh: 」晉江左廢絕。

translations.literal: ' Under Jin east of the River it was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin court south of the Yangzi abandoned it.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武大明中修復。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song restored it in the Daming era.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu of Song revived the practice in the Daming period.

sentences.zh: 上古寢處皮毛，未有制度。

translations.literal: In high antiquity men slept and dwelt in fur and hide; there were no institutions.
translations.idiomatic: In deepest antiquity people slept in skins and furs, without regulated dress at all.

sentences.zh: 後代聖人見鳥獸毛羽及其文章與草木華采之色，因染絲綵以作衣裳，為玄黃之服，以法乾坤上下之儀；

translations.literal: Later sages saw the feathers and pelts of birds and beasts and their patterns, and the colors of flowers and plants; therefore they dyed silk to make garments, making black-and-yellow dress to model the rites of heaven and earth above and below;
translations.idiomatic: Later sages, observing the plumage of birds and beasts and the hues of plants, dyed silk into robes and set black above and yellow below to mirror heaven and earth.

sentences.zh: 觀鳥獸冠胡之形，制冠冕纓蕤之飾。

translations.literal: observing the forms of birds' and beasts' crests and beards, they fashioned caps, crowns, tassels, and fringe ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: From crests and muzzles they devised caps, crowns, cords, and hanging regalia.

sentences.zh: 虞氏作繢，采章彌文，夏后崇約，猶美黻冕。

translations.literal: The Yu clan made embroidery; colored patterns grew more ornate; the Xia sovereign honored simplicity, yet still prized the fu-and-mian crown.
translations.idiomatic: Yu introduced embroidery and ever richer pattern; Xia prized restraint, yet still revered the patterned coronet.

sentences.zh: 咎繇陳謨，則稱五服五章。

translations.literal: When Gao Yao presented his counsels, he spoke of the five garments and five patterns.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Yao laid out his plan, he spoke of five garments and five emblems.

sentences.zh: 皆後王所不得異也。

translations.literal: All were what later kings could not alter.
translations.idiomatic: No later king might change these foundations.

sentences.zh: 周監二代，典制詳密，故弁師掌六冕，司服掌六服，設擬等差，各有其序。

translations.literal: Zhou surveyed the two dynasties; its institutions were detailed and close, so the cap master governed the six crowns and the robe master the six garments, setting grades and distinctions, each with its order.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou, reviewing Xia and Yin, codified dress with precision: one office for the six crowns, another for the six robes, each rank in its proper sequence.

sentences.zh: 禮記冠義曰：「冠者禮之始，嘉事之重者也。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites, Meaning of the Cap, says: 'The cap is the beginning of ritual, the weightiest of auspicious affairs.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites declares: 'The cap is where ritual begins—the foremost of celebratory observances.'

sentences.zh: 」太古布冠，齊則緇之。

translations.literal: ' In utmost antiquity there was the cloth cap; in Qi it was dyed black.
translations.idiomatic: The earliest cap was plain cloth; in Qi it was dyed black.

sentences.zh: 夏曰毋追，殷曰章甫，周曰委貌，此皆三代常所囗囗周之祭冕，繅采備飾，故夫子曰「服周之冕」，以盡美稱之。

translations.literal: Xia called it wuzhui, Yin called it zhangfu, Zhou called it weimao—these were what the Three Dynasties constantly [---]; Zhou's sacrificial crown had spun colors and full ornamentation, so the Master said 'wear Zhou's crown,' calling it utmost beauty.
translations.idiomatic: Xia named it wuzhui, Yin zhangfu, Zhou weimao—the everyday crowns of the Three Dynasties. Only Zhou's sacrificial crown bore spun silk and full regalia; hence Confucius's praise, 'Wear the crown of Zhou,' as the perfection of beauty.

sentences.zh: 至秦以戰國即天子位，滅去古制，郊祭之服，皆以袀玄。
