translations.literal: When Qin, having been a Warring States king, took the Son of Heaven's throne, it abolished ancient institutions; suburban-sacrifice dress was all dark cross-collared black.
translations.idiomatic: Qin, rising from a feudal king of the Warring States, swept away the old wardrobe; suburban sacrifice was performed in plain dark robes.

sentences.zh: 至漢明帝始採周官、禮記、尚書諸儒說，還備袞冕之服。

translations.literal: Only under Emperor Ming of Han were the explanations of the Offices of Zhou, Record of Rites, Documents, and the various scholars taken up, and the gun-and-mian regalia restored.
translations.idiomatic: Not until Emperor Ming of Han drew on the Offices of Zhou, the Record of Rites, the Documents, and the ru scholars was full gun-mian dress restored.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝以公卿袞衣黼黻之文，擬於至尊，復損略之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei, because the gun robes of dukes and ministers with fu-and-fu patterns rivaled the supreme lord's, again reduced and simplified them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei trimmed ministerial gun robes when their fu-and-fu emblems too closely matched the emperor's.

sentences.zh: 晉以來無改更也。

translations.literal: From Jin onward there has been no further change.
translations.idiomatic: Since Jin times the wardrobe has remained essentially unchanged.

sentences.zh: 天子禮郊廟，則黑介幘，平冕，今所謂平天冠也。

translations.literal: When the Son of Heaven performs suburban and temple rites, he wears the black cap-kerchief and level crown—what is now called the level-heaven crown.
translations.idiomatic: For suburban and temple rites the emperor wears a black cap-kerchief under the level crown—the pingtian guan of later usage.

sentences.zh: 皁表朱綠裏，廣七寸，長尺二寸，垂珠十二旒。

translations.literal: Black outside, vermilion and green lining, seven inches wide, one foot two inches long, with twelve strings of beads hanging.
translations.idiomatic: The crown is black outside with vermilion-green lining, seven inches wide and one foot two long, with twelve bead strings.

sentences.zh: 以朱組為纓，衣皁上絳下，前三幅，後四幅，衣畫而裳繡，為日、月、星辰、山、龍、華、蟲、藻、火、粉米、黼、黻之象，凡十二章也。

translations.literal: Vermilion cords form the tassel; the robe is black above and crimson below, three panels in front and four behind; the upper garment is painted and the lower skirt embroidered with the images of sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, flowers, insects, algae, fire, powdered grain, fu, and fu—twelve emblems in all.
translations.idiomatic: Vermilion cords serve as the chin strap; the coat is black above and crimson below, three panels fore and four aft; the upper robe is painted and the skirt embroidered with sun, moon, stars, mountains, dragons, flowers, insects, waterweed, fire, grain, fu, and fu—twelve symbols in all.

sentences.zh: 素帶廣四寸，朱裏，以朱緣裨飾其側。

translations.literal: The plain belt is four inches wide, vermilion lined, with vermilion edging the border of the flap to ornament its sides.
translations.idiomatic: A plain belt four inches wide, lined in vermilion, its flaps edged in vermilion.

sentences.zh: 中衣以絳緣其領袖。

translations.literal: The inner garment has crimson edging at collar and sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: The under-robe bears crimson trim at collar and cuffs.

sentences.zh: 赤皮蔽膝。

translations.literal: Red-leather knee cover.
translations.idiomatic: A knee-piece of red leather.

sentences.zh: 蔽膝，古之韍也。

translations.literal: The knee cover is the ancient fu.
translations.idiomatic: That knee-piece is the ancient fu.

sentences.zh: 絳袴，絳襪，赤舄。

translations.literal: Crimson trousers, crimson socks, red shoes.
translations.idiomatic: Crimson trousers and socks, red court shoes.

sentences.zh: 未加元服者，空頂介幘。

translations.literal: Those who have not yet received the capping ceremony wear the open-topped cap-kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: Youths not yet capped wore the open-topped cap-kerchief.

sentences.zh: 其釋奠先聖，則皁紗裙，絳緣中衣，絳袴袜，黑舄。

translations.literal: For the libation to the sage, then black gauze skirt, crimson-edged inner garment, crimson trousers and socks, black shoes.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifices to Confucius he wore a black gauze skirt, crimson-trimmed under-robe, crimson trousers and socks, and black shoes.

sentences.zh: 其臨軒亦袞冕也。

translations.literal: For holding court before the throne he also wears gun-and-mian.
translations.idiomatic: He also wears full gun-mian when holding audience.

sentences.zh: 其朝服，通天冠，高九寸，金博山顏，黑介幘，絳紗裙，皁緣中衣。

translations.literal: For court dress, the penetrating-heaven crown, nine inches high, with golden Bo Mountain on the brow, black cap-kerchief, crimson gauze skirt, black-edged inner garment.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress paired the tongtian crown—nine inches high, with a golden Bo Mountain motif—with a black cap-kerchief, crimson gauze skirt, and black-trimmed under-robe.

sentences.zh: 其拜陵，黑介幘，菚單衣。

translations.literal: For visiting the tombs, black cap-kerchief and plain hemp single robe.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb visits called for a black cap-kerchief and a plain white hemp robe.

sentences.zh: 其雜服，有青赤黃白緗黑色介幘，五色紗裙，五梁進賢冠，遠遊冠，平上幘，武冠。

translations.literal: For miscellaneous dress there are cap-kerchiefs in blue, red, yellow, white, light-yellow, and black; five-colored gauze skirts; the five-ribbed advancement-worthy crown, far-wandering crown, level-top kerchief, and martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Miscellaneous occasions allowed kerchiefs in six colors, five-colored gauze skirts, and crowns ranging from the five-ribbed jinxian to the yuanyou, pingshang kerchief, and wuguan.

sentences.zh: 其素服，白𢂿單衣。

translations.literal: For plain dress, white zong single robe.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning or plain dress meant a white zong-cloth robe.

sentences.zh: 漢儀，立秋日獵服緗幘。

translations.literal: Han protocol: on the day of Beginning of Autumn, hunt dress with light-yellow kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: Han ritual prescribed a light-yellow kerchief for the autumn hunt on Beginning of Autumn.

sentences.zh: 晉哀帝初，博士曹弘之等儀：「立秋御讀令，不應緗幘。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ai of Jin, Academician Cao Hongzhi and others proposed: 'On Beginning of Autumn, when the emperor reads the autumn ordinance, the light-yellow kerchief should not be worn.'
translations.idiomatic: Early in Emperor Ai's reign, Academician Cao Hongzhi argued that the autumn ordinance ceremony should not use the light-yellow kerchief.

sentences.zh: 求改用素。

translations.literal: They asked to change to plain white.
translations.idiomatic: They petitioned to use plain white instead.

sentences.zh: 」詔從之。

translations.literal: ' An edict followed this.
translations.idiomatic: The throne approved.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉六年，奉朝請徐道娛表：「不應素幘。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yuanjia of Emperor Wen of Song, Attendant-at-Court Xu Daoyu memorialized: 'Plain white kerchief should not be used.'
translations.idiomatic: In Song Yuanjia 6, Attendant Xu Daoyu protested that plain white was wrong for the occasion.

sentences.zh: 」詔門下詳議，帝執宜如舊。

translations.literal: ' An edict ordered the Secretariat to deliberate in detail; the emperor held that the old practice should stand.
translations.idiomatic: The Secretariat was ordered to debate; the emperor insisted on keeping the old color.

sentences.zh: 遂不改。

translations.literal: Thus it was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: The light-yellow kerchief remained in use.

sentences.zh: 進賢冠，前高七寸，後高三寸，長八寸，梁數隨貴賤，古之緇布冠也。

translations.literal: The advancement-worthy crown: seven inches high in front, three behind, eight inches long; the number of ribs follows rank and eminence—it is the ancient black-cloth cap.
translations.idiomatic: The jinxian crown stood seven inches high in front, three behind, eight long; the number of ribs marked rank—it evolved from the ancient black cloth cap.

sentences.zh: 文儒者之所服。

translations.literal: What literary scholars wear.
translations.idiomatic: Literati and classicists wore it.

sentences.zh: 上公、卿助祭於郊廟，皆平冕，王公八旒，卿七旒，以組為纓，色如其綬。

translations.literal: When great dukes and ministers assist at suburban and temple sacrifices, all wear the level crown: kings and dukes eight tassels, ministers seven, with cord for the chin-strap, the color matching their sash.
translations.idiomatic: Great dukes and ministers assisting at suburban and temple rites all wore the level crown—eight tassels for kings and dukes, seven for ministers—with cord chin-straps dyed to match their sashes.

sentences.zh: 王公衣山龍以下，九章也，卿衣華蟲以下，七章也。

translations.literal: Kings and dukes wear the robe from mountain-dragon downward—nine emblems; ministers from floral creature downward—seven emblems.
translations.idiomatic: Kings and dukes bore nine emblems from the mountain-dragon down; ministers bore seven from the floral creature down.

sentences.zh: 行鄉射禮，則公卿委貌冠，以皁絹為之，形如覆杯，與皮弁同制。

translations.literal: For the village archery rite, dukes and ministers wear the weimao crown, made of black silk gauze, shaped like an inverted cup, same form as the deer-skin cap.
translations.idiomatic: For the village archery ceremony, dukes and ministers wore the weimao—black silk gauze shaped like an inverted cup, identical in form to the deer-skin cap.

sentences.zh: 長七寸，高四寸。

translations.literal: Seven inches long, four inches high.
translations.idiomatic: It measured seven inches long and four inches high.

sentences.zh: 衣黑而裳素。

translations.literal: Black robe and plain white skirt.
translations.idiomatic: They wore black robes with plain white skirts.

sentences.zh: 其中衣以皁緣領袖。

translations.literal: The inner garment has black edging at collar and sleeves.
translations.idiomatic: The under-robe bore black trim at collar and cuffs.

sentences.zh: 其執事之人皮弁，以鹿皮為之。

translations.literal: Those who perform the rites wear the deer-skin cap, made of deerskin.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual attendants wore the deer-skin cap, fashioned from deerskin.

sentences.zh: 武冠，昔惠文冠，本趙服也，一名大冠。

translations.literal: The martial crown was formerly the Huizwen crown, originally Zhao dress, also called the great crown.
translations.idiomatic: The wuguan—once the Huizwen crown—was originally Zhao attire, also known as the great crown.

sentences.zh: 凡侍臣則加貂蟬。

translations.literal: All attendant ministers add marten and cicada ornaments.
translations.idiomatic: Palace attendants added marten and cicada ornaments to it.

sentences.zh: 應劭漢官曰：「說者以金取堅剛，百鍊不耗；

translations.literal: Ying Shao's Offices of Han says: 'Expositors take gold for toughness and firmness, refined a hundred times without wear;
translations.idiomatic: Ying Shao's Offices of Han records the gloss: expositors likened gold to toughness—refined a hundred times without loss;

sentences.zh: 蟬居高食潔，口在腋下；

translations.literal: the cicada dwells high and feeds on purity, its mouth beneath its armpits;
translations.idiomatic: the cicada dwells aloft on purity, its mouth tucked beneath its wings;

sentences.zh: 貂內勁悍而外溫潤。

translations.literal: the marten fierce within yet warm and smooth without.
translations.idiomatic: the marten fierce within, warm and sleek without.

sentences.zh: 」此因物生義，非其實也。

translations.literal: ' This derives meaning from the things themselves—not the actual origin.
translations.idiomatic: ' Such readings derive moral meaning from the emblems—not their true history.

sentences.zh: 其實趙武靈王變胡，而秦滅趙，以其君冠賜侍臣，故秦、漢以來，侍臣有貂蟬也。

translations.literal: In fact King Wuling of Zhao adopted Hu dress; when Qin extinguished Zhao, the ruler's crown was bestowed on attendant ministers—hence since Qin and Han, attendants have worn marten and cicada.
translations.idiomatic: In truth King Wuling of Zhao adopted northern dress; when Qin conquered Zhao, the royal crown passed to palace attendants—hence the marten and cicada on courtiers since Qin and Han.

sentences.zh: 徐廣車服注稱其意曰：「北土寒涼，本以貂皮㬉額，附施於冠，因遂變成首飾乎？

translations.literal: Xu Guang's commentary on carriages and dress explains the idea: 'The northern lands are cold; originally marten fur warmed the brow, attached to the crown—thus did it become head ornament?
translations.idiomatic: Xu Guang's notes on carriages and dress suggest: 'In the cold north, marten fur first lined the brow and was fixed to the crown—did it then become mere ornament?

sentences.zh: 」侍中左貂，常侍右貂。

translations.literal: ' The palace attendant wears the marten on the left, the regular attendant on the right.
translations.idiomatic: ' The palace attendant wore the marten on the left, the regular attendant on the right.

sentences.zh: 法冠，本楚服也。

translations.literal: The law crown was originally Chu dress.
translations.idiomatic: The law crown originated as Chu court dress.

sentences.zh: 一名柱後，一名獬豸。

translations.literal: Also called pillar-behind, also called xiezhi.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called pillar-behind and xiezhi.

sentences.zh: 說者云：「獬豸獸知曲直，以角觸不正者也。

translations.literal: Expositors say: 'The xiezhi beast knows right from wrong, goring the crooked with its horn.
translations.idiomatic: Expositors claimed: 'The xiezhi beast discerns right from wrong and gores the unjust with its horn.

sentences.zh: 」秦滅楚，以其君冠賜法官。

translations.literal: ' When Qin extinguished Chu, the ruler's crown was bestowed on law officers.
translations.idiomatic: ' When Qin conquered Chu, the royal crown was given to judges.

sentences.zh: 謁者高山冠，本齊服也。

translations.literal: The usher's high-mountain crown was originally Qi dress.
translations.idiomatic: The usher's high-mountain crown came from Qi.

sentences.zh: 一名側注冠。

translations.literal: Also called the side-pouring crown.
translations.idiomatic: It was also called the side-pouring crown.

sentences.zh: 秦滅齊，以其君冠賜謁者。

translations.literal: When Qin extinguished Qi, the ruler's crown was bestowed on ushers.
translations.idiomatic: When Qin conquered Qi, the royal crown passed to ushers.

sentences.zh: 魏明帝以其形似通天、遠遊，乃毀變之。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming of Wei, because it resembled the penetrating-heaven and far-wandering crowns, had it destroyed and altered.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming of Wei, finding it too like the tongtian and yuanyou crowns, had it remade.

sentences.zh: 樊噲冠，廣九寸，制似平冕，殿門衞士服之。

translations.literal: The Fan Kuai crown, nine inches wide, made like the level crown—worn by palace-gate guards.
translations.idiomatic: The Fan Kuai crown, nine inches wide and modeled on the level crown, was worn by palace-gate guards.

sentences.zh: 漢將樊噲常持鐵盾。

translations.literal: The Han general Fan Kuai always carried an iron shield.
translations.idiomatic: The Han general Fan Kuai habitually carried an iron shield.

sentences.zh: 鴻門之會，項羽欲害漢王，乃裂裳以苞盾，戴入見羽。

translations.literal: At the Feast at Hong Gate, when Xiang Yu meant to harm the King of Han, he tore his robe to wrap the shield and wore it in to see Yu.
translations.idiomatic: At Hong Gate, when Xiang Yu plotted against the King of Han, Fan Kuai tore his robe to sheath the shield and entered wearing it.

sentences.zh: 漢承秦制，冠有十三種，魏、晉以來，不盡施用。

translations.literal: Han inherited Qin institutions: thirteen kinds of crown; since Wei and Jin, not all have remained in use.
translations.idiomatic: Han took over Qin's thirteen crown types, but since Wei and Jin not all remained in service.

sentences.zh: 今志其施用者也。

translations.literal: Here is recorded what is still worn.
translations.idiomatic: What follows records those still in use.

sentences.zh: 幘者，古賤人不冠者之服也。

translations.literal: The kerchief was ancient dress for those of low rank who did not wear caps.
translations.idiomatic: The kerchief was originally the headwear of commoners who wore no formal cap.

sentences.zh: 漢元帝額有壯髮，始引幘服之。

translations.literal: Emperor Yuan of Han had thick hair on his brow and first drew the kerchief down to wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yuan of Han, with heavy brow hair, first wore the kerchief pulled low.

sentences.zh: 王莽頂禿，又加其屋也。

translations.literal: Wang Mang was bald on top and added a crown to it.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Mang, bald on top, added a crown to the kerchief.

sentences.zh: 漢注曰：「冠進賢者宜長耳，今介幘也。

translations.literal: Han commentary says: 'Those who wear the advancement-worthy crown should have long flaps—now the bound kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: Han commentary states: 'The jinxian crown calls for long flaps—today's bound kerchief.

sentences.zh: 冠惠文者宜短耳，今平上幘也。

translations.literal: Those who wear the Huizwen crown should have short flaps—now the level-top kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: The Huizwen crown calls for short flaps—today's level-top kerchief.

sentences.zh: 知時各隨所宜，後遂因冠為別。

translations.literal: ' Knowing the times, each suited what was fit; later they were distinguished by the cap worn.
translations.idiomatic: ' Each era chose what fit; later the kerchief types diverged according to the crown worn.

sentences.zh: 」介幘服文吏，平上服武官也。

translations.literal: ' The bound kerchief suited civil officials, the level-top kerchief military officers.
translations.idiomatic: ' Civil officials wore the bound kerchief; military officers the level-top kerchief.

sentences.zh: 童子幘無屋者，示未成人也。

translations.literal: A youth's kerchief without a crown showed one was not yet adult.
translations.idiomatic: A youth's kerchief without a top showed he was not yet of age.

sentences.zh: 又有納言幘，後收，又一重，方三寸。

translations.literal: There was also the remonstrance kerchief, gathered at the back, with another layer, three inches square.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the remonstrance kerchief, gathered at the back with an extra layer three inches square.

sentences.zh: 又有赤幘，騎吏、武吏、乘輿鼓吹所服。

translations.literal: There was also the red kerchief, worn by mounted clerks, martial clerks, and imperial escort musicians.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the red kerchief for mounted clerks, martial clerks, and imperial musicians.

sentences.zh: 救日蝕，文武官皆免冠，著赤幘，對朝服，示威武也。

translations.literal: For rescue at a solar eclipse, civil and military officials all removed their caps and wore red kerchiefs, facing their court dress, to display martial might.
translations.idiomatic: During eclipse rites, civil and military officials doffed their caps for red kerchiefs over court dress, displaying martial resolve.

sentences.zh: 宋乘輿鼓吹，黑幘武冠。

translations.literal: In Song, the imperial carriage musicians wore black kerchiefs and martial crowns.
translations.idiomatic: Song imperial musicians wore black kerchiefs with the wuguan.

sentences.zh: 漢制，祀事五郊，天子與執事所服各如方色；

translations.literal: Han protocol: for sacrifices at the five suburbs, the Son of Heaven and those performing the rites dressed each in the color of the direction;
translations.idiomatic: Under Han ritual, at sacrifices to the five suburbs the emperor and officiants dressed in each quarter's color;

sentences.zh: 百官不執事者，自服常服以從。

translations.literal: officials not performing the rites wore their ordinary dress to follow.
translations.idiomatic: non-officiating officials wore ordinary dress to attend.

sentences.zh: 常服，絳衣也。

translations.literal: Ordinary dress was crimson robes.
translations.idiomatic: Ordinary dress meant crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 魏祕書監秦靜曰：「漢氏承秦，改六冕之制，俱玄冠絳衣而已。

translations.literal: Qin Jing, Director of the Secretariat of Wei, said: 'Han inherited Qin, altering the six crowns to black caps and crimson robes only.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Jing, Director of the Wei Secretariat, wrote: 'Han took Qin's six crowns and reduced them to black caps and crimson robes.

sentences.zh: 」晉名曰五時朝服；

translations.literal: ' Jin named this the five-season court dress;
translations.idiomatic: ' Jin called this the five-season court dress;

sentences.zh: 有四時朝服，又有朝服。

translations.literal: there is four-season court dress, and there is also court dress.
translations.idiomatic: alongside four-season court dress and plain court dress.

sentences.zh: 凡兵事，總謂之戎。

translations.literal: All military affairs are collectively called rong.
translations.idiomatic: All military affairs were collectively termed rong.

sentences.zh: 尚書云：「一戎衣而天下定。

translations.literal: The Documents says: 'With one military garment the realm was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: 'One military garment and the realm was settled.

sentences.zh: 」周禮：「革路以即戎。

translations.literal: " The Offices of Zhou: "The leather route for going to war."
translations.idiomatic: " The Offices of Zhou: "The leather carriage for taking the field."

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「兵事韋弁服。

translations.literal: " It also says: "For military affairs, the rawhide cap and dress."
translations.idiomatic: " It also says: "For military affairs, the rawhide cap and dress."

sentences.zh: 」以𩎟韋為弁，又以為衣裳。

translations.literal: ' Rawhide was used for the cap and also for robe and skirt.
translations.idiomatic: ' Rawhide served for both cap and garments.

sentences.zh: 春秋左傳：「戎服將事。

translations.literal: The Zuo Commentary: 'In military dress he will perform the affair.
translations.idiomatic: The Zuo Commentary: 'He will conduct the affair in military dress.

sentences.zh: 」又云：「晉郤至衣𩎟韋之跗。

translations.literal: " It also says: "Jin's Xi Zhi wore rawhide leggings."
translations.idiomatic: " It also records that "Jin's Xi Zhi wore rawhide leggings."

sentences.zh: 」注，先儒云：「𩎟，絳色。

translations.literal: " Commentary: early scholars say, "Rawhide is crimson."
translations.idiomatic: " Early commentators glossed rawhide as "crimson."

sentences.zh: 」今時伍伯衣。

translations.literal: ' Today the headmen wear it.
translations.idiomatic: ' Headmen wear it today.

sentences.zh: 說者云，五霸兵戰，猶有綬紱、冠纓、漫胡，則戎服非袴褶之制，未詳所起。

translations.literal: Expositors say that in the military campaigns of the Five Hegemons there were still sash, cord, crown tassels, and manhu fringes—thus military dress was not the jacket-and-trousers style; its origin is unclear.
translations.idiomatic: Expositors note that even under the Five Hegemons, armies still bore sashes, cords, crown tassels, and manhu fringes—so military dress was not yet jacket and trousers; its origins remain obscure.

sentences.zh: 近代車駕親戎中外戒嚴之服，無定色，冠黑帽，綴紫褾。

translations.literal: In recent times the dress when the imperial carriage went personally to war and when martial law was declared inside and outside had no fixed color; they wore a black cap with a purple pennon attached.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, when the emperor took the field or martial law was proclaimed, dress had no fixed hue: a black cap with a purple pennon attached.

sentences.zh: 褾以繒為之，長四寸，廣一寸。

translations.literal: The pennon was made of silk, four inches long and one inch wide.
translations.idiomatic: The pennon was silk, four inches long and one inch wide.

sentences.zh: 腰有絡帶，以代鞶革。

translations.literal: At the waist was a mesh belt, replacing the panther hide.
translations.idiomatic: A mesh belt at the waist replaced the panther-skin baldric.

sentences.zh: 中官紫褾，外官絳褾。

translations.literal: Inner officials had purple pennons, outer officials crimson pennons.
translations.idiomatic: Inner officials wore purple pennons; outer officials crimson.

sentences.zh: 又有纂嚴戎服，而不綴褾。

translations.literal: There was also the gathered-alert military dress, without a pennon attached.
translations.idiomatic: There was also the gathered-alert military dress, worn without a pennon.

sentences.zh: 行留文武悉同。

translations.literal: Whether moving or staying, civil and military were all alike.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military officials alike wore it whether on the march or in camp.

sentences.zh: 其畋獵巡幸，則唯從官戎服，帶鞶革；

translations.literal: For hunting and touring, only the attending officials wore military dress, bearing panther hide;
translations.idiomatic: On hunts and tours only attendants wore military dress with panther-skin baldrics;

sentences.zh: 文官不下纓，武官脫冠。

translations.literal: civil officials did not lower their tassels; military officers removed their caps.
translations.idiomatic: civil officials kept their tassels up; military officers doffed their caps.

sentences.zh: 宋文帝元嘉中，巡幸蒐狩皆如之；

translations.literal: Under Emperor Wen of Song in the Yuanjia era, tours and hunts followed the same rule;
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Wen of Song in Yuanjia, tours and hunts followed the same rule;

sentences.zh: 救宮廟水火，亦如之。

translations.literal: so did rescue from fire or flood at palace temples.
translations.idiomatic: as did responses to fire or flood at palace temples.

sentences.zh: 漢制，太后入廟祭神服，紺上皁下，親蠶，青上縹下，皆深衣。

translations.literal: Han protocol: the Empress Dowager's dress for entering temples to sacrifice—dark blue above, black below; for the silkworm rite, blue above and light blue below—all deep garments.
translations.idiomatic: Han law prescribed for the Empress Dowager at temple sacrifice dark blue above and black below; for the silkworm rite, blue above and light blue below—all as deep garments.

sentences.zh: 深衣，即單衣也。

translations.literal: Deep garment means a single-layer robe.
translations.idiomatic: The deep garment was a single-layer robe.

sentences.zh: 首飾剪氂幗。

translations.literal: Head ornaments were cut lambskin headcloths.
translations.idiomatic: Head ornaments were trimmed lambskin headcloths.

sentences.zh: 漢制，皇后謁廟服，紺上皁下。

translations.literal: Han protocol: the queen's dress for visiting temples—dark blue above, black below.
translations.idiomatic: Han law gave the queen dark blue above and black below for temple visits.

sentences.zh: 親蠶，青上縹下。

translations.literal: For the silkworm rite, blue above, light blue below.
translations.idiomatic: For the silkworm rite, blue above and light blue below.

sentences.zh: 首飾，假髻，步搖，八雀，九華，加以翡翠。

translations.literal: Head ornaments: false topknot, step-shake, eight sparrows, nine flowers, with kingfisher feather added.
translations.idiomatic: Her headgear included a false topknot, step-shake, eight sparrows, nine flowers, and kingfisher inlay.

sentences.zh: 晉先蠶儀注，皇后十二䥖，步搖，大手髻，衣純青之衣，帶綬佩。

translations.literal: Jin protocol for the silkworm rite: the queen twelve hairpins, step-shake, great hand-bun, pure blue robe, sash and pendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jin silkworm protocol gave the queen twelve hairpins, step-shake, a great hand-bun, a pure blue robe, sash, and jade pendant.

sentences.zh: 今皇后謁廟服袿䙱大衣，謂之褘衣。

translations.literal: Today the queen's temple dress is the great robe with skirt panels, called huiyi.
translations.idiomatic: Today the queen's temple dress is the great panelled robe called huiyi.

sentences.zh: 公主三夫人大手髻，七䥖，蔽髻。

translations.literal: Princesses and the three ladies of rank had the great hand-bun, seven hairpins, and covered topknot.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and the three chief consorts wore the great hand-bun, seven hairpins, and covered topknot.

sentences.zh: 九嬪及公夫人五䥖。

translations.literal: The nine consorts and ducal wives had five hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: The nine consorts and ducal wives wore five hairpins.

sentences.zh: 世婦三䥖。

translations.literal: Palace women had three hairpins.
translations.idiomatic: Palace women wore three.

sentences.zh: 公主會見，大手髻。

translations.literal: Princesses at audiences wore the great hand-bun.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses at audiences wore the great hand-bun.

sentences.zh: 其長公主得有步搖。

translations.literal: Senior princesses might wear step-shake.
translations.idiomatic: Senior princesses alone might wear step-shake.

sentences.zh: 公主封君以上皆帶綬，以采組為緄帶，各如其綬色。

translations.literal: Princesses and ennobled ladies of rank and above all wore sashes, with colored cords as border belts, each matching their sash color.
translations.idiomatic: Princesses and ennobled ladies of rank and above wore sashes with colored cord border belts matching their sash hues.

sentences.zh: 公特進列侯夫人、卿校世婦、二千石命婦年長者，紺繒幗。

translations.literal: Wives of specially advanced dukes and ranked marquises, palace women of grandees and generals, and elder titled wives of 2000-bush officials wore dark-blue silk headcloths.
translations.idiomatic: Wives of specially advanced dukes and marquises, palace women of grandees and generals, and elder titled wives of 2000-bush rank wore dark-blue silk headcloths.

sentences.zh: 佐祭則皁絹上下。

translations.literal: For assisting sacrifice, black silk above and below.
translations.idiomatic: When assisting sacrifice they wore black silk above and below.

sentences.zh: 助蠶則青絹上下。

translations.literal: For assisting the silkworm rite, blue silk above and below.
translations.idiomatic: When assisting the silkworm rite, blue silk above and below.

sentences.zh: 自皇后至二千石命婦，皆以蠶衣為朝服。

translations.literal: From the queen down to titled wives of 2000-bush officials, silkworm-rite dress served as court dress.
translations.idiomatic: From the queen down to titled wives of 2000-bush rank, silkworm dress doubled as court dress.

sentences.zh: 劉向曰：「古者天子至于士，王后至于命婦，必佩玉，尊卑各有其制。

translations.literal: Liu Xiang said: 'In antiquity from the Son of Heaven down to the shi, from the queen down to titled wives, all had to wear jade pendants—high and low each with its regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xiang wrote: 'In antiquity, from the Son of Heaven to the shi, from the queen to titled wives, all wore jade—each rank by its rule.

sentences.zh: 」禮記曰：「天子佩白玉而玄組綬，公侯山玄玉而朱組綬，卿大夫水蒼玉而緇組綬，士佩瓀玟而縕組綬。

translations.literal: " The Record of Rites says: "The Son of Heaven wore white jade on a black cord sash; dukes and marquises mountain-black jade on vermilion cord; grandees and ministers water-green jade on black cord; shi wore ruo-min jade on a tawny cord."
translations.idiomatic: " The Record of Rites specifies: "the Son of Heaven white jade on black cord; dukes and marquises mountain-black jade on vermilion cord; grandees and ministers water-green jade on black cord; shi ruo-min jade on tawny cord."

sentences.zh: 」縕，赤黃色。

translations.literal: ' Yun is red-yellow.
translations.idiomatic: ' Yun denotes red-yellow.

sentences.zh: 綬者，所貫佩相承受也。

translations.literal: The sash is what strung the pendants together in succession.
translations.idiomatic: The sash strung the pendants together in sequence.

sentences.zh: 上下施韍如蔽膝，貴賤亦各有殊。

translations.literal: Above and below the fu was applied like the knee cover—high and low also differed.
translations.idiomatic: Above and below hung the fu, like the knee-piece—each rank distinct.

sentences.zh: 五霸之後，戰兵不息，佩非兵器，韍非戰儀，於是解去佩韍，留其繫襚而已。

translations.literal: After the Five Hegemons, warfare never ceased; pendants were not weapons, fu not battle ritual—so pendants and fu were removed, leaving only the fastening cords.
translations.idiomatic: After the Five Hegemons war never ceased; pendants were not weapons, fu not battle gear—so both were cast off, leaving only the fastening cords.

sentences.zh: 秦乃以采組連結於襚，轉相結受，謂之綬。

translations.literal: Qin then linked colored cords to the cords, passing and linking in succession—called the sash.
translations.idiomatic: Qin linked colored cords to those fastenings in interlocking succession—this became the sash.

sentences.zh: 漢承用之。

translations.literal: Han inherited and used this.
translations.idiomatic: Han adopted the practice.

sentences.zh: 至明帝始復制佩，而漢末又亡絕。

translations.literal: Under Emperor Ming the jade pendant was first restored, yet by late Han it was again lost.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming restored jade pendants, but by late Han they vanished again.

sentences.zh: 魏侍中王粲識其形，乃復造焉。

translations.literal: Wei Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Can recognized its form and had it made anew.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Attendant Wang Can recovered the design and had it recreated.

sentences.zh: 今之佩，粲所制也。

translations.literal: Today's pendants are those Can devised.
translations.idiomatic: Today's pendants are his.

sentences.zh: 皇后至命婦所佩，古制不存，今與外同制，秦組綬，仍又施之。

translations.literal: What the queen down to titled wives wear—the ancient institution does not survive; now they follow outside practice, Qin-style cord sashes, with pendants still applied.
translations.idiomatic: For the queen down to titled wives the ancient rules are lost; they now follow court practice—Qin-style cord sashes with pendants restored.

sentences.zh: 漢制，自天子至于百官，無不佩刀。

translations.literal: Han protocol: from the Son of Heaven down to all officials, none went without wearing a sword.
translations.idiomatic: Under Han law, from the Son of Heaven to every official, all wore swords.

sentences.zh: 司馬彪志具有其制。

translations.literal: Sima Biao's Treatise gives the full regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Biao's Treatise records the full regulations.

sentences.zh: 漢高祖為泗水亭長，拔劍斬白蛇。

translations.literal: When Han Gaozu was chief of Sishui precinct, he drew his sword and slew the white serpent.
translations.idiomatic: As chief of Sishui precinct, Han Gaozu drew his sword and slew the white serpent.

sentences.zh: 雋不疑云：「劍者，君子武備。

translations.literal: Jun Buyi said: "The sword is the gentleman's martial equipment.
translations.idiomatic: Jun Buyi wrote: "The sword is a gentleman's martial gear.

sentences.zh: 」張衡東京賦，「紆黃組，腰干將。

translations.literal: " Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital reads, "They loop yellow cords and gird Ganjiang at the waist."
translations.idiomatic: " Zhang Heng's Rhapsody on the Eastern Capital has it: "Yellow cords looped, Ganjiang at the waist."

sentences.zh: 」然則自人君至士人，又帶劍也。

translations.literal: " Thus from the ruler down to the scholar, they also wore swords at the belt.
translations.idiomatic: " So from the ruler to the scholar, all wore swords at the belt as well.

sentences.zh: 自晉代以來，始以木劍代刃劍。

translations.literal: From the Jin dynasty onward, wooden swords began to replace bladed swords.
translations.idiomatic: From the Jin dynasty on, wooden swords replaced edged blades.

sentences.zh: 乘輿六璽，秦制也。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage's six seals were a Qin institution.
translations.idiomatic: The six seals of the imperial equipage were a Qin institution.

sentences.zh: 漢舊儀曰：「皇帝行璽，皇帝之璽，皇帝信璽，天子行璽，天子之璽，天子信璽。

translations.literal: Old Han Protocol says: "The Emperor's Traveling Seal, the Emperor's Seal, the Emperor's Trust Seal, the Son of Heaven's Traveling Seal, the Son of Heaven's Seal, the Son of Heaven's Trust Seal."
translations.idiomatic: Old Han Protocol lists them: the Emperor's Traveling Seal, the Emperor's Seal, the Emperor's Trust Seal, the Son of Heaven's Traveling Seal, the Son of Heaven's Seal, and the Son of Heaven's Trust Seal.

sentences.zh: 」此則漢遵秦也。

translations.literal: " This was Han following Qin.
translations.idiomatic: " Han simply followed Qin in this.

sentences.zh: 初高祖入關，得秦始皇藍田玉璽，螭虎紐，文曰「受天之命，皇帝壽昌」。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor first entered the Pass, he obtained Qin Shihuang's Lantian jade seal with a dragon-tiger knob, inscribed "Having received Heaven's mandate, may the emperor endure and prosper."
translations.idiomatic: When the High Ancestor first entered the Pass, he took Qin Shihuang's Lantian jade seal—dragon-tiger knob, inscription: "Having received Heaven's mandate, may the emperor endure and prosper."

sentences.zh: 高祖佩之，後代名曰傳國璽。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor wore it on his person; later ages named it the Heirloom Seal of the Realm.
translations.idiomatic: The High Ancestor wore it at his belt; later ages called it the Heirloom Seal of the Realm.

sentences.zh: 與斬白蛇劍俱為乘輿所寶。

translations.literal: Together with the sword that slew the white serpent, both were treasured by the imperial equipage.
translations.idiomatic: With the sword that slew the white serpent, both were treasures of the imperial equipage.

sentences.zh: 傳國璽，魏、晉至今不廢；

translations.literal: The Heirloom Seal, from Wei and Jin to the present, has never been abandoned;
translations.idiomatic: The Heirloom Seal, from Wei and Jin to the present day, has never been set aside;

sentences.zh: 斬白蛇劍，晉惠帝武庫火燒之，今亡。

translations.literal: the white-serpent sword was burned when Emperor Hui of Jin's arsenal caught fire—today it is lost.
translations.idiomatic: the white-serpent sword burned in the arsenal fire under Emperor Hui of Jin and is lost today.

sentences.zh: 晉懷帝沒胡，傳國璽沒於劉聰，後又屬石勒。

translations.literal: When Emperor Huai of Jin perished among the Hu, the Heirloom Seal fell to Liu Cong, and later passed to Shi Le.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Huai of Jin died among the Hu, the Heirloom Seal fell to Liu Cong and later to Shi Le.

sentences.zh: 及石勒弟石虎死，胡亂，晉穆帝代，乃還天府。

translations.literal: When Shi Le's brother Shi Hu died amid Hu turmoil, in the reign of Emperor Mu of Jin it at last returned to the royal treasury.
translations.idiomatic: After Shi Hu, Shi Le's brother, died in the Hu upheavals, it returned to the royal treasury in the reign of Emperor Mu of Jin.

sentences.zh: 虞喜志林曰：「傳國璽，自在六璽之外，天子凡七璽也。

translations.literal: Yu Xi's Forest of Records says: "The Heirloom Seal stood outside the six seals—the Son of Heaven had seven seals in all."
translations.idiomatic: Yu Xi's Forest of Records notes: "The Heirloom Seal lay outside the six—the Son of Heaven had seven seals in all."

sentences.zh: 」漢注曰：「璽，印也。

translations.literal: " Han commentary says: "Xi means seal."
translations.idiomatic: " Han commentary glosses: "Xi means seal."

sentences.zh: 自秦以前，臣下皆以金玉為印，龍虎紐，唯所好。

translations.literal: Before Qin, subjects all used gold and jade for seals, with dragon and tiger knobs as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: Before Qin, subjects used gold or jade seals with dragon or tiger knobs as they chose.

sentences.zh: 秦以來，以璽為稱，又獨以玉，臣下莫得用。

translations.literal: Since Qin, the term xi was used exclusively, and only jade—subjects might not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Since Qin the term xi was reserved, jade alone was used, and subjects might not employ it.

sentences.zh: 」漢制，皇帝黃赤綬，四采，黃、赤、縹、紺。

translations.literal: " Han protocol gave the emperor a yellow-vermilion sash of four colors: yellow, vermilion, light blue, and dark blue.
translations.idiomatic: " Under Han law the emperor wore a yellow-vermilion sash in four colors: yellow, vermilion, light blue, and dark blue.

sentences.zh: 皇后金璽，綬亦如之。

translations.literal: The empress had a gold seal; her sash was the same.
translations.idiomatic: The empress bore a gold seal and the same sash.

translations.idiomatic: On the imperial staircase or in the guard of honor they wore crossbill plumes and scarlet gauze single robes.

sentences.zh: 鶡鳥似雞，出上黨。

translations.literal: The crossbill resembles a chicken and comes from Shangdang.
translations.idiomatic: The crossbill resembles a fowl and is native to Shangdang.

sentences.zh: 為鳥強猛，鬭不死不止。

translations.literal: As a bird it is fierce and bold; in combat it does not stop until death.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce bird, it fights to the death without yielding.

sentences.zh: 復著鶡尾。

translations.literal: Again they wore crossbill plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Hence they again wore the crossbill plume.

sentences.zh: 北軍中候、殿中監，銅印，墨綬。

translations.literal: Central Inspector of the Northern Army and Palace Supervisor: bronze seal, black sash.
translations.idiomatic: The Central Inspector of the Northern Army and Palace Supervisor: bronze seal, black sash.

sentences.zh: 給四時朝服，武冠。

translations.idiomatic: They received four-season court dress and the martial crown.

translations.literal: Protector General of the Xiongnu, Central Cadets protecting the Qiang, Yi, Rong, barbarians, Yue, Wuhuan, and Western Regions, and Colonel of the Geng and Ji: bronze seal, blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: The Protector General of the Xiongnu, protector cadets for the Qiang, Yi, Rong, southern tribes, Wuhuan, and Western Regions, and the Colonel of Geng and Ji: bronze seal, blue sash.

translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the martial crown.

translations.idiomatic: Grand Administrators, Chancellors, and Chief Administrators of commanderies and states: silver badge, blue sash.

translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the two-ribbed worthy crown.

translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangzuo court they wore only single robes and kerchiefs.

translations.idiomatic: Those advanced to the middle two-thousand-bushel rank followed the dress of ministers and metropolitan chiefs.

sentences.zh: 牙門將，銀章，青綬。

translations.literal: Gate-guard generals: silver badge, blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: Gate-guard generals: silver badge, blue sash.

translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the martial crown.

translations.literal: Cavalry commanders-in-chief and defenders: silver seal, blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry commanders-in-chief and defenders: silver seal, blue sash.

translations.literal: Court dress, the martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the martial crown.

translations.literal: Left and Right Assistants of the Masters of Writing and Secretariat Aides: bronze seal, yellow sash.
translations.idiomatic: Left and Right Assistants of the Masters of Writing and Secretariat Aides: bronze seal, yellow sash.

sentences.zh: 朝服，進賢一梁冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the one-ribbed worthy crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the one-ribbed worthy crown.

sentences.zh: 尚書祕書郎、太子中舍人、洗馬、舍人，朝服，進賢一梁冠。

translations.literal: Gentlemen of the Masters of Writing and Secretariat, Household Gentlemen of the Center for the Heir Apparent, Grooms of the Heir Apparent, and Household Gentlemen: court dress, the one-ribbed worthy crown.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen of the Masters of Writing and Secretariat, Household Gentlemen of the Center, Grooms of the Heir Apparent, and Household Gentlemen wore court dress and the one-ribbed worthy crown.

sentences.zh: 黃沙治書侍御史，銀印，墨綬。

translations.literal: Attending Imperial Secretary for Punishments of the Yellow Sands: silver seal, black sash.
translations.idiomatic: The Attending Imperial Secretary for Punishments of the Yellow Sands: silver seal, black sash.

sentences.zh: 朝服，法冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the law crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the law crown.

sentences.zh: 侍御史，朝服，法冠。

translations.literal: Attending censors: court dress, the law crown.
translations.idiomatic: Attending censors wore court dress and the law crown.

sentences.zh: 關內、關中名號侯，金印，紫綬。

translations.literal: Named marquises within the passes and in Guanzhong: gold seal, purple sash.
translations.idiomatic: Named marquises within the passes and in Guanzhong: gold seal, purple sash.

sentences.zh: 朝服，進賢兩梁冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the two-ribbed worthy crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the two-ribbed worthy crown.

sentences.zh: 諸博士，給皁朝服，進賢兩梁冠。

translations.literal: All erudites: granted black court dress, the two-ribbed worthy crown.
translations.idiomatic: All erudites received black court dress and the two-ribbed worthy crown.

sentences.zh: 佩水蒼玉。

translations.literal: Wore water-green jade.
translations.idiomatic: They wore water-green jade.

sentences.zh: 公府長史、諸卿尹丞、諸縣署令秩千石者，銅印，墨綬。

translations.literal: Chief administrators of princely establishments, aides of ministers and metropolitan chiefs, and magistrates of county offices at the thousand-bushel rank: bronze seal, black sash.
translations.idiomatic: Chief administrators of princely establishments, aides of ministers and metropolitan chiefs, and county magistrates at the thousand-bushel rank: bronze seal, black sash.

sentences.zh: 朝服，進賢兩梁冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the two-ribbed worthy crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the two-ribbed worthy crown.

sentences.zh: 江左公府長史無朝服，縣令止單衣幘。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi, princely chief administrators had no court dress; county magistrates wore only single robes and kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jiangzuo court, princely chief administrators had no court dress; county magistrates wore only single robes and kerchiefs.

sentences.zh: 宋後廢帝元徽四年，司徒右長史王儉議公府長史應服朝服。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Yuanhui under the deposed Emperor of Later Song, Wang Jian, Right Chief Administrator of the Excellency of Works, debated that princely chief administrators ought to wear court dress.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Yuanhui under the deposed Emperor of Song, Wang Jian, Right Chief Administrator of the Excellency of Works, argued that princely chief administrators should wear court dress.

sentences.zh: 曰：「春秋國語云：『貌者情之華，服者心之文。

translations.literal: He said: "The Spring and Autumn Annals and Discourses of the States say: 'Countenance is the flower of feeling; dress is the writing of the heart.
translations.idiomatic: He said: "The Discourses of the States says: 'Countenance is the bloom of emotion; dress is the script of the heart.

sentences.zh: 』巖廊盛禮，衣冠為大。

translations.literal: ' In the grand rites of the palace hall, cap and gown rank first.
translations.idiomatic: ' In the solemn rites of the palace hall, cap and gown come first.

sentences.zh: 是故軍國異容，內外殊序。

translations.literal: Therefore army and state differ in appearance; inner and outer differ in order.
translations.idiomatic: Hence army and court differ in dress, and inner and outer offices in rank.

sentences.zh: 而自頃承用，每有乖違。

translations.literal: Yet in recent application there have often been violations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet recent practice has often strayed from the rule.

sentences.zh: 府職掌人，教四方是則。

translations.literal: Princely establishments govern people; they teach the four quarters what is normative.
translations.idiomatic: Princely establishments govern men and set the pattern for the realm.

sentences.zh: 臣居毗佐，志在當官，永言先典，載懷夕惕。

translations.literal: I serve as assistant at his side; my will is to fulfill office; I ever invoke the ancient canon and bear evening vigilance in mind.
translations.idiomatic: I stand at his side as aide; my aim is to discharge my office. I ever recall the ancient canon and keep vigilance at dusk in mind.

sentences.zh: 按晉令，公府長史，官品第六，銅印，墨綬，朝服，進賢兩梁冠。

translations.literal: According to the Jin ordinance, the princely chief administrator, official rank six, bronze seal, black sash, court dress, two-ribbed worthy crown.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin ordinance ranks the princely chief administrator at grade six—bronze seal, black sash, court dress, and the two-ribbed worthy crown.

sentences.zh: 掾、屬，官品第七，朝服，進賢一梁冠。

translations.literal: Aides and staff officers, official rank seven, court dress, one-ribbed worthy crown.
translations.idiomatic: Aides and staff officers, grade seven—court dress and the one-ribbed worthy crown.

sentences.zh: 晉官表注，亦與令同。

translations.literal: Jin official tables and commentaries likewise accord with the ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: Jin official tables and their annotations agree with the ordinance.

sentences.zh: 而今長史、掾、屬，但著朱服而已，此則公違明文，積習成謬。

translations.literal: Yet today chief administrators, aides, and staff wear only scarlet robes—this openly violates written statute; long usage has become error.
translations.idiomatic: Today chief administrators, aides, and staff wear only scarlet robes—an open breach of written law, a long misuse hardened into error.

sentences.zh: 謂宜依舊制，長史兩梁冠，掾、屬一梁冠，並同備朝服。

translations.literal: I propose restoring the old system: chief administrators the two-ribbed crown, aides and staff the one-ribbed crown, all likewise provided court dress.
translations.idiomatic: I propose restoring the old rule: chief administrators the two-ribbed crown, aides and staff the one-ribbed crown, all fully equipped with court dress.

sentences.zh: 中單韋舄，率由舊章。

translations.literal: Inner tunics and leather slippers—all according to the old regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Inner tunics and leather slippers, all as the old regulations prescribe.

sentences.zh: 若所上蒙允，并請班司徒二府及諸儀同三府，通為永準。

translations.literal: If the memorial is approved, I also request promulgation to both establishments of the Excellency of Works and all honorary three-establishment offices, as an everlasting standard.
translations.idiomatic: If approved, I ask that it be issued to both Works establishments and all honorary three-establishment offices as a permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 又尋舊事，司徒公府領步兵者職僚悉同降朝不領兵者。

translations.literal: Further, reviewing old precedents: in the Excellency of Works establishment, staff of the office that commanded infantry all matched those who attended court but did not command troops.
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing precedent, in the Works establishment the staff of offices commanding infantry matched those who attended court without commanding troops.

sentences.zh: 主簿祭酒，中單韋舄並備，令史以下，唯著玄衣。

translations.literal: Chief clerks and libationers had inner tunics and leather slippers complete; clerks below wore only dark robes.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks and libationers were fully equipped with inner tunics and leather slippers; clerks below wore only dark robes.

sentences.zh: 今府既開公，謹遵此制。

translations.literal: Now that the establishment is opened as a princely domain, I respectfully follow this regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Now that the establishment is opened as a princely domain, I respectfully follow this rule.

sentences.zh: 其或有署臺位者，玄服為疑。

translations.literal: Those who hold concurrent positions at the Secretariat—the dark robes present a difficulty.
translations.idiomatic: For those who also hold Secretariat posts, the dark robes raise a question.

sentences.zh: 按令稱諸有兼官，皆從重官之例。

translations.literal: The ordinance states that all who hold concurrent offices follow the higher office's rule.
translations.idiomatic: The ordinance says that all who hold concurrent posts follow the higher office.

sentences.zh: 尋內官為重，其署臺位者，悉宜著位之服，不在玄服之例。

translations.literal: Considering that inner-court offices are higher, those who hold Secretariat posts should all wear the dress of their Secretariat rank, not falling under the dark-robe rule.
translations.idiomatic: Inner-court offices outrank the rest; those with Secretariat posts should wear their Secretariat dress and not fall under the dark-robe rule.

sentences.zh: 若署諸卿寺位兼府職者，雖三品，而卿寺為卑，則宜依公府玄衣之制。

translations.literal: If they hold posts in the various ministers' bureaus concurrently with princely duties, though third rank, the ministerial bureau is lower—then they should follow the princely establishment's dark-robe rule.
translations.idiomatic: If they hold ministerial bureau posts alongside princely duties, though third rank, the bureau is lower—they should follow the princely establishment's dark-robe rule.

sentences.zh: 服章事重，禮儀所先，請臺詳服。

translations.literal: Cap and insignia are weighty matters; ritual precedes all—I request the Secretariat deliberate on dress.
translations.idiomatic: Cap and insignia are weighty matters and ritual comes first—I ask the Secretariat to rule on dress.

sentences.zh: 」儀曹郎中沈俁之議曰：「制珪象德，損替因時；

translations.literal: " Shen Yizhi, Gentleman of the Bureau of Rites, argued: "Regulations and jades symbolize virtue; increase and decrease follow the times;
translations.idiomatic: " Shen Yizhi of the Bureau of Rites argued: "Regulations and jades embody virtue; additions and reductions follow the times;

sentences.zh: 裁服象功，施用隨代。

translations.literal: Garments cut to symbolize merit, applied as each age requires.
translations.idiomatic: Garments shaped to embody merit are deployed as each age demands.

sentences.zh: 車旗變於商、周，冠佩革於秦、漢，豈必殊代襲容，改尚沿物哉。

translations.literal: Carriages and banners changed from Shang to Zhou; caps and ornaments were transformed under Qin and Han—must each age inherit the same appearance and merely alter what is revered?
translations.idiomatic: Carriages and banners changed from Shang to Zhou; caps and ornaments were remade under Qin and Han—must every age inherit the same look and only swap what it reveres?

sentences.zh: 夫邊貂假幸侍之首，賤幘登尊極之顏，一適時用，便隆後制。

translations.literal: Marten tails at the border assumed the foremost place of attendants; humble kerchiefs mounted to the imperial countenance—suited to the moment, they at once elevated later institutions.
translations.idiomatic: Border marten tails stood in for attendants' foremost insignia; humble kerchiefs rose to the imperial brow—once suited to the moment, they at once became later institutions.

sentences.zh: 況朱裳以朝，緬傾百祀，韋舄不加，浩然惟舊。

translations.literal: How much more scarlet robes for court, spanning a hundred generations; to omit leather slippers would violate what has stood firm as custom.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet robes for court have spanned a hundred generations; to drop leather slippers would break what has long stood as custom.

sentences.zh: 服為定章，事成永則。

translations.literal: Dress is fixed regulation; once settled it becomes everlasting rule.
translations.idiomatic: Dress is fixed statute; once settled it becomes everlasting law.

sentences.zh: 其儉之所秉，會非古訓。

translations.literal: What Jian champions does not accord with ancient teaching.
translations.idiomatic: What Jian urges does not match ancient teaching.

sentences.zh: 青素相因，代有損益，何事棄盛宋之興法，追往晉之頹典。

translations.literal: Blue and green succeed each other; each age has its adjustments—why abandon the flourishing statutes of Song to chase Jin's decayed canon?
translations.idiomatic: Blue and green succeed one another; each age adjusts its own—why cast off Song's flourishing statutes to chase Jin's decayed canon?

sentences.zh: 變改空煩，謂不宜革。

translations.literal: Empty reforms would be toil; I hold reform inappropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Change for change's sake is mere trouble; reform is unwarranted.

sentences.zh: 」儉又上議曰：「自頃服章多闕，有違前準，近議依令文，被報不宜改革，又稱左丞劉議，『按令文，凡有朝服，今多闕亡。

translations.literal: " Jian again submitted: "Of late dress and insignia have been widely lacking, in breach of former standards. A recent proposal followed the ordinance text but was answered that reform was inappropriate. It also cited Assistant Director Liu: 'According to the ordinance, all who should have court dress now largely lack it.
translations.idiomatic: " Jian submitted again: "Lately dress and insignia have been widely neglected, contrary to former standards. A recent proposal followed the ordinance, but the reply was that reform was inappropriate. It also cited Assistant Director Liu: 'The ordinance text requires court dress for all who should have it, yet most now lack it.

sentences.zh: 然則文存服損，非唯鉉佐，用捨既久，即為舊章』。

translations.literal: Thus the text survives while dress is diminished—not only for aides and staff; long disuse has itself become old custom.'
translations.idiomatic: So the text survives while the dress is lost—not for aides alone; long disuse has itself become custom.'

sentences.zh: 如下旨。

translations.literal: As the imperial directive states.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the imperial reply.

sentences.zh: 伏尋皇宋受終，每因晉舊制，律令條章，同規在昔。

translations.literal: I reflect that when Great Song received the mandate, it always followed Jin institutions; statutes and ordinances alike looked to the past.
translations.idiomatic: When Great Song received the mandate, it always followed Jin institutions; statutes and ordinances alike looked to the past.

sentences.zh: 若事有宜，必合懲改，則當上關詔書，下由朝議，縣諸日月，垂則後昆。

translations.literal: If something ought to be changed, it must be reported in an edict and decided in court, posted to the sun and moon, and made a model for posterity.
translations.idiomatic: If change is warranted, it should go up in an edict and down through court debate, set beside sun and moon, and made a model for posterity.

sentences.zh: 豈得因外府之乖謬，以為盛宋之興典，用晉氏之律令，而謂其儀為頹法哉。

translations.literal: How can the errors of an outer establishment be taken as the flourishing statutes of Great Song, and Jin ordinances be called decayed law?
translations.idiomatic: How can one outer establishment's lapse stand as Great Song's flourishing statute, or Jin ordinances be called decayed law?

sentences.zh: 順違從失，非所望於高議；

translations.literal: To follow error and abandon what is right is not what a lofty debate should seek;
translations.idiomatic: To follow error and abandon right is not what a high debate should aim at;

sentences.zh: 申明舊典，何改革之可論。

translations.literal: to clarify the old canon—what room is there to argue for reform?
translations.idiomatic: to clarify the old canon—what case is there for reform?

sentences.zh: 又左丞引令史之闕服，以為鉉佐之明比。

translations.literal: The Assistant Director also cited clerks' lack of dress as a parallel for aides' clarity.
translations.idiomatic: The Assistant Director also cited clerks' curtailed dress as a parallel for aides.

sentences.zh: 夫名位不同，禮數異等，令史從省，或有權宜；

translations.literal: Names and ranks differ; ritual numbers differ in grade. Clerks may be simplified by expedient;
translations.idiomatic: Names and ranks differ; ritual grades differ. Clerks may be reduced by expedient;

sentences.zh: 達官簡略，為失彌重。

translations.literal: for high officials to be curtailed is a far graver fault.
translations.idiomatic: for high officers to be curtailed is a far graver lapse.

sentences.zh: 又主簿、祭酒，備服於王庭，長史、掾、屬，朱衣以就列。

translations.literal: Chief clerks and libationers were fully equipped for attendance at court, while chief administrators, aides, and staff wore scarlet robes to take their places.
translations.idiomatic: Chief clerks and libationers were fully dressed for court, while chief administrators, aides, and staff took their places in scarlet robes.

sentences.zh: 於是倫比，自成矛盾。

translations.literal: Thus compared by rank, the practice contradicts itself.
translations.idiomatic: Set side by side by rank, the practice contradicts itself.

sentences.zh: 此而可忍，孰不可安。

translations.literal: If this can be borne, what cannot be endured?
translations.idiomatic: If this can be tolerated, what cannot?

sentences.zh: 將引令以遵舊，臺據失以為例，研詳符旨，良所未譬。

translations.literal: To cite the ordinance to follow the old, yet take the office's lapse as precedent—having studied the directive, I truly cannot understand.
translations.idiomatic: To invoke the ordinance for the old rule, yet treat the office's lapse as precedent—having weighed the reply, I cannot fathom it.

sentences.zh: 當官而行，何強之有，制令昭然，守以無貳。

translations.literal: To act as office requires—where is the force? The ordinance is plain; hold to it without wavering.
translations.idiomatic: To do one's office—where is the compulsion? The ordinance is clear; keep it without second thought.

sentences.zh: 」俁之又議：「雲火從物，沿損異儀，帝樂五殊，王禮三變，豈獨大宋造命，必咸仍於晉舊哉！

translations.literal: " Yizhi argued again: "Cloud and fire follow things; along the way dress differs. The emperor's music has five variants; royal rites have three changes—must Great Song, receiving the mandate, wholly cling to Jin custom?
translations.idiomatic: " Yizhi argued again: "Cloud and fire follow their objects; dress alters along the way. Imperial music has five forms; royal rites three changes—must Great Song, on receiving the mandate, cling wholly to Jin custom?

sentences.zh: 夫宗社疑文，庭廟闕典，或上降制書，下協朝議，何乃鉉府佐屬裳黻，稍改白虎之詔，斷宣室之疇咨乎。

translations.literal: When the altars of state or court rites lack clear text, edicts descend and court debate agrees—how can aides of the great establishment alter their patterned robes and overturn an imperial pronouncement from the Hall of Brightness?
translations.idiomatic: When state altars or court rites lack clear text, edicts descend and court debate settles it—how can aides of the great establishment alter their robes and overturn an imperial ruling from the Hall of Brightness?

sentences.zh: 又許令史之從省，咎達官之簡略。

translations.literal: He also approves clerks' reduction yet blames high officers' simplification.
translations.idiomatic: He approves clerks' reduction yet faults high officers' simplification.

sentences.zh: 律苟可遵，固無辨於貴賤；

translations.literal: If the statute can be followed, rank high or low makes no difference;
translations.idiomatic: If the statute can be followed, rank makes no difference;

sentences.zh: 規若必等，亦何關於權宜。

translations.literal: if the rule must be equal, what has expedient to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: if the rule must be uniform, what has expedient to do with it?

sentences.zh: 一用一舍，彌增其滯。

translations.literal: One use, one discard—only deepens the stagnation.
translations.idiomatic: One rule applied, one waived—only deepens the deadlock.

sentences.zh: 且佐非韋舄之職，吏本朝服之官，凡在班列，罔不如一，此蓋前令違而遂改，今制允而長用也。

translations.literal: Aides are not officers of leather slippers; clerks are by nature officers of court dress. All in the ranks should be alike—this is where the old ordinance was breached and then changed; the present rule was approved and has long been used.
translations.idiomatic: Aides are not officers of leather slippers; clerks are by nature court-dress officers. All in the ranks should match—here the old ordinance was breached and then changed; the present rule was approved and has long stood.

sentences.zh: 爵異服殊，寧會矛盾之譬；

translations.literal: Ranks differ and dress differs—how can that invite talk of contradiction?
translations.idiomatic: Ranks differ and dress differs—how does that invite talk of contradiction?

sentences.zh: 討論疑制，焉取強弱之辨。

translations.literal: To debate doubtful regulations, why invoke distinctions of strong and weak?

translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen-of-the-Interior, colonels, and commandants of Pacifying the Barbarians and Martial Fierce: silver seal.

sentences.zh: 朝服，武冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 其以此官為千人司馬虎賁督以上、及司馬史者，皆假青綬。

translations.literal: Those who held these posts as Tiger Garrison superintendents of thousand-man units and above, or as masters-of-carriages clerks, all wore provisionally granted blue sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held these posts as Tiger Garrison superintendents of thousand-man units and above, or as masters-of-carriages clerks, all wore blue sashes provisionally.

sentences.zh: 別部司馬、軍假司馬，銀印。

translations.literal: Separate-division masters of carriages and army provisional masters of carriages: silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: Separate-division masters of carriages and army provisional masters of carriages: silver seal.

sentences.zh: 朝服，武冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 圖像都匠行水中郎將、校尉、都尉，銀印，青綬。

translations.literal: Gentlemen-of-the-Interior, colonels, and commandants of the Director of Iconography and Craftsmen and the Director of Waterways: silver seal, blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: Gentlemen-of-the-Interior, colonels, and commandants of the Director of Iconography and Craftsmen and the Director of Waterways: silver seal, blue sash.

sentences.zh: 朝服，武冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 若非以工伎巧能特加此官者，不加綬。

translations.literal: Unless the post was specially conferred for craft skill and ingenuity, no sash was added.
translations.idiomatic: Unless the post was specially conferred for craft skill and ingenuity, no sash was issued.

sentences.zh: 羽林郎、羽林長郎，佩武猛都尉以上印者，假青綬。

translations.literal: Cadets and senior cadets of the Forest of Feathers who wore seals of Martial Fierce commandants and above wore provisionally granted blue sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Forest of Feathers cadets and senior cadets who bore seals of Martial Fierce commandants and above wore blue sashes provisionally.

sentences.zh: 別部司馬以下，假墨綬。

translations.literal: Below separate-division masters of carriages, provisionally granted black sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Below separate-division masters of carriages, black sashes were granted provisionally.

sentences.zh: 朝服，武冠。

translations.literal: Court dress, the martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 其長郎壯士，武弁冠。

translations.literal: Their senior cadets and stalwart soldiers: the martial-cap crown.
translations.idiomatic: Their senior cadets and stalwart soldiers wore the martial-cap crown.

sentences.zh: 在陛列及鹵簿，服絳縠單衣。

translations.literal: In the imperial staircase ranks and the guard of honor, scarlet-patterned single robes.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial staircase and in the guard of honor they wore scarlet-patterned single robes.

sentences.zh: 陛下甲僕射主事吏將騎、廷上五牛旗假使虎賁，在陛列及備鹵簿，服錦文衣，武冠，鶡尾。

translations.literal: Majordomos, chief clerks, chariot leaders, and cavalry of the Imperial Staircase A-Guard, and Tiger Garrison soldiers provisionally assigned to the Five-Ox Banner on the imperial terrace: when in the imperial staircase ranks or serving in the guard of honor, brocade-patterned robes, the martial crown, and crossbill plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Majordomos, chief clerks, chariot leaders, and cavalry of the Imperial Staircase A-Guard, and Tiger Garrison soldiers provisionally assigned to the Five-Ox Banner on the imperial terrace wore brocade-patterned robes, the martial crown, and crossbill plumes on the imperial staircase and in the guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 陛長，假銅印，墨綬。

translations.literal: Staircase chiefs wore provisionally granted bronze seals and black sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Staircase chiefs wore bronze seals and black sashes granted provisionally.

sentences.zh: 旄頭。

translations.literal: Maotou.
translations.idiomatic: They wore maotou.

sentences.zh: 羽林在陛列及備鹵簿，服絳科單衣，上著韋畫要襦。

translations.literal: When the Forest of Feathers was in the imperial staircase ranks or serving in the guard of honor, they wore scarlet regulation single robes with painted-leather waist-jackets over them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Forest of Feathers stood on the imperial staircase or in the guard of honor, they wore scarlet regulation single robes with painted-leather waist-jackets over them.

sentences.zh: 假旄頭。

translations.literal: Provisionally granted maotou.
translations.idiomatic: They were granted maotou provisionally.

sentences.zh: 舉輦跡禽前驅由基強弩司馬、守陵虎賁，佩武猛都尉以上印者，假青綬。

translations.literal: Masters of carriages of the palanquin-bearers, track-followers, bird-scouts, vanguard archers, and strong crossbowmen, and tomb-guard Tiger Garrison soldiers who wore seals of Martial Fierce commandants and above wore provisionally granted blue sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Masters of carriages of the palanquin-bearers, track-followers, bird-scouts, vanguard archers, and strong crossbowmen, and tomb-guard Tiger Garrison soldiers who bore seals of Martial Fierce commandants and above wore blue sashes provisionally.

sentences.zh: 別部司馬以下，假墨綬。

translations.literal: Below separate-division masters of carriages, provisionally granted black sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Below separate-division masters of carriages, black sashes were granted provisionally.

sentences.zh: 守陵虎賁，給絳科單衣，武冠。

translations.literal: Tomb-guard tiger guards: granted scarlet regulated single robes, martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Tomb-guard tiger guards received scarlet regulated single robes and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 殿中宂從虎賁、殿中虎賁、及守陵者持鈒戟宂從虎賁，佩武猛都尉以下印者，假青綬。

translations.literal: Supernumerary tiger guards of the hall, hall tiger guards, and tomb-guard supernumerary tiger guards bearing hooked halberds who wore seals below Martial-Fierce Commandant: provisional blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: Supernumerary hall tiger guards, hall tiger guards, and tomb-guard supernumerary tiger guards bearing hooked halberds who wore seals below Martial-Fierce Commandant wore a provisional blue sash.

sentences.zh: 別部司馬以下，假墨綬。

translations.literal: Below detached-division marshal: provisional black sash.
translations.idiomatic: Below detached-division marshal: provisional black sash.

sentences.zh: 絳科單衣，武冠。

translations.literal: Scarlet regulated single robes, martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Scarlet regulated single robes and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 持椎斧武騎虎賁、五騎傳詔虎賁、殿中羽林及守陵者太官尚食虎賁、稱飯宰人、諸宮尚食虎賁，佩武猛都尉以上印者，假青綬。

translations.literal: Tiger guards bearing mace-axes as martial riders, Five-Horse edict-bearers, hall Forest Guards and tomb-guards of the Grand Provisioner's food service, food-presenting stewards, and palace food-service tiger guards who wore seals of Martial-Fierce Commandant or above: provisional blue sash.
translations.idiomatic: Tiger guards bearing mace-axes as martial riders, Five-Horse edict-bearers, hall Forest Guards, tomb-guards of the Grand Provisioner's food service, food-presenting stewards, and palace food-service tiger guards who wore seals of Martial-Fierce Commandant or above wore a provisional blue sash.

sentences.zh: 別部司馬以下，假墨綬。

translations.literal: Below detached-division marshal: provisional black sash.
translations.idiomatic: Below detached-division marshal: provisional black sash.

sentences.zh: 給絳褠，武冠。

translations.literal: Granted scarlet jackets, martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: They received scarlet jackets and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 其在陛列及備鹵簿，五騎虎賁，服錦文衣，鶡尾。

translations.literal: When in the imperial staircase ranks and in the guard of honor, Five-Horse tiger guards wore brocade-pattern robes and crossbill plumes.
translations.idiomatic: On the imperial staircase or in the guard of honor, Five-Horse tiger guards wore brocade-pattern robes and crossbill plumes.

sentences.zh: 宰人服離支衣。

translations.literal: Stewards wore lychee-pattern robes.
translations.idiomatic: Stewards wore lychee-pattern robes.

sentences.zh: 黃門鼓吹、及釘官僕射、黃門鼓吹史主事、諸官鼓吹、尚書廊下都坐門下守閤、殿中威儀騶、虎賁常直殿黃雲龍門者、門下左右部虎賁羽林騶、給傳事者諸導騶、門下中書守閤，給絳褠，武冠。

translations.literal: Yellow Gate musicians, Nail Office director, Yellow Gate musician clerks and chief clerks, all office musicians, Secretariat corridor attendants, Gate Office and Secretariat gatekeepers, hall protocol outriders, tiger guards regularly posted at the Yellow Cloud Dragon Gate, Gate Office left and right tiger-guard and Forest Guard outriders, all guide-outriders for message-bearers, and Gate Office Secretariat gatekeepers: granted scarlet jackets, martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow Gate musicians, the Nail Office director, Yellow Gate musician clerks and chief clerks, all office musicians, Secretariat corridor attendants, Gate Office and Secretariat gatekeepers, hall protocol outriders, tiger guards regularly posted at the Yellow Cloud Dragon Gate, Gate Office left and right tiger-guard and Forest Guard outriders, guide-outriders for message-bearers, and Gate Office Secretariat gatekeepers received scarlet jackets and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 南書門下虎賁羽林騶、蘭臺五曹節藏射廊下守閤、威儀、發符騶、都水使者黃沙廊下守閤、謁者、錄事、威儀騶、河隄謁者騶、諸官謁者騶，絳褠，武冠。

translations.literal: South Documents Gate Office tiger-guard and Forest Guard outriders, Orchid Terrace Five Offices seal-store corridor gatekeepers, protocol officers, tally-issuing outriders, Chief of Waters corridor gatekeepers at Yellow Sand, ushers, recorders, protocol outriders, Yellow River embankment usher outriders, and all office usher outriders: scarlet jackets, martial crown.
translations.idiomatic: South Documents Gate Office tiger-guard and Forest Guard outriders, Orchid Terrace Five Offices seal-store corridor gatekeepers, protocol officers, tally-issuing outriders, Chief of Waters corridor gatekeepers at Yellow Sand, ushers, recorders, protocol outriders, Yellow River embankment usher outriders, and all office usher outriders wore scarlet jackets and the martial crown.

sentences.zh: 給其衣服，自如故事。

translations.literal: Their garments were supplied according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Their garments were supplied according to precedent.

sentences.zh: 大誰士皁科單衣，樊噲冠。

translations.literal: Chief challenge-guards: black regulated single robes, Fan Kuai cap.
translations.idiomatic: Chief challenge-guards wore black regulated single robes and the Fan Kuai cap.

sentences.zh: 衞士墨布褠，却敵冠。

translations.literal: Guardsmen: black cloth jackets, repelling-enemy cap.
translations.idiomatic: Guardsmen wore black cloth jackets and the repelling-enemy cap.

sentences.zh: 凡此前眾職，江左多不備，又多闕朝服。

translations.literal: In general, for all these offices above, east of the Yangzi many were not provided for, and court dress was often lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In general, for all these offices above, the Jiangzuo court often did not supply them, and court dress was frequently lacking.

sentences.zh: 諸應給朝服佩玉，而不在京都者給朝服，非護烏丸羌夷戎蠻諸校尉以上及刺史、西域戊己校尉，皆不給佩玉。

translations.literal: All who should receive court dress with jade pendants but were not in the capital received court dress; except Protectors of the Wuhuan, Qiang, Rong, Yi, Man, and colonels above them, and inspectors, and the Garrison of Wuji Colonel in the Western Regions—none received jade pendants.
translations.idiomatic: All who were due court dress with jade pendants but were not in the capital received court dress; except colonels who protected the Wuhuan, Qiang, Rong, Yi, and Man, colonels of that rank and above, inspectors, and the Garrison of Wuji Colonel in the Western Regions—none received jade pendants.

sentences.zh: 其來朝會，權時假給，會罷輸還。

translations.literal: When they came to court audiences, it was granted provisionally for the occasion; when the audience ended, it was returned.
translations.idiomatic: When they came to court audiences, dress was loaned for the occasion and returned when the audience ended.

sentences.zh: 凡應朝服者，而官不給，聽自具之。

translations.literal: All who should have court dress but whom the office did not supply were permitted to provide it themselves.
translations.idiomatic: All who were due court dress but whom the office did not supply might provide it themselves.

sentences.zh: 諸假印綬而官不給鞶囊者，得自具作。

translations.literal: Those who held provisional seals and sashes but whom the office did not supply pan pouches might make them themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Those who held provisional seals and sashes but received no pan pouch from the office might make one themselves.

sentences.zh: 其但假印不假綬者，不得佩綬。

translations.literal: Those who received only a provisional seal and not a sash might not wear a sash.
translations.idiomatic: Those who received only a provisional seal and not a sash might not wear a sash.

sentences.zh: 鞶，古制也。

translations.literal: The pan was an ancient institution.
translations.idiomatic: The pan pouch was an ancient institution.

sentences.zh: 漢代著鞶囊者，側在腰間。

translations.literal: In Han those who wore pan pouches carried them at the side of the waist.
translations.idiomatic: In Han those who wore pan pouches carried them at the side of the waist.

sentences.zh: 或謂之傍囊，或謂之綬囊。

translations.literal: Some called it the side pouch, some the sash pouch.
translations.idiomatic: Some called it the side pouch, some the sash pouch.

sentences.zh: 然則以此囊盛綬也。

translations.literal: Thus this pouch held the sash.
translations.idiomatic: Thus this pouch held the sash.

sentences.zh: 或盛或散，各有其時乎。

translations.literal: Whether it held the sash or lay empty, each had its season, it seems.
translations.idiomatic: Whether it held the sash or lay empty, each had its season, it seems.

sentences.zh: 朝服一具，冠幘各一，絳緋袍、皁緣中單衣領袖各一領，革帶袷袴各一，舄、袜各一量，簪導餉自副。

translations.literal: One set of court dress: one cap and one kerchief each; one crimson robe, one black-bordered inner robe with collar and sleeves each; one leather belt and lined trousers each; one pair of shoes and one measure of socks each; hairpin, hair-guide, and ear-stops as accessories.
translations.idiomatic: One set of court dress comprised one cap and one kerchief; one crimson robe and one black-bordered inner robe with collar and sleeves; one leather belt and one pair of lined trousers; one pair of shoes and socks; and hairpin, hair-guide, and ear-stops as accessories.

sentences.zh: 四時朝服者，加絳絹黃緋青緋皁緋袍單衣各一領；

translations.literal: For four-season court dress, add one each of crimson silk, yellow, green, blue-green, and black unlined robes;
translations.idiomatic: Four-season court dress added one each of crimson silk, yellow, green, blue-green, and black unlined robes;

sentences.zh: 五時朝服者，加給白絹袍單衣一領。

translations.literal: for five-season court dress, add one white silk unlined robe.
translations.idiomatic: Five-season court dress added one white silk unlined robe.

sentences.zh: 諸受朝服，單衣七丈二尺，科單衣及褠五丈二尺，中衣絹五丈，緣皁一丈八尺，領袖練一匹一尺，絹七尺五寸。

translations.literal: For all who received court dress: unlined robe seven zhang two chi; regulated unlined robe and jacket five zhang two chi; inner-robe silk five zhang; black border one zhang eight chi; collar and sleeve refined silk one bolt one chi; silk seven chi five cun.
translations.idiomatic: Those who received court dress were allotted seven zhang two chi of cloth for the unlined robe; five zhang two chi for the regulated unlined robe and jacket; five zhang of silk for the inner robe; one zhang eight chi of black border; one bolt one chi of refined silk for collar and sleeves; and seven chi five cun of silk.

sentences.zh: 給袴練一丈四尺，縑二丈。

translations.literal: Granted for trousers: refined silk one zhang four chi, thin silk two zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Trousers were supplied with one zhang four chi of refined silk and two zhang of thin silk.

sentences.zh: 袜布三尺。

translations.literal: Sock cloth three chi.
translations.idiomatic: Sock cloth: three chi.

sentences.zh: 單衣及褠袷帶，縑各一段，長七尺。

translations.literal: For unlined robe and jacket lined belt, thin silk one section each, seven chi long.
translations.idiomatic: For the unlined robe and jacket lined belt, one section of thin silk each, seven chi long.

sentences.zh: 江左止給絹各有差。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi only silk was granted, each grade differing.
translations.idiomatic: East of the Yangzi only silk was granted, in differing amounts by rank.

sentences.zh: 宋元嘉末，斷不復給，至今。

translations.literal: At the end of Yuanjia in Song and Yuan, the grant was cut off and has not resumed to the present.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Yuanjia in Song and Yuan, the grant was cut off and has not resumed to the present.

sentences.zh: 山鹿、豽、柱豽、白豽、施毛狐白領、黃豹、斑白鼲子、渠搜裘、步搖、八䥖、蔽結、多服蟬、明中、欋白，又諸織成衣帽、錦帳、純金銀器、雲母從廣一寸以上物者，皆為禁物。

translations.literal: Mountain-deer, ferret-badger, pillar-ferret, white ferret-badger, fox fur with white collar, yellow leopard, spotted white sable, Qusou fur coats, swaying hairpins, eight-prong ornaments, covering-knots, multi-layer cicada ornaments, mingzhong, qubai, and all woven caps and robes, brocade curtains, pure gold and silver vessels, and mica pieces more than one cun wide were all forbidden objects.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain-deer fur, ferret-badger, pillar-ferret, white ferret-badger, fox fur with white collar, yellow leopard, spotted white sable, Qusou fur coats, swaying hairpins, eight-prong ornaments, covering-knots, multi-layer cicada ornaments, mingzhong, qubai, and all woven caps and robes, brocade curtains, pure gold and silver vessels, and mica pieces more than one cun wide were all forbidden luxuries.

sentences.zh: 諸在官品令第二品以上，其非禁物，皆得服之。

translations.literal: All officials of rank two and above in the office-rank ordinance might wear what was not forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: Officials of rank two and above in the office-rank ordinance might wear anything not on the forbidden list.

sentences.zh: 第三品以下，加不得服三䥖以上、蔽結、爵叉、假真珠翡翠校飾纓佩、雜采衣、杯文綺、齊繡黼、𨮹離、袿袍。

translations.literal: Rank three and below were further forbidden three-prong ornaments and above, covering-knots, noble-fork ornaments, false pearl and jadeite trappings on tassels and pendants, mixed-color garments, cup-pattern brocade, Qi embroidery with fu patterns, quli, and gui robes.
translations.idiomatic: Rank three and below were further barred from three-prong ornaments and above, covering-knots, noble-fork ornaments, false pearl and jadeite trappings on tassels and pendants, mixed-color garments, cup-pattern brocade, Qi embroidery with fu patterns, quli, and gui robes.

sentences.zh: 第六品以下，加不得服金䥖、綾、錦、錦繡、七緣綺、貂豽裘、金叉鐶鉺、及以金校飾器物、張絳帳。

translations.literal: Rank six and below were further forbidden gold prongs, damask, brocade, brocade embroidery, seven-border gauze, sable and ferret-badger coats, gold fork-rings and ear-stops, and gold-trimmed vessels, and hanging crimson curtains.
