translations.idiomatic: Rank six and below were further barred from gold prongs, damask, brocade, brocade embroidery, seven-border gauze, sable and ferret-badger coats, gold fork-rings and ear-stops, gold-trimmed vessels, and crimson curtains.

sentences.zh: 第八品以下，加不得服羅、紈、綺、縠，雜色真文。

translations.literal: Rank eight and below were further forbidden gauze, fine silk, patterned silk, regulated gauze, and mixed-color true patterns.
translations.idiomatic: Rank eight and below were further barred from gauze, fine silk, patterned silk, regulated gauze, and mixed-color true patterns.

sentences.zh: 騎士卒百工人，加不得服大絳紫襈、假結、真珠璫珥、犀、瑇瑁、越疊、以銀飾器物、張帳、乘犢車，履色無過綠、青、白。

translations.literal: Cavalry soldiers and hundred-craftsmen were further forbidden great crimson and purple bordered robes, false knots, true pearl ear-pendants, rhinoceros horn, tortoise shell, Yue layered fabrics, silver-trimmed vessels, hanging curtains, riding calf carts, and shoe colors beyond green, blue, and white.
translations.idiomatic: Cavalry soldiers and artisans were further barred from great crimson and purple bordered robes, false knots, true pearl ear-pendants, rhinoceros horn, tortoise shell, Yue layered fabrics, silver-trimmed vessels, hanging curtains, calf carts, and shoe colors beyond green, blue, and white.

sentences.zh: 奴婢衣食客，加不得服白幘、蒨、絳、金黃銀叉、鐶、鈴、𨮹、鉺，履色無過純青。

translations.literal: Slaves, servants, and dependent clients were further forbidden white kerchiefs, madder, crimson, gold, yellow, silver forks, rings, bells, quli, and ear-stops, and shoe colors beyond plain blue.
translations.idiomatic: Slaves, servants, and dependent clients were further barred from white kerchiefs, madder, crimson, gold, yellow, silver forks, rings, bells, quli, and ear-stops, and shoe colors beyond plain blue.

sentences.zh: 諸去官及薨卒不祿物故，家人所服，皆得從故官之例。

translations.literal: For all who left office, died without salary, or perished, what their households might wear all followed the former office's rule.
translations.idiomatic: When officials left office, died without salary, or perished, what their households might wear all followed the former office's rule.

sentences.zh: 諸王皆不得私作禁物，及罽碧校鞍，珠玉金銀錯刻鏤彫飾無用之物。

translations.literal: All princes might not privately make forbidden objects, or saddles with felt and jade trappings, or useless things carved, inlaid, chased, and engraved in pearl, jade, gold, and silver.
translations.idiomatic: Princes might not privately make forbidden objects, saddles with felt and jade trappings, or useless things carved, inlaid, chased, and engraved in pearl, jade, gold, and silver.

sentences.zh: 天子坐漆牀，居朱屋。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven sat on a lacquered couch and dwelt in a vermilion hall.
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven sat on a lacquered couch and dwelt in a vermilion hall.

sentences.zh: 史臣按左傳，丹桓宮之楹。

translations.literal: The historian notes that the Zuo Commentary records reddening the pillars of Duke Huan's palace.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes that the Zuo Commentary records reddening the pillars of Duke Huan's palace.

sentences.zh: 何休注公羊，亦有朱屋以居。

translations.literal: He Xiu's commentary on the Gongyang also has dwelling in a vermilion hall.
translations.idiomatic: He Xiu's commentary on the Gongyang also mentions dwelling in a vermilion hall.

sentences.zh: 所從來久矣。

translations.literal: The practice has been long in coming.
translations.idiomatic: The practice is of long standing.

sentences.zh: 漆牀亦當是漢代舊儀，而漢儀不載。

translations.literal: The lacquered couch too must be Han old usage, yet the Han Rites do not record it.
translations.idiomatic: The lacquered couch too must be old Han usage, yet the Han Rites do not record it.

sentences.zh: 尋所以必朱必漆者，其理有可言焉。

translations.literal: To seek why it must be vermilion and lacquer, the reason can be stated.
translations.idiomatic: As for why it must be vermilion and lacquer, the reason can be stated.

sentences.zh: 夫珍木嘉樹，其品非一，莫不植根深岨，致之未易。

translations.literal: Fine timbers and excellent trees are not of one kind; none fail to root deep on lofty slopes, and to obtain them is not easy.
translations.idiomatic: Rare timbers and fine trees come in many kinds; all root deep on high ground, and none is easy to obtain.

sentences.zh: 藉地廣之資，因人多之力，則役苦費深，為敝滋重。

translations.literal: Relying on broad land and many men's strength, labor is bitter, cost deep, and waste grows heavy.
translations.idiomatic: With broad lands and many hands at work, toil grows bitter, expense runs deep, and waste grows ever heavier.

sentences.zh: 是以上古聖王，采椽不斵，斵之則懼刻桷彫楹，莫知其限也。

translations.literal: Therefore the sage kings of high antiquity used undressed rafters; to dress them would fear carved corbels and painted pillars without knowing limit.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore the sage kings of high antiquity used undressed rafters; to dress them would invite carved corbels and painted pillars without limit.

sentences.zh: 哲人縣鑑微遠，杜漸防萌，知采椽不愜後代之心，不斵不為將來之用，故加朱施漆，以傳厥後。

translations.literal: The wise hung a mirror on what was minute and far, checked the first sprout and barred the bud, knowing undressed rafters would not satisfy later hearts and that not dressing them would leave nothing for future use—so they added vermilion and applied lacquer to hand it down to posterity.
translations.idiomatic: The wise fixed their mirror on what was minute and far off, checked the first sprout and barred the bud, knowing undressed rafters would not satisfy later ages and that not dressing them would leave nothing for the future—so they added vermilion and applied lacquer to hand the practice down to posterity.

sentences.zh: 散木凡材，皆可入用。

translations.literal: Common timber and ordinary wood can all enter use.
translations.idiomatic: Common timber and ordinary wood can all be put to use.

sentences.zh: 遠探幽旨，將在斯乎。

translations.literal: To probe the hidden intent far—does it lie in this?
translations.idiomatic: To probe the hidden intent from afar—is it not here?

sentences.zh: 殿屋之為圓淵方井兼植荷華者，以厭火祥也。

translations.literal: When hall buildings have round pools and square wells with lotus planted together, it is to quell fire omens.
translations.idiomatic: When hall buildings have round pools and square wells with lotus planted together, it is to quell fire omens.

sentences.zh: 古者貴賤皆執笏，其有事則搢之於腰帶，所謂搢紳之士者，搢笏而垂紳帶也。

translations.literal: In antiquity noble and base all held tablets; when there was business they tucked them in the belt—what are called girdle-and-sash gentlemen tuck the tablet and let the sash hang.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity noble and base all held tablets; when there was business they tucked them in the belt—hence the girdled gentleman, who tucks his tablet and lets the sash hang.

sentences.zh: 紳垂三尺。

translations.literal: The sash hung three chi.
translations.idiomatic: The sash hung three chi.

sentences.zh: 笏者有事則書之，故常簪筆，今之白筆，是其遺象。

translations.literal: The tablet was for writing when there was business; therefore a brush was always worn—today's white brush is its surviving image.
translations.idiomatic: The tablet was for writing when there was business; therefore a brush was always worn—today's white brush is its surviving trace.

sentences.zh: 三臺五省二品文官簪之。

translations.literal: Civil officials of the Three Terraces and Five Ministries of rank two wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Civil officials of the Three Terraces and Five Ministries of rank two wore it.

sentences.zh: 王公侯伯子男卿尹及武官不簪。

translations.literal: Kings, dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, ministers, prefects, and military officers did not wear it.
translations.idiomatic: Kings, dukes, marquises, earls, viscounts, barons, ministers, prefects, and military officers did not wear it.

sentences.zh: 加內侍位者，乃簪之。

translations.literal: Only those who added inner-attendant rank wore it.
translations.idiomatic: Only those who added inner-attendant rank wore it.

sentences.zh: 手板，則古笏矣。

translations.literal: The hand board is the ancient tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The hand board is the ancient tablet.

sentences.zh: 尚書令、僕射、尚書手板頭復有白筆，以紫皮裹之，名笏。

translations.literal: Director, Vice Director, and Directors of the Secretariat had white brushes again at the head of the hand board, wrapped in purple leather—called the tablet.
translations.idiomatic: The Director, Vice Director, and Directors of the Secretariat had white brushes again at the head of the hand board, wrapped in purple leather—this was called the tablet.

sentences.zh: 朝服肩上有紫生袷囊，綴之朝服外，俗呼曰紫荷。

translations.literal: Court dress had on the shoulder a purple raw lined pouch, stitched outside the court dress; vulgarly called purple lotus.
translations.idiomatic: Court dress had on the shoulder a purple raw lined pouch stitched outside the robe; vulgarly called the purple lotus.

sentences.zh: 或云漢代以盛奏事，負荷以行，未詳也。

translations.literal: Some say in Han it held memorials, carried on the back when walking—not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Some say in Han it held memorials, carried on the back when walking—the point is not clear.

sentences.zh: 魏文帝黃初三年，詔賜漢太尉楊彪几杖，待以客禮。

translations.literal: In the third year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei decreed granting Han Grand Commandant Yang Biao armrest and staff, treating him with guest ritual.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Huangchu, Emperor Wen of Wei decreed that Han Grand Commandant Yang Biao receive armrest and staff and be treated with guest ritual.

sentences.zh: 延請之日，使挾杖入朝。

translations.literal: On the day he was invited, he was made to enter court leaning on the staff.
translations.idiomatic: On the day he was invited, he was made to enter court leaning on the staff.

sentences.zh: 又令著鹿皮冠。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to wear a deerskin cap.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to wear a deerskin cap.

sentences.zh: 彪辭讓，不聽。

translations.literal: Biao declined and remonstrated; the emperor would not listen.
translations.idiomatic: Biao declined and remonstrated; the emperor would not listen.

sentences.zh: 乃使服布單衣皮弁以見。

translations.literal: He was then made to appear in cloth single robe and skin cap.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made to appear in a cloth single robe and skin cap.

sentences.zh: 傅玄子曰：「漢末王公名士，多委王服，以幅巾為雅。

translations.literal: Fu Xuan's son said: "At the end of Han kings, dukes, and famous gentlemen mostly set aside royal dress and took the wide kerchief as refined.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Xuan's son said: "At the end of Han, kings, dukes, and famous gentlemen mostly set aside royal dress and took the wide kerchief as refined.

sentences.zh: 是以袁紹、崔鈞之徒，雖為將帥，皆著㡘巾。

translations.literal: Therefore Yuan Shao, Cui Jun, and the like, though generals and commanders, all wore folded kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Yuan Shao, Cui Jun, and the like, though generals and commanders, all wore folded kerchiefs.

sentences.zh: 」魏武以天下凶荒，資財乏匱，擬古皮弁，裁縑帛以為𢂿，合乎簡易隨時之義，以色別其貴賤。

translations.literal: " Emperor Wu of Wei, because the realm was fierce and waste and goods were scarce, modeled the ancient skin cap and cut thin silk to make the ze, fitting the meaning of simplicity suited to the time, using color to distinguish noble and base.
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Wu of Wei, because the realm knew famine and ruin and goods ran scarce, modeled the ancient skin cap and cut thin silk to make the ze, fitting simplicity suited to the time and using color to distinguish noble and base.

sentences.zh: 本施軍飾，非為國容也。

translations.literal: Originally it was military adornment, not state ceremonial dress.
translations.idiomatic: Originally it was military adornment, not state ceremonial dress.

sentences.zh: 徐爰曰：「俗說𢂿本未有歧，荀文若巾之，行觸樹枝成歧，謂之為善，因而弗改。

translations.literal: Xu Ai said: "Popular lore says the ze originally had no fork; Xun Wenruo wore it, and walking he struck a branch and made a fork, which was called auspicious, and therefore was not changed.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai said: "Popular lore says the ze originally had no fork; Xun Wenruo wore it, and walking he struck a branch and made a fork, which was called auspicious, and therefore was not changed.

sentences.zh: 」通以為慶弔服。

translations.literal: " In general it was taken as congratulation and mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: " In general it was taken as congratulation and mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 巾以葛為之，形如𢂿，而橫著之，古尊卑共服也。

translations.literal: The kerchief was made of kudzu, shaped like the ze but worn crosswise; ancient noble and base wore it alike.
translations.idiomatic: The kerchief was made of kudzu, shaped like the ze but worn crosswise; ancient noble and base wore it alike.

sentences.zh: 故漢末妖賊以黃為巾，時謂之「黃巾賊」。

translations.literal: Therefore at the end of Han rebel bandits used yellow for kerchiefs, and the age called them "Yellow Turban bandits."
translations.idiomatic: Therefore at the end of Han rebel bandits used yellow for kerchiefs, and the age called them "Yellow Turban bandits."

sentences.zh: 今國子太學生冠之，服單衣以為朝服，執一卷經以代手板。

translations.literal: Today National University students wear it, take single robe as court dress, and hold one scroll of classics in place of the hand board.
translations.idiomatic: Today National University students wear it, take the single robe as court dress, and hold one scroll of classics in place of the hand board.

sentences.zh: 居士野人，皆服巾焉。

translations.literal: Retired gentlemen and rustics all wear the kerchief.
translations.idiomatic: Retired gentlemen and rustics all wear the kerchief.

sentences.zh: 徐爰曰：「帽名猶冠也。

translations.literal: Xu Ai said: "The cap's name is like the crown.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Ai said: "The cap's name is like the crown.

sentences.zh: 義取於蒙覆其首。

translations.literal: The meaning is taken from covering the head.
translations.idiomatic: The meaning is taken from covering the head.

sentences.zh: 其本纚也。

translations.literal: Its origin is the tassel.
translations.idiomatic: Its origin is the tassel.

sentences.zh: 古者有冠無幘，冠下有纚，以繒為之。

translations.literal: In antiquity there were crowns without kerchiefs; below the crown was a tassel made of silk.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity there were crowns without kerchiefs; below the crown was a tassel made of silk.

sentences.zh: 後世施幘於冠，因裁纚為帽。

translations.literal: Later generations put kerchiefs on the crown and cut the tassel into a cap.
translations.idiomatic: Later generations put kerchiefs on the crown and cut the tassel into a cap.

sentences.zh: 自乘輿宴居，下至庶人無爵者，皆服之。

translations.literal: From the imperial carriage at leisure down to commoners without rank, all wore it.
translations.idiomatic: From the imperial carriage at leisure down to commoners without rank, all wore it.

sentences.zh: 」史臣案晉成帝咸和九年制，聽尚書八座丞郎、門下三省侍郎乘車白帢低幘出入掖門。

translations.literal: The historian notes that in the ninth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin it was decreed that Directors of the Eight Seats and Secretariat, Gate Office Three Departments vice-directors might ride in carriages with white kerchief and low kerchief when entering and leaving the side gates.
translations.idiomatic: The historian notes that in the ninth year of Xianhe of Emperor Cheng of Jin it was decreed that Directors of the Eight Seats and Secretariat, and Gate Office Three Departments vice-directors, might ride in carriages with white kerchief and low kerchief when entering and leaving the side gates.

sentences.zh: 又二宮直官著烏紗𢂿。

translations.literal: Also direct officials of the Two Palaces wore black silk ze.
translations.idiomatic: Direct officials of the Two Palaces also wore black silk ze.

sentences.zh: 然則士人宴居，皆著帢矣。

translations.literal: Thus gentlemen at leisure all wore kerchiefs.
translations.idiomatic: Thus gentlemen at leisure all wore kerchiefs.

sentences.zh: 而江左時野人已著帽，士人亦往往而然，但其頂圓耳。

translations.literal: Yet in the Jiangzuo age rustics already wore caps, and gentlemen often did so too, but the crown was round.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in the Jiangzuo age rustics already wore caps, and gentlemen often did so too, but the crown was round.

sentences.zh: 後乃高其屋云。

translations.literal: Later they raised the crown, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Later they raised the crown, it is said.

sentences.zh: 古者人君有朝服，有祭服，有宴服，有弔服。

translations.literal: In antiquity the ruler had court dress, sacrificial dress, feast dress, and mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity the ruler had court dress, sacrificial dress, feast dress, and mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 弔服皮弁疑衰，今以單衣黑幘為宴會服，拜陵亦如之。

translations.literal: Mourning dress was skin cap and suspected hemp; today single robe and black kerchief serve as feast dress, and tomb-visits are the same.
translations.idiomatic: Mourning dress was skin cap and suspected hemp; today single robe and black kerchief serve as feast dress, and tomb-visits are the same.

sentences.zh: 以單衣白裌為弔服，修敬尊秩亦服之也。

translations.literal: Single robe with white lining serves as mourning dress; for showing respect in rank it is also worn.
translations.idiomatic: Single robe with white lining serves as mourning dress; for showing respect in rank it is also worn.

sentences.zh: 單衣，古之深衣也。

translations.literal: The single robe is the ancient deep robe.
translations.idiomatic: The single robe is the ancient deep robe.

sentences.zh: 今單衣裁製與深衣同，唯絹帶為異。

translations.literal: Today's single robe is cut like the deep robe, differing only in the silk belt.
translations.idiomatic: Today's single robe is cut like the deep robe, differing only in the silk belt.

sentences.zh: 深衣絹帽以居喪。

translations.literal: The deep robe used silk cap in dwelling for mourning.
translations.idiomatic: The deep robe used silk cap in dwelling for mourning.

sentences.zh: 單衣素帢以施吉。

translations.literal: The single robe used plain kerchief for auspicious occasions.
translations.idiomatic: The single robe used plain kerchief for auspicious occasions.

sentences.zh: 晉武帝泰始三年，詔太宰安平王孚服侍中之服，賜大司馬義陽王望袞冕之服。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, an edict granted Grand Preceptor Prince Fu of Ping'an the dress of Attendant-in-Ordinary, and granted Grand Marshal Prince Wang of Yiyang the robe and coronet of highest honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taishi of Emperor Wu of Jin, an edict granted Grand Preceptor Prince Fu of Ping'an the dress of Attendant-in-Ordinary, and granted Grand Marshal Prince Wang of Yiyang the robe and coronet of highest honor.

sentences.zh: 四年，又詔趙、樂安、燕王服散騎常侍之服。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, an edict again ordered the kings of Zhao, Le'an, and Yan to wear the dress of Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year, another edict required the kings of Zhao, Le'an, and Yan to adopt the dress of a Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 十年，賜彭城王袞冕之服。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the Prince of Pengcheng was granted gun-and-mian robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, the Prince of Pengcheng received the highest ceremonial robe and coronet.

sentences.zh: 偽楚桓玄將篡，亦加安帝母弟太宰琅邪王袞冕服。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan of the false Chu regime was about to usurp the throne, he also bestowed gun-and-mian dress upon the Grand Preceptor, the Langye King, younger brother of Emperor An's mother.
translations.idiomatic: As the usurper Huan Xuan of false Chu prepared to seize the throne, he likewise invested the Grand Preceptor, the Langye King and younger brother of Emperor An's mother, with gun-and-mian dress.

sentences.zh: 宋興以來，王公貴臣加侍中、散騎常侍，乃得服貂璫也。

translations.literal: Since the rise of Song, princes and great ministers only upon receiving added titles of Attendant-in-Ordinary or Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry might wear sable and ornamental pendants.
translations.idiomatic: Since the founding of Song, only when princes and great ministers received the added titles of Attendant-in-Ordinary or Regular Attendant of the Rapid Cavalry might they wear sable fur and ornamental pendants.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武孝建元年，丞相南郡王義宣，二年，雍州刺史武昌王渾，又有異圖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the Chancellor Prince of Nanjun Yixuan; in the second year, the Inspector of Yongzhou Prince of Wuchang Hun—each harbored divergent ambitions.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, Chancellor Prince of Nanjun Yixuan rebelled; in the second year, Inspector of Yongzhou Prince of Wuchang Hun likewise harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 世祖嫌侯王強盛，欲加減削。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor resented the strength of the feudatory princes and wished to reduce and curtail them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu, posthumously Shizu, resented the power of the feudatory princes and sought to cut it back.

sentences.zh: 其年十月己未，大司馬江夏王義恭、驃騎大將軍竟陵王誕表改革諸王車服制度，凡九條，表在義恭傳。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day jiwei in the tenth month of that year, Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and Rapid Cavalry General Prince of Jingling Dan memorialized reform of the princes' carriage-and-dress regulations, nine articles in all, the memorial being in Yigong's biography.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei day in the tenth month of that year, Grand Marshal Prince of Jiangxia Yigong and Rapid Cavalry General Prince of Jingling Dan submitted a memorial reforming princely carriage and dress, nine articles in all, recorded in Yigong's biography.

sentences.zh: 上因諷有司更增廣條目。

translations.literal: The emperor thereby used indirect speech to prompt the relevant offices to add and expand the articles.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then prompted the responsible offices, by pointed allusion, to broaden the regulations further.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「車服以庸，虞書茂典；

translations.literal: They memorialized, saying: "Carriages and dress mark merit—an august canon of the Documents of Yu;
translations.idiomatic: The memorial read: "Carriages and dress mark merit—this is the august canon in the Documents of Yu;

sentences.zh: 名器慎假，春秋明誡。

translations.literal: titles and regalia are lent with caution—a clear warning of the Spring and Autumn Annals.
translations.idiomatic: titles and regalia must be granted with caution—the Spring and Autumn Annals state the warning plainly."

sentences.zh: 是以尚方所制，禁嚴漢律，諸侯竊服，雖親必罪。

translations.literal: Therefore what the Imperial Workshop makes is strictly forbidden in Han law; if feudatory lords usurp such dress, even kin must be punished.
translations.idiomatic: What the Imperial Workshop fashions is strictly barred by Han law: if a feudatory lord steals such insignia, kinship itself will not spare him from punishment.

sentences.zh: 自頃以來，下僭彌盛。

translations.literal: In recent times, usurpation below has grown ever worse.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years the usurpation of rank from below has grown ever worse.

sentences.zh: 器服裝飾，樂舞音容，通於王公，達于眾庶。

translations.literal: Utensils, dress, ornament, music, dance, voice, and bearing reach princes and dukes and extend to the common people.
translations.idiomatic: Vessels, dress, ornament, music, dance, voice, and bearing now match those of princes and reach down to commoners.

sentences.zh: 上下無辨，民志靡一。

translations.literal: High and low are undistinguished; the people's will lacks unity.
translations.idiomatic: High and low are no longer distinguished, and public order loses its single standard.

sentences.zh: 今表之所陳，實允禮度。

translations.literal: What the present memorial sets forth truly accords with ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: What this memorial proposes truly accords with ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 九條之格，猶有未盡，謹共附益，凡二十四條。

translations.literal: Though the nine-article code still leaves gaps, we respectfully add further provisions, twenty-four articles in all.
translations.idiomatic: Though the nine-article code still has gaps, we respectfully add provisions until there are twenty-four articles in all.

sentences.zh: 聽事不得南向坐，施帳并𢃕。

translations.literal: In the audience hall one may not sit facing south; canopy curtains and screens are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: In the hall of business one may not sit facing south, nor deploy canopy curtains and screens.

sentences.zh: 蕃國官正冬不得跣登國殿，及夾侍國師傳令及油戟。

translations.literal: Officials of feudatory states at the winter court may not go barefoot to mount the state hall, nor flank-attend with state masters relaying orders or with oil-painted halberds.
translations.idiomatic: Feudatory officials at the winter court may not ascend the state hall barefoot, nor be flanked by state masters relaying orders or by oil-painted halberds.

sentences.zh: 公主王妃傳令，不得朱服。

translations.literal: Princesses and princes' consorts relaying orders may not wear vermilion dress.
translations.idiomatic: When princesses or princes' consorts relay orders, they may not wear vermilion dress.

sentences.zh: 輿不得重杠。

translations.literal: Carriages may not have double crossbars.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages may not have double crossbars.

sentences.zh: 鄣扇不得雉尾。

translations.literal: Barrier fans may not have pheasant-tail plumes.
translations.idiomatic: Barrier fans may not bear pheasant-tail plumes.

sentences.zh: 劍不得鹿盧形。

translations.literal: Swords may not have stag-path hilts.
translations.idiomatic: Swords may not have the curved "stag-path" hilt.

sentences.zh: 槊毦不得孔雀白鷩。

translations.literal: Spear-shaft yak-tails may not use peacock or white-pheasant feathers.
translations.idiomatic: Yak-tail ornaments on spear shafts may not use peacock or white-pheasant feathers.

sentences.zh: 夾轂隊不得絳襖。

translations.literal: Hub-flanking squads may not wear crimson jackets.
translations.idiomatic: Squads flanking the carriage hub may not wear crimson jackets.

sentences.zh: 平乘誕馬不得過二匹。

translations.literal: Leading horses for ping-type light carriages may not exceed two.
translations.idiomatic: Horses leading a ping-type light carriage may not exceed two.

sentences.zh: 胡伎不得綵衣。

translations.literal: Hu performers may not wear colored robes.
translations.idiomatic: Hu performers may not wear colored robes.

sentences.zh: 舞伎正冬著袿衣，不得莊面蔽花。

translations.literal: At the winter court, dancing girls wear gui robes but may not paint their faces with covering flowers.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter court, dancing girls may wear gui robes but may not wear elaborate face paint and floral veils.

sentences.zh: 正冬會不得鐸舞、杯柈舞。

translations.literal: At the winter assembly, bell dance and cup-and-plate dance are forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter assembly, bell dance and cup-and-plate dance are forbidden.

sentences.zh: 長蹻伎、䞬舒、丸劍、博山伎、緣大橦伎、升五案伎，自非正冬會奏舞曲，不得舞。

translations.literal: Long-stilt performers, Zhusu, ball-and-sword, Mount Bo, great-pole, and five-table ascent performers—except when a formal winter assembly plays dance music, they may not perform.
translations.idiomatic: Long-stilt performers, Zhusu, ball-and-sword, Mount Bo, great-pole, and five-table ascent performers may not dance except at a formal winter assembly playing dance music.

sentences.zh: 諸妃主不得著袞帶。

translations.literal: All consorts and princesses may not wear gun sashes.
translations.idiomatic: Consorts and princesses may not wear gun sashes.

sentences.zh: 信幡，非臺省官悉用絳。

translations.literal: Trust banners: all except metropolitan offices must use crimson.
translations.idiomatic: Trust banners: except for metropolitan offices, all must use crimson.

sentences.zh: 郡縣內史相及封內官長，於其封君，既非在三，罷官則不復追敬，不合稱臣，正宜上下官敬而已。

translations.literal: Prefects, district magistrates, and chief officials within a fief toward their enfeoffed lord—since they are not among the three bonds, once removed from office they do not again offer obeisance; they should not address him as subject, but only observe the courtesy due between superior and subordinate officials.
translations.idiomatic: Prefects, magistrates, and chief officials within a fief toward their enfeoffed lord: once they are no longer in the three bonds of service and have left office, they need not resume full obeisance or call themselves his subjects—only the courtesy between superior and subordinate officials is fitting.

sentences.zh: 諸鎮常行，車前後不得過六隊，白直夾轂，不在其限。

translations.literal: On routine travel from princely fiefs, the squads before and after the carriage may not exceed six; white-guard hub-flankers are not counted in this limit.
translations.idiomatic: When feudatory princes travel on routine business, escort squads before and after the carriage may not exceed six; white-guard hub-flankers are exempt from this limit.

sentences.zh: 刀不得過銀銅為裝。

translations.literal: Knives may not be mounted beyond silver and copper.
translations.idiomatic: Knives may not be mounted in materials beyond silver and copper.

sentences.zh: 諸王女封縣主、諸王子孫襲封王王之妃及封侯者夫人行，並不得鹵簿。

translations.literal: Daughters of princes enfeoffed as district ladies, daughters-in-law of princes' heirs who succeed as kings, consorts of such kings, and wives of enfeoffed marquises on formal progress—all may not use a guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: District ladies who are princes' daughters, consorts of princes' heirs who succeed as kings, and wives of enfeoffed marquises on formal progress may none of them use a guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 諸王子繼體為王者，婚葬吉凶，悉依諸國公侯之禮，不得同皇弟皇子。

translations.literal: When a prince's son succeeds as king, weddings, funerals, and omens follow entirely the rites of feudatory dukes and marquises, and may not be treated like imperial younger brothers or sons.
translations.idiomatic: When a prince's son succeeds as king, weddings, funerals, and omens follow the rites of feudatory dukes and marquises only, not those of imperial younger brothers or sons.

sentences.zh: 車輿不得油幢，軺車不在其限。

translations.literal: Carriages may not use oiled banners; light post carriages are excepted.
translations.idiomatic: Carriages may not use oiled banners; light post carriages are excepted.

sentences.zh: 平乘舫皆平兩頭作露平形，不得擬像龍舟，悉不得朱油。

translations.literal: Ping-type boats and light carriages must be flat at both ends in exposed flat form, may not imitate dragon boats, and may not use vermilion lacquer.
translations.idiomatic: Ping-type boats and light carriages must have flat exposed ends, may not imitate dragon boats, and may not use vermilion lacquer.

sentences.zh: 帳𨪋不得作五花及豎筍形。

translations.literal: Palanquin valances may not be made in five-colored or upright-bamboo-shoot shapes.
translations.idiomatic: Palanquin valances may not be made in five-colored patterns or upright bamboo-shoot shapes.

sentences.zh: 若先有器物者，悉輸送臺臧。

translations.literal: If such objects already exist, they must all be delivered to the imperial storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: Objects already in violation must be surrendered to the imperial storehouse.

sentences.zh: 書到後二十日期，若有竊玩犯禁者，及統司無舉糾，並臨時議罪。

translations.literal: Within twenty days after the document arrives, if anyone secretly keeps or violates the ban, or if supervising offices fail to report and impeach, guilt will be determined on the spot.
translations.idiomatic: Within twenty days of the document's arrival, anyone who keeps forbidden items or violates the ban, and any supervising office that fails to report it, will be punished as the case requires.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: "] The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 車前五百者，卿行旅從，五百人為一旅。

translations.literal: "Five hundred before the carriage" means that when a minister travels, five hundred men form one brigade.
translations.idiomatic: "Five hundred before the carriage" refers to a minister's traveling escort: five hundred men formed one brigade.

sentences.zh: 漢氏一統，故去其人，留其名也。

translations.literal: When the Han unified the realm, they removed the men but kept the name.
translations.idiomatic: After Han unified the realm, the men were removed but the name was kept.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武孝建二年十一月乙巳，有司奏：「侍中祭酒何偃議：『自今臨軒，乘輿法服，燾華蓋，登殿宜依廟齋以夾御，侍中、常侍夾扶上殿，及應為王公興，又夾扶，畢，還本位。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day yisi in the eleventh month of the second year of Xiaojian of Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the relevant offices memorialized: "Attendant-in-Ordinary and Libationer He Yan proposed: 'From now on, when the emperor faces the throne hall, the imperial carriage in statutory dress, with the flaming canopy, ascends the hall—when mounting, it should follow temple fasting practice with attendants flanking the carriage; Attendants-in-Ordinary and Regular Attendants should flank and support him up the hall; and when it is necessary to rise for princes and dukes, they should again flank and support; when finished, return to original posts.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi day in the eleventh month of the second year of Xiaojian under Emperor Xiaowu of Song, the relevant offices memorialized: "Attendant-in-Ordinary and Libationer He Yan proposed: 'Henceforth, when the emperor faces the throne hall in statutory dress, with the flaming canopy, mounting the hall should follow temple fasting practice: attendants flank the carriage; Attendants-in-Ordinary and Regular Attendants flank and support him up the hall; when it is necessary to rise for princes and dukes, they flank and support again; when finished, they return to their posts.

sentences.zh: 』求詳議。

translations.literal: ' Request detailed deliberation."
translations.idiomatic: 'We request detailed deliberation."

sentences.zh: 」曹郎中徐爰參議：「宜如省所稱，以為永准。

translations.literal: Bureau Director Xu Ai offered a joint opinion: "It should be as the ministry proposed, taken as permanent standard."
translations.idiomatic: Bureau Director Xu Ai offered a joint opinion: "The ministry's proposal should be adopted as the permanent standard."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 孝建三年五月壬戌，有司奏：「案漢胡廣、蔡邕並云古者諸侯貳車九乘，秦滅六國，兼其車服，故王者大駕屬車八十一乘。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day renxu in the fifth month of the third year of Xiaojian, the relevant offices memorialized: "According to Hu Guang and Cai Yong of Han, both say that in antiquity feudatory lords had nine secondary carriages; when Qin extinguished the six states it took over their carriages and dress, so the king's great guard had eighty-one escort carriages.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the fifth month of the third year of Xiaojian, the relevant offices memorialized: "Hu Guang and Cai Yong of Han both state that in antiquity feudatory lords had nine secondary carriages; when Qin extinguished the six states it absorbed their carriages and dress, so the king's great procession had eighty-one escort carriages.

sentences.zh: 尚書、御史乘之。

translations.literal: Directors of the Masters of Writing and the Imperial Secretary rode in them.
translations.idiomatic: Directors of the Masters of Writing and the Imperial Secretary rode in them.

sentences.zh: 最後一車，懸豹尾。

translations.literal: On the last carriage, a leopard tail was suspended.
translations.idiomatic: The last carriage bore a suspended leopard tail.

sentences.zh: 法駕則三十六乘。

translations.literal: The statutory guard had thirty-six carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The statutory guard had thirty-six carriages.

sentences.zh: 檢晉江左逮至于今，乘輿出行，副車相承五乘。

translations.literal: Examining Jin east of the Yangzi down to the present, when the imperial carriage goes out, escort carriages follow in succession, five in number."
translations.idiomatic: Examining Jin east of the Yangzi down to the present, when the imperial carriage travels, five escort carriages follow in succession."

sentences.zh: 」尚書令建平王宏參議：「八十一乘，義兼九國，三十六乘無所准，並不出經典。

translations.literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Hong of Pingping offered a joint opinion: "Eighty-one carriages take in meaning from nine states; thirty-six carriages have no standard and both fall outside the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Hong of Pingping offered a joint opinion: "Eighty-one carriages symbolize the nine states; thirty-six have no classical basis—neither appears in the canon.

sentences.zh: 自邕、廣傳說，又是從官所乘，非帝者副車正數。

translations.literal: From Yong and Guang onward it is transmitted lore, and moreover what Directors of Writing and Imperial Secretary ride is what follow officials use—not the emperor's proper escort count.
translations.idiomatic: From Yong and Guang onward it is transmitted lore; moreover, what Directors of Writing and the Imperial Secretary ride are follow-official carriages, not the emperor's proper escort count.

sentences.zh: 江左五乘，儉不中禮。

translations.literal: Jiangzuo's five carriages are austere and miss the mark of ritual.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzuo's five carriages are too austere and fall short of ritual.

sentences.zh: 案周官云：『上公九命，貳車九乘。

translations.literal: According to the Offices of Zhou: 'The highest duke has nine orders, nine secondary carriages.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou states: 'The highest duke has nine orders and nine secondary carriages.

sentences.zh: 侯伯七命，車七乘。

translations.literal: Marquises and earls have seven orders, seven carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Marquises and earls have seven orders and seven carriages.

sentences.zh: 子男五命，車五乘。

translations.literal: Viscounts and barons have five orders, five carriages.
translations.idiomatic: Viscounts and barons have five orders and five carriages.

sentences.zh: 』然則帝王十二乘。

translations.literal: ' Thus the Son of Heaven and king should have twelve carriages."
translations.idiomatic: ' Therefore the Son of Heaven and king should have twelve carriages."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大明元年九月丁未朔，有司奏：「未有皇太后出行副車定數，下禮官議正。

translations.literal: On the first day dingwei in the ninth month of the first year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "There is as yet no fixed number of escort carriages when the Empress Dowager travels; let the ritual offices deliberate and fix it."
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, the first day of the ninth month of the first year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "No fixed number of escort carriages has been set for the Empress Dowager's travel; let the ritual offices deliberate and establish one."

sentences.zh: 」博士王燮之議：「周禮，后六服五路之數，悉與王同，則副車之制，不應獨異。

translations.literal: Erudite Wang Xiezhi offered an opinion: "In the Offices of Zhou, the queen's six robes and five carriages match the king in number; then the escort-carriage rule should not differ alone.
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Xiezhi offered an opinion: "In the Offices of Zhou, the queen's six robes and five carriages match the king's numbers; the escort-carriage rule should not stand apart.

sentences.zh: 又記云：『古者后立六宮、三夫人、九嬪、二十七世婦、八十一御妻，以聽天下之內治。

translations.literal: " The Record also says: 'In antiquity the queen established six palaces, three consorts, nine concubines, twenty-seven world-wives, and eighty-one chief wives to administer inner governance of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The Record also says: 'In antiquity the queen established six palaces, three consorts, nine concubines, twenty-seven world-wives, and eighty-one chief wives to govern inner affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 』『天子立六官、三公、九卿、二十七大夫、八十一元士，以聽天下之外治。

translations.literal: ' 'The Son of Heaven established six offices, three dukes, nine ministers, twenty-seven grand masters, and eighty-one chief scholars to administer outer governance of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: ' 'The Son of Heaven established six offices, three dukes, nine ministers, twenty-seven grand masters, and eighty-one chief scholars to govern outer affairs of the realm.

sentences.zh: 』鄭注云：『后象王立六宮而居之，亦正寢一，燕寢五。

translations.literal: ' Zheng's commentary says: 'The queen mirrors the king in establishing six palaces to dwell in them, likewise one main chamber and five inner chambers.
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng's commentary says: 'The queen mirrors the king in establishing six palaces to dwell in, likewise one main chamber and five inner chambers.

sentences.zh: 』推所立每與王同，禮無降亦明矣。

translations.literal: ' Inferring what is established, each matches the king; that ritual admits no lowering is also clear.
translations.idiomatic: ' What is established in each case matches the king; that ritual admits no lowering is clear.

sentences.zh: 皇太后既禮均至極，彌不應殊。

translations.literal: The Empress Dowager, her ritual equal to the utmost, all the more should not differ.
translations.idiomatic: The Empress Dowager, equal in ritual to the utmost degree, should differ even less.

sentences.zh: 謂並應同十二乘。

translations.literal: We hold that she should likewise have twelve carriages."
translations.idiomatic: We hold that she should likewise have twelve carriages."

sentences.zh: 」通關為允。

translations.literal: Passed through review as acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Passed through review as acceptable.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大明四年正月戊辰，尚書左丞荀萬秋奏：「籍田儀注，『皇帝冠通天冠，朱紘，青介幘，衣青紗袍。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day wuchen in the first month of the fourth year of Daming, Left Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Wanqiu memorialized: "The ceremonial regulations for the plowing field state: 'The emperor wears the Heaven-Penetrating Crown, vermilion tassel-cord, green kerchief, and green gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day in the first month of the fourth year of Daming, Left Director of the Masters of Writing Xun Wanqiu memorialized: "The plowing-field regulations state: 'The emperor wears the Heaven-Penetrating Crown, vermilion tassel-cord, green kerchief, and green gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 侍中陪乘，奉車郎秉轡。

translations.literal: Attendant-in-Ordinary rides as companion; Director of the Imperial Carriage holds the reins.
translations.idiomatic: The Attendant-in-Ordinary rides as companion; the Director of the Imperial Carriage holds the reins.

sentences.zh: 』案漢輿服志曰：『通天冠，乘輿常服也。

translations.literal: ' According to the Han Treatise on Carriages and Dress: 'The Heaven-Penetrating Crown is the imperial carriage's ordinary dress.
translations.idiomatic: ' The Han Treatise on Carriages and Dress says: 'The Heaven-Penetrating Crown is the imperial carriage's ordinary dress.

sentences.zh: 』若斯豈可以常服降千畝邪？

translations.literal: ' How can such dress be used to lower oneself to the thousand-mu field?"
translations.idiomatic: ' How can ordinary dress be used to descend to the thousand-mu field?'"

sentences.zh: 禮記曰：『昔者天子為籍千畝，冕而朱紘，躬秉耒耜。

translations.literal: The Record of Rites says: 'In former times the Son of Heaven plowed the thousand-mu field in coronet and vermilion tassel-cord, personally holding the plow and hoe.
translations.idiomatic: The Record of Rites says: 'In former times the Son of Heaven plowed the thousand-mu field in coronet and vermilion tassel-cord, personally holding plow and hoe.

sentences.zh: 』鄭玄注周官司服曰：『六服同冕』，尊故也。

translations.literal: ' Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Offices of Zhou, Director of Dress, says: 'The six robes share the coronet'—from respect.
translations.idiomatic: ' Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Offices of Zhou, Director of Dress, says: 'The six robes share the coronet'—from respect.

sentences.zh: 時服雖變，冕制不改。

translations.literal: Though seasonal dress changes, the coronet system is not altered.
translations.idiomatic: Though seasonal dress changes, the coronet system does not.

sentences.zh: 又潘岳籍田賦云：『常伯陪乘，太僕秉轡。

translations.literal: Pan Yue's Rhapsody on the Plowing Field also says: 'The Chief Minister rides as companion; the Grand Master of the Imperial Carriage holds the reins.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Yue's Rhapsody on the Plowing Field also says: 'The Chief Minister rides as companion; the Grand Master of the Imperial Carriage holds the reins.

sentences.zh: 』推此，輿駕籍田，宜冠冕，璪十二旒，朱紘，黑介幘，衣青紗袍。

translations.literal: ' Inferring from this, when the imperial carriage goes to the plowing field, it should wear coronet with twelve jade beads, vermilion tassel-cord, black kerchief, and green gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: ' Inferring from this, for the plowing field the emperor should wear coronet with twelve jade beads, vermilion tassel-cord, black kerchief, and green gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 常伯陪乘，太僕秉轡。

translations.literal: Chief Minister as companion, Grand Master of the Imperial Carriage holding the reins.
translations.idiomatic: The Chief Minister should ride as companion; the Grand Master of the Imperial Carriage should hold the reins.

sentences.zh: 宜改儀注，一遵二禮以為定儀。

translations.literal: The ceremonial regulations should be revised to follow both rites as the fixed ceremony."
translations.idiomatic: The ceremonial regulations should be revised to follow both rites as the fixed ceremony."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大明四年正月己卯，有司奏：「南郊親奉儀注，皇帝初著平天冠，火龍黼黻之服。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day jimao in the first month of the fourth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "For the southern suburb, when the emperor personally presents offerings, the regulations state that the emperor first wears the Level-Heaven Crown and robes with fire dragon and fu-fu patterns.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao day in the first month of the fourth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "For the southern suburb, when the emperor personally presents offerings, the regulations state that he first wears the Level-Heaven Crown and robes with fire dragon and fu-fu patterns.

sentences.zh: 還，變通天冠，絳紗袍。

translations.literal: On returning, he changes to the Heaven-Penetrating Crown and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: On returning, he changes to the Heaven-Penetrating Crown and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 廟祠親奉，舊儀，皇帝初服與郊不異，而還變著黑介幘，單衣即事，乖體。

translations.literal: For temple sacrifice when the emperor personally presents offerings, the old regulations had the emperor's initial dress no different from the suburb, but on returning he changed to black kerchief and single robe for the service—contrary to proper form.
translations.idiomatic: For temple sacrifice when the emperor personally presents offerings, the old regulations matched the suburb for the initial dress, but on returning he changed to black kerchief and single robe for the service—contrary to proper form.

sentences.zh: 謂宜同郊還，亦變著通天冠，絳紗袍。

translations.literal: We hold that on returning from the temple he should likewise change to the Heaven-Penetrating Crown and crimson gauze robe.
translations.idiomatic: We hold that on returning from the temple he should likewise change to the Heaven-Penetrating Crown and crimson gauze robe.

sentences.zh: 又舊儀乘金根車。

translations.literal: Also, the old regulations used the golden-root carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The old regulations also used the golden-root carriage.

sentences.zh: 今五路既備，依禮玉路以祀，亦宜改金根車為玉路。

translations.literal: Now that the five carriages are complete, according to ritual the jade carriage should be used for sacrifice; the golden-root carriage should also be changed to the jade carriage."
translations.idiomatic: Now that the five carriages are complete, ritual requires the jade carriage for sacrifice; the golden-root carriage should be changed to the jade carriage."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大明六年八月壬戌，有司奏：「漢儀注『大駕鹵簿，公卿奉引，大將軍參乘，太僕卿御。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day renxu in the eighth month of the sixth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "The Han ceremonial regulations state: 'Great guard of honor: dukes and ministers lead the way, the Grand General rides as companion, the Director of the Imperial Carriage drives.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu day in the eighth month of the sixth year of Daming, the relevant offices memorialized: "The Han ceremonial regulations state: 'Great guard of honor: dukes and ministers lead the way, the Grand General rides as companion, the Director of the Imperial Carriage drives.

sentences.zh: 法駕，侍中參乘，奉車郎御』。

translations.literal: Statutory guard: Attendant-in-Ordinary rides as companion, Director of the Imperial Carriage drives.'
translations.idiomatic: Statutory guard: the Attendant-in-Ordinary rides as companion, the Director of the Imperial Carriage drives.'

sentences.zh: 晉氏江左，大駕未立，故郊祀用法駕，宗廟以小駕。

translations.literal: Under Jin east of the Yangzi the great guard was not established, so suburban sacrifice used the statutory guard and the ancestral temple used the small guard.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin east of the Yangzi the great guard was not established, so suburban sacrifice used the statutory guard and the ancestral temple the small guard.

sentences.zh: 至於儀服，二駕不異。

translations.literal: As for ceremonial dress, the two guards did not differ.
translations.idiomatic: As for ceremonial dress, the two guards did not differ.

sentences.zh: 拜陵，御服單衣幘，百官陪從，朱衣而已，亦謂之小駕，名實乖舛。

translations.literal: For tomb-visits, the imperial dress was single robe and kerchief, accompanying officials wore only vermilion robes—also called the small guard; name and reality were at odds.
translations.idiomatic: For tomb-visits, the emperor wore single robe and kerchief while accompanying officials wore only vermilion robes—also called the small guard; the name and reality were at odds.

sentences.zh: 考尋前記，大駕上陵，北郊。

translations.literal: Examining earlier records, the great guard was used for mounting tombs and the northern suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier records show the great guard used for mounting tombs and the northern suburb.

sentences.zh: 周禮宗廟於昊天有降，宜以大駕郊祀，法駕祠廟，小駕上陵，如為從序。

translations.literal: In the Offices of Zhou the ancestral temple descends from August Heaven; the great guard should be used for suburban sacrifice, the statutory guard for temple sacrifice, and the small guard for mounting tombs—thus following proper order.
translations.idiomatic: The Offices of Zhou show the ancestral temple descending from August Heaven; the great guard should serve suburban sacrifice, the statutory guard temple sacrifice, and the small guard tomb-visits—thus following proper order.

sentences.zh: 今改祠廟為法駕鹵簿，其軍幢多少，臨時配之。

translations.literal: Now temple sacrifice is changed to the statutory guard of honor; how many military banners are used will be assigned provisionally.
translations.idiomatic: Temple sacrifice is now changed to the statutory guard of honor; the number of military banners will be assigned as needed.

sentences.zh: 至尊乘玉路，以金路象路革路木路小輦輪御軺衣書等車為副。

translations.literal: His Majesty rides the jade carriage; golden, elephant, leather, and wooden carriages, small palanquins, wheel carriages, imperial light carriages, robe carriages, book carriages, and the like serve as escorts.
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty rides the jade carriage, with golden, elephant, leather, and wooden carriages, small palanquins, wheel carriages, imperial light carriages, robe carriages, book carriages, and the like as escorts.

sentences.zh: 其餘並如常儀。

translations.literal: The rest follows the usual regulations."
translations.idiomatic: All else follows the usual regulations."

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 大明七年二月甲寅，輿駕巡南豫、兗二州，冕服，御玉路，辭二廟。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day jiayin in the second month of the seventh year of Daming, the imperial carriage toured the two provinces of Southern Yu and Yan, wearing ceremonial crown and robes, driving the jade carriage, and took leave of the two ancestral temples.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day in the second month of the seventh year of Daming, the emperor toured Southern Yu and Yan provinces in full ceremonial dress, riding the jade carriage and taking leave of the two ancestral temples.

sentences.zh: 改服通天冠，御木路，建大麾，備春蒐之典。

translations.literal: He changed to the Heaven-Penetrating Crown, drove the wood carriage, raised the great standard, and observed the spring-hunt ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: He then changed to the Heaven-Penetrating Crown, took the wood carriage, raised the great standard, and carried out the spring hunt rites.

sentences.zh: 明帝泰始四年五月甲戌，尚書令建安王休仁參議：「天子之子，與士齒讓，達於辟雍，無生而貴者也。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day jiaxu in the fifth month of the fourth year of Taishi, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Xiu Ren of Jian'an offered a joint opinion: "The Son of Heaven's sons yield place by rank with gentlemen; at the Imperial Academy none is noble by birth alone.
translations.idiomatic: On jiaxu day in the fifth month of the fourth year of Taishi, Director of the Masters of Writing Prince Xiu Ren of Jian'an submitted a joint opinion: "A son of Heaven yields in rank to gentlemen; at the Imperial Academy no one is born to privilege.

sentences.zh: 既命而尊，禮同上公。

translations.literal: Once appointed he is honored; ritual matches the highest duke.
translations.idiomatic: Once invested he is honored, and his ritual standing matches the highest duke.

sentences.zh: 周制五等，車服相涉，公降王者，一等而已。

translations.literal: Under Zhou's five ranks, carriages and dress interlinked; a duke below the king differed by only one grade.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou's five ranks, carriage and dress were graded together: a duke stood only one step below the king.

sentences.zh: 王以金路賜同姓諸侯，象及革木，以賜異姓侯伯，在朝卿士，亦準斯禮。

translations.literal: The king granted the golden carriage to feudal lords of the same surname; ivory, leather, and wood carriages to feudal lords of other surnames; court ministers likewise followed this rule.
translations.idiomatic: The king granted the golden carriage to same-surname feudal lords and ivory, leather, or wood carriages to lords of other surnames; ministers at court followed the same rule.

sentences.zh: 按如此制，則東宮應乘金路。

translations.literal: According to such regulation, the Eastern Palace should ride the golden carriage.
translations.idiomatic: On that rule the Eastern Palace ought to ride the golden carriage.

sentences.zh: 自晉武過江，禮儀疏舛，王公以下，車服卑雜；

translations.literal: From when Emperor Wu of Jin crossed the Yangzi, ritual was loose and awry; from kings and dukes downward, carriages and dress were base and confused;
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wu of Jin crossed the Yangzi, ritual grew careless; from kings and dukes down, carriage and dress were debased and confused;

sentences.zh: 唯有東宮，禮秩崇異，上次辰極，下絕侯王。

translations.literal: only the Eastern Palace, its ritual rank lofty and distinct, rose next below the pole star and stood far above feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: only the Eastern Palace remained exalted, second to the throne yet far above every feudal lord.

sentences.zh: 而皇太子乘石山安車，義不見經，事無所出。

translations.literal: Yet the crown prince rode the stone-mountain comfort carriage—its meaning appears in no classic, and the practice has no source.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the crown prince rode the stone-mountain comfort carriage, a usage found in no classic and without any textual warrant.

sentences.zh: 禮所謂金、玉路者，正以金玉飾輅諸末耳。

translations.literal: What ritual calls the golden and jade carriages means simply that gold and jade ornament the carriage's extremities.
translations.idiomatic: In ritual, "golden" and "jade" carriages mean only that gold and jade ornament the carriage's extremities.

sentences.zh: 左右前後，同以漆畫。

translations.literal: Left, right, front, and rear were alike lacquered and painted.
translations.idiomatic: Left, right, front, and rear were all lacquered and painted alike.

sentences.zh: 秦改周輅，制為金根，通以金薄，周匝四面。

translations.literal: Qin altered Zhou carriages and fashioned the golden-root type, covering all four sides with gold leaf.
translations.idiomatic: Qin reworked Zhou carriages into the golden-root type, sheathing all four sides in gold leaf.

sentences.zh: 漢、魏、二晉，因循莫改。

translations.literal: Han, Wei, and the two Jin dynasties followed without change.
translations.idiomatic: Han, Wei, and the two Jin dynasties followed suit without change.

sentences.zh: 逮于大明，始備五輅。

translations.literal: By the Daming era the five carriages were first made complete.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the Daming era were the five carriages fully provided.

sentences.zh: 金玉二制，並類金根，造次瞻覩，殆無差別。

translations.literal: The golden and jade types both resembled the golden-root; seen in passing they were almost indistinguishable.
translations.idiomatic: The golden and jade types both resembled the golden-root carriage; at a glance they were nearly indistinguishable.

sentences.zh: 若錫之東儲，於禮嫌重，非所以崇峻陛級，表示等威。

translations.literal: If granted to the Eastern Storehouse, ritual would be excessively heavy—not the way to heighten the throne steps and display graded majesty.
translations.idiomatic: To grant them to the heir apparent would be ritually excessive and would not heighten the throne or display proper gradations of majesty.

sentences.zh: 且春秋之義，降下以兩，臣子之義，宜從謙約。

translations.literal: Moreover the Spring and Autumn principle is to lower rank by two steps; the principle for subjects is to follow modest restraint.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Spring and Autumn Annals teach lowering rank by two degrees, and subjects ought to observe modest restraint.

sentences.zh: 謂東宮車服，宜降天子二等，驂駕四馬，乘象輅，降龍碧旂九葉。

translations.literal: We hold that the Eastern Palace's carriages and dress should be two grades below the Son of Heaven: four horses in the team, riding the ivory carriage, with a nine-leaf jasper-green banner bearing descending dragons.
translations.idiomatic: The Eastern Palace's carriage and dress should stand two grades below the emperor: a four-horse team, the ivory carriage, and a nine-leaf jasper-green banner with descending dragons.

sentences.zh: 進不斥尊，退不逼下，沿古酌時，於禮為衷。

translations.literal: Advancing without offending the honored, retreating without pressing the lower—following antiquity and adjusting to the age, this is the mean in ritual.
translations.idiomatic: It neither challenges the sovereign nor presses upon inferiors—anchored in antiquity yet tuned to the times, the proper balance of ritual.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 泰始四年八月甲寅，詔曰：「車服之飾，象數是遵。

translations.literal: On the cyclical day jiayin in the eighth month of the fourth year of Taishi, an edict said: "Ornamentation of carriages and dress follows symbolic numbers.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin day in the eighth month of the fourth year of Taishi, an edict read: "Carriage and dress ornamentation must follow symbolic numbers.

sentences.zh: 故盛皇留範，列聖垂制。

translations.literal: Therefore august emperors left models and successive sages handed down regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Great emperors left models; successive sages handed down regulations.

sentences.zh: 朕近改定五路，酌古代今，修成六服，沿時變禮。

translations.literal: We have lately revised the five carriages, weighing antiquity against the present, completed the six robes, and adjusted ritual to the times.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately revised the five carriages, weighing antiquity against the present, completed the six robes, and adapted ritual to the age.

sentences.zh: 所施之事，各有條敍。

translations.literal: Each matter to which they apply has its own ordered provisions.
translations.idiomatic: Each occasion they serve has its own ordered provisions.

sentences.zh: 便可付外，載之典章。

translations.literal: Let this be issued abroad and recorded in the canonical statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Issue this abroad and record it in the canonical statutes.

sentences.zh: 朕以大冕純玉繅，玄衣黃裳，乘玉輅，郊祀天，宗祀明堂。

translations.literal: We wear the great mian with pure jade tassels, black upper robe and yellow lower robe, ride the jade carriage, perform suburban sacrifice to Heaven, and offer joint sacrifice at the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: For suburban sacrifice to Heaven and joint sacrifice at the Bright Hall we wear the great mian with pure jade tassels, black upper robe and yellow lower robe, and ride the jade carriage.

sentences.zh: 又以法冕五綵繅，玄衣絳裳，乘金路，祀太廟，元正大會諸侯。

translations.literal: We also wear the statutory mian with five-color tassels, black upper robe and crimson lower robe, ride the golden carriage, sacrifice at the Grand Temple, and at the New Year's Day assembly receive the feudal lords.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifice at the Grand Temple and the New Year's assembly of feudal lords we wear the statutory mian with five-color tassels, black upper robe and crimson lower robe, and ride the golden carriage.

sentences.zh: 又以飾冠冕四綵繅，紫衣紅裳，乘象輅，小會宴饗，餞送諸侯，臨軒會王公。

translations.literal: We also wear the adorned ceremonial crown with four-color tassels, purple upper robe and red lower robe, ride the ivory carriage, for minor assemblies and banquets, farewells to feudal lords, and holding court before the throne to meet kings and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: For minor assemblies and banquets, farewells to feudal lords, and audiences with kings and dukes before the throne we wear the adorned ceremonial crown with four-color tassels, purple upper robe and red lower robe, and ride the ivory carriage.

sentences.zh: 又以繡冕三綵繅，朱衣裳，乘革路，征伐不賓，講武校獵。

translations.literal: We also wear the embroidered mian with three-color tassels, vermilion robes, ride the leather carriage, for campaigns against those who do not submit, military reviews, and hunts.
translations.idiomatic: For campaigns against recalcitrant lords, military reviews, and hunts we wear the embroidered mian with three-color tassels and vermilion robes and ride the leather carriage.

sentences.zh: 又以紘冕二綵繅，青衣裳，乘木輅，耕稼，饗國子。

translations.literal: We also wear the hong mian with two-color tassels, green robes, ride the wood carriage, for plowing, and feasting the National University students.
translations.idiomatic: For plowing the sacred field and feasting National University students we wear the hong mian with two-color tassels, green robes, and the wood carriage.

sentences.zh: 又以通天冠，朱紗袍，為聽政之服。」

translations.literal: We also use the Heaven-Penetrating Crown and vermilion gauze robe as dress for hearing government."
translations.idiomatic: The Heaven-Penetrating Crown and vermilion gauze robe serve as dress for conducting government."

sentences.zh: 泰始六年正月戊辰，有司奏：「被敕皇太子正冬朝賀，合著袞冕九章衣不？

translations.literal: On the cyclical day wuchen in the first month of the sixth year of Taishi, the relevant offices memorialized: "By imperial order: should the crown prince wear gun-and-mian with the nine-emblem robe for the midwinter court congratulation?"
translations.idiomatic: On wuchen day in the first month of the sixth year of Taishi, the relevant offices memorialized: "By imperial order: should the crown prince wear gun-and-mian with the nine-emblem robe for the midwinter court congratulation?"

sentences.zh: 」儀曹郎丘仲起議：「案周禮，公自袞冕以下。

translations.literal: Clerk of the Bureau of Rites Qiu Zhongqi offered an opinion: "According to the Offices of Zhou, dukes begin with gun-and-mian downward.
translations.idiomatic: Clerk of the Bureau of Rites Qiu Zhongqi argued: "The Offices of Zhou place dukes at gun-and-mian and below.

sentences.zh: 鄭注：『袞冕以至卿大夫之玄冕，皆其朝聘天子之服也。

translations.literal: Zheng's commentary: 'Gun-and-mian down to the dark mian of ministers and grand masters—all are robes for audience and visiting the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan comments: 'From gun-and-mian down to the dark mian of ministers and grand masters—all are robes for audience and visiting the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 』伏尋古之上公，尚得服袞以朝。

translations.literal: ' Respectfully examining antiquity, even the highest duke of old could wear gun for court.
translations.idiomatic: ' Respectfully examining antiquity, even the highest duke of old could wear gun at court.

sentences.zh: 皇太子以儲副之尊，率土瞻仰。

translations.literal: The crown prince, in the honor of heir apparent, is gazed upon by all within the realm.
translations.idiomatic: As heir apparent, the crown prince is looked to by all within the realm.

sentences.zh: 愚謂宜式遵盛典，服袞冕九旒以朝賀。

translations.literal: I hold that he should follow the great precedent and wear gun-and-mian with nine tassels for the congratulatory audience.
translations.idiomatic: I hold that he should follow the great precedent and wear gun-and-mian with nine tassels for the congratulatory audience.

sentences.zh: 」兼左丞陸澄議：「服冕以朝，實著經典。

translations.literal: Associate Left Director Lu Cheng offered an opinion: "Wearing the mian for court is indeed set out in the classics.
translations.idiomatic: Associate Left Director Lu Cheng argued: "Wearing the mian at court is expressly set out in the classics.

sentences.zh: 秦除六冕之制，至漢明帝始與諸儒還備古章。

translations.literal: Qin abolished the six-mian system; only under Emperor Ming of Han did he and the ru scholars restore the ancient regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Qin abolished the six crowns; only under Emperor Ming of Han did the court, with the ru scholars, restore the ancient wardrobe.

sentences.zh: 自魏、晉以來，宗廟行禮之外，不欲令臣下服袞冕，故位公者，每加侍官。

translations.literal: From Wei and Jin onward, apart from ancestral-temple rites, the court did not wish subjects to wear gun-and-mian; therefore those of ducal rank were repeatedly given attendant offices.
translations.idiomatic: From Wei and Jin onward, outside ancestral-temple rites the court kept subjects from gun-and-mian; hence men of ducal rank were repeatedly given attendant offices instead.

sentences.zh: 今皇太子承乾作副，禮絕羣后，宜遵聖王之盛典，革近代之陋制。

translations.literal: Now the crown prince holds Heaven's deputy station, his ritual standing above all consorts; he should follow the sage kings' great precedent and abolish the shabby rules of recent times.
translations.idiomatic: Now the crown prince holds Heaven's deputy station, standing above all consorts; he should follow the sage kings' great precedent and cast off the shabby rules of recent times.

sentences.zh: 臣等參議，依禮，皇太子元正朝賀，應服袞冕九章衣。

translations.literal: We jointly submit: according to ritual, for the crown prince's New Year's congratulatory audience he should wear gun-and-mian with the nine-emblem robe.
translations.idiomatic: We jointly submit that, by ritual, the crown prince at the New Year's congratulatory audience should wear gun-and-mian with the nine-emblem robe.

sentences.zh: 以仲起議為允。

translations.literal: Qiu Zhongqi's opinion is adopted as acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Qiu Zhongqi's opinion is adopted.

sentences.zh: 撰載儀注。

translations.literal: Compile and record it in the ceremonial regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Compile and record it in the ceremonial regulations.

sentences.zh: 」詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 後廢帝即位，尊所生陳貴妃為皇太妃，輿服一如晉孝武太妃故事。

translations.literal: When the Deposed Emperor took the throne, he honored his birth mother, Consort Chen, as Imperial Grand Consort; her carriage and dress followed entirely the precedent of the Grand Consort of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Fei took the throne, he honored his birth mother, Consort Chen, as Imperial Grand Consort; her carriage and dress followed the precedent of Emperor Xiaowu of Jin's grand consort.

sentences.zh: 唯省五牛旗及赤旂。

translations.literal: Only the Five-Ox Banner and the crimson banner were omitted.
translations.idiomatic: Only the Five-Ox Banner and the crimson banner were omitted.
